title: Apex Logistics Warehouse Operations Policy
policy:
1. All personnel must report to the main dock no later than 07:45 on their scheduled shift. Late arrivals exceeding fifteen minutes require written approval from the shift supervisor.
2. The following materials are strictly prohibited from being stored in Zone C: lithium-ion batteries, compressed gas cylinders, and aerosol propellants. Storage of any other hazardous substance requires prior environmental safety clearance.
3. Incident reports must be filed within four days of the event. Reports submitted after the deadline will be marked as non-compliant and may affect quarterly safety bonuses.
4. No employee may operate powered machinery without holding a valid Level 1 certification. This requirement applies to all warehouse floors and loading bays.
5. Seasonal workers assigned to the packing line may operate tape dispensers and box sealers after completing the mandatory ten-minute orientation. These workers are exempt from the Level 1 certification requirement for these specific devices.
6. Personal electronic devices are not permitted on the warehouse floor. Staff must store phones and smartwatches in designated lockers before passing through the security turnstile.

items.case: On November 12, 2024, logistics coordinator Samira Vance requests to store fifty cases of industrial spray paint in Zone C.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The item is not listed in the prohibition list, and the list is treated as complete, so the item is not prohibited.
criteria.no: The item is similar to a listed example, and the list is treated as illustrative, so the item is prohibited.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the prohibition list is complete, so spray paint (not listed) is permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so spray paint (similar to aerosol propellants) is prohibited.

items.case: On Friday, October 11, 2024, a conveyor belt malfunction occurred in Aisle 4. The maintenance team submitted the incident report on Wednesday, October 16, 2024.
items.question: Is the filing deadline met?

criteria.yes: The filing date falls within four business days of the event date.
criteria.no: The filing date falls outside four calendar days of the event date.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the four-day period counts business days (Oct 14-17), making the Oct 16 filing timely. Under instruction B, the period counts calendar days (Oct 12-15), making the Oct 16 filing late.

items.case: On November 15, 2024, seasonal packer Leo Chen requests to use a heavy-duty box sealer on the packing line after completing the ten-minute orientation but without a Level 1 certification.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The specific clause for seasonal workers overrides the general certification requirement.
criteria.no: The stricter general certification requirement overrides the specific seasonal worker exemption.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the stricter general certification rule applies, denying permission. Under instruction B, the more specific seasonal worker exemption applies, granting permission.

title: Aethelgard Logistics Ltd. Procurement Policy
policy:
1. This Procurement Policy governs all purchases made by Aethelgard Logistics Ltd. employees for operational use. All requests must be submitted through the central purchasing portal to Procurement Manager Marcus Chen with a detailed justification.
2. Purchases up to $10,000 require approval from the requesting department head. Purchases exceeding $10,000 but not exceeding $50,000 require dual approval from the department head and the Chief Financial Officer. Purchases over $50,000 require board authorization.
3. All vendors must be registered in the approved supplier directory before any purchase order is issued. Unregistered suppliers may only be used in documented emergencies, pending retroactive registration within five business days.
4. The policy explicitly restricts the procurement of luxury office furnishings, including but not limited to ergonomic executive chairs, standing desks, and premium leather sofas. Standard office supplies and industrial equipment are permitted.
5. Requests submitted between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024 are evaluated under the 2023 version of this policy. On 15 March 2024, Clause 4 was amended to introduce a restriction on height-adjustable standing desks, while retaining the existing restriction on ergonomic executive chairs.
6. All procurement decisions must be documented with a justification memo referencing the applicable clause. Failure to comply may result in reimbursement denial.
7. This policy supersedes all prior departmental purchasing guidelines effective 1 January 2023.

items.case: On 10 February 2024, procurement officer Elena Rostova submitted a request for a $4,200 adjustable monitor arm mount with integrated cable management for the executive suite. The department head approved the purchase.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The requested item is not explicitly listed in Clause 4, and treating the list as complete means only the listed items are restricted.
criteria.no: The requested item is functionally similar to the listed restricted items, and treating the list as illustrative extends the restriction to it.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, Clause 4's list is exhaustive, so the monitor arm mount falls outside the restriction and is permitted. Under Instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the similar ergonomic office accessory is covered by the restriction and is not permitted.

items.case: On 5 April 2024, operations manager David Lin submitted a request for a $12,500 charitable donation to the local community food bank. The department head and CFO both signed off on the transfer.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request involves a charitable donation, which falls outside the policy's scope of operational purchases and approval thresholds, and the instruction states uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: The request involves a charitable donation, which falls outside the policy's scope, and the instruction states uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: The policy exclusively governs operational purchases and vendor approvals. A charitable donation is not covered by any clause. Instruction A permits uncovered requests, yielding yes. Instruction B prohibits them, yielding no.

items.case: On 10 March 2024, facilities coordinator Sarah Jenkins submitted a request for a $3,800 height-adjustable standing desk for the warehouse office. The procurement committee reviewed the submission and issued a final decision on 20 March 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request was made on 10 March 2024, before the 15 March 2024 amendment, so the original policy version applies and permits standing desks.
criteria.no: The decision was made on 20 March 2024, after the 15 March 2024 amendment, so the updated policy version applies and restricts standing desks.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, the pre-amendment version applies, permitting standing desks. Under Instruction B, the post-amendment version applies, restricting them.

title: Aether Dynamics Ltd. Standard Warranty Policy
policy:
1. Coverage Period: All Aether Dynamics Ltd. consumer electronics purchased after March 1, 2024 are covered under the Standard Warranty for exactly twelve (12) months from the original purchase date. Claims submitted after this period are automatically denied.
2. Eligible Defects: The warranty covers specific manufacturing defects that cause complete functional failure, including: faulty solder joints, misaligned optical lenses, and defective power regulators. Cosmetic damage and physical impact are excluded.
3. Claim Process: Customers must submit a completed digital claim form alongside a scanned copy of the original sales receipt to Claims Manager Marcus Thorne within the coverage period. Upon verification, eligible claims receive a brand-new replacement unit shipped directly to the registered address. Partial refunds, repair vouchers, or store credits are not issued under this policy.
4. High-Value Items: Products with an original purchase price exceeding $800 require a mandatory technical inspection by an Aether-certified engineer before any replacement is authorized. This inspection must be completed within fourteen (14) days of claim submission.
5. Transferability: Warranty coverage is non-transferable and remains strictly tied to the original purchaser named on the sales receipt. Gifts, secondary market purchases, or inherited units do not qualify for warranty service.
6. Repeat Claims: Customers who have previously received a warranty replacement for the same product model within a rolling twenty-four-month period are ineligible for additional warranty service on subsequent units.

items.case: On May 10, 2024, customer Leo Vance purchased an Aether Dynamics Smart Thermostat for $299. On August 15, 2024, the device’s companion app stopped syncing with the company’s cloud servers. Leo submits a request for a complimentary two-year premium software subscription upgrade to restore full app functionality.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the instruction permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the instruction prohibits uncovered requests.

items.rationale: The policy covers hardware replacement for manufacturing defects, not software subscription upgrades. Since no clause addresses software licenses, Instruction A permits it while Instruction B denies it.

items.case: On April 5, 2024, user Nina Patel purchased an Aether Dynamics Noise-Canceling Headset for $320. On September 12, 2024, the left audio driver stopped working due to a manufacturing defect. Nina submits a digital claim form with her original receipt to the Claims Department on September 13, 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy excludes customers who previously received a replacement for the same model. Under Instruction A, this unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, making the customer eligible.
criteria.no: Under Instruction B, the unestablished condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the exclusion and making the customer ineligible.

items.rationale: The case omits whether Nina previously received a replacement for this headset model. Clause 6 excludes such customers. Instruction A treats the unproven condition as false (no prior replacement), permitting the claim. Instruction B treats it as true (prior replacement occurred), denying the claim.

items.case: On July 20, 2024, customer Omar Hayes purchased an Aether Dynamics Portable Projector for $550. On November 2, 2024, the device’s internal wiring harness short-circuited due to a factory insulation flaw, causing total failure. Omar submits a claim for a replacement unit.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy lists examples of covered defects. Under Instruction B, the short-circuited wiring harness is treated as a similar covered defect, permitting the claim.
criteria.no: Under Instruction A, the list of covered defects is treated as exhaustive. Since the wiring harness issue is not explicitly listed, the claim is denied.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists specific covered defects. The case involves a short-circuited wiring harness, which is not listed but is similar to the examples. Instruction A restricts coverage to the exact list (denial), while Instruction B extends it to similar defects (permission).

title: Lumina Live Events Ticketing Policy
policy:
1. Full refunds for ticket purchases are granted only if Lumina Live Events officially cancels the performance or postpones it by more than fourteen days from the original date.
2. Partial refunds of up to one hundred dollars are available for attendees who submit a verified medical certificate within three days of the scheduled gate opening time.
3. Ticket transfers to a different named individual are not permitted if the original purchase was funded by a corporate or business account.
4. Group bookings comprising twelve or more tickets qualify for a fifteen percent discount, provided the full adjusted payment is received by the invoice due date specified in the booking confirmation.
5. Requests for wheelchair seating or companion assistance must be submitted in writing to the accessibility desk at least twenty-one days before the event date to guarantee provision.
6. All refund, transfer, and accommodation requests must be submitted through the official Lumina customer portal and include the original twelve-digit order confirmation number.

items.case: Elena Rostova requests to transfer her March 15 concert ticket to Marcus Chen. She submitted the digital transfer form and paid the thirty-dollar processing fee six days before the event. The case does not mention the funding source of the original purchase.
items.question: Is the ticket transfer request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated corporate funding condition is treated as not satisfied, so the prohibition in clause 3 does not apply.
criteria.no: The unstated corporate funding condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the prohibition in clause 3.

items.rationale: Clause 3 prohibits transfers only if the original purchase was funded by a corporate account. The case omits the funding source. Under instruction A, the missing condition is not satisfied, meaning the prohibition is inapplicable and the transfer is permitted. Under instruction B, the missing condition is satisfied, triggering the prohibition and denying the request.

items.case: Elena Rostova requests a partial refund for her ticket to the Friday, March 22 concert. She submitted a verified medical certificate on Tuesday, March 19. The gate opening time is 7:00 PM on the day of the event. She originally paid eighty-five dollars for the ticket.
items.question: Is the partial refund request permitted?

criteria.no: The submission spans four business days, exceeding the three-day limit in clause 2.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires submission within three days. Counting calendar days from March 19 to March 22 yields exactly three days, meeting the requirement. Counting business days yields four days (Tuesday through Friday), exceeding the limit. Instruction A applies business day counting, resulting in denial. Instruction B applies calendar day counting, resulting in approval.

items.case: Elena Rostova requests to change her ticket from a Balcony seat to an Orchestra seat for the same attendee name on the March 15 concert. She submitted the request via the official portal with her order number and paid a ten-dollar service fee.

criteria.yes: No clause addresses same-name seat changes, and instruction A permits requests not covered by any clause.
criteria.no: No clause addresses same-name seat changes, and instruction B denies requests not covered by any clause.

items.rationale: Clause 3 covers transfers to different named individuals, but this request maintains the same name. No other clause governs seat upgrades or section changes. Under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted.

title: Oakridge University Grade Adjustment Protocol
policy:
Oakridge University Grade Adjustment Protocol (Effective 2024-09-01)
1. All grade adjustment requests must be submitted electronically via the Student Portal within fourteen calendar days of the official grade publication date. Late submissions are logged but not processed under standard procedure.
2. Appeals are explicitly denied for trivial circumstances, such as personal scheduling conflicts, minor illness under forty-eight hours, or preference for a different grading rubric.
3. Academic staff, including Dr. Aris Thorne and the Department of Computational Studies, retain final discretion over qualitative grading rubrics and essay evaluations.
4. A processing fee of $45.00 is waived for first-time appeals but automatically charged for subsequent submissions by the same student in the same academic term.
5. Adjustments exceeding a ten-percentage-point increase require written authorization from the Dean of Academic Affairs, currently held by Elena Rostova.
6. Requests submitted after the fourteen-day window are automatically routed to the Office of the Registrar for discretionary review, which typically concludes by November 15 of the relevant term.
7. No grade may be altered once the official transcript has been issued to external institutions or employers.

items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The stated reason is not in the explicit list of denied circumstances, so under a complete-list interpretation it does not trigger a denial.
criteria.no: The stated reason is substantially similar to the listed denied circumstances, so under an illustrative-list interpretation it triggers a denial.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the policy’s list of denied circumstances is exhaustive; since caring for a sick pet is not listed, the appeal is not denied and is therefore permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; caring for a sick pet closely resembles minor illness and scheduling conflicts, so it falls under the denial category and is not permitted.

criteria.no: No policy clause addresses equipment failures during assessments, so the default restriction rule applies.

items.rationale: The policy contains no clause governing grade adjustments for laboratory equipment malfunctions. Under instruction A, the absence of a governing rule means the request is permitted by default. Under instruction B, the absence of a governing rule means the request is not permitted by default.

items.case: Student Julian Cross submits an appeal on October 5 for an 11-point grade increase in Course HIST-204, attaching a verified medical certificate and paying the $45.00 processing fee.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated requirement for Dean authorization is treated as fulfilled, satisfying the clause’s condition for large adjustments.
criteria.no: The unstated requirement for Dean authorization is treated as unfulfilled, failing the clause’s condition for large adjustments.

items.rationale: The policy mandates written Dean authorization for increases over ten points. The case does not state whether Julian obtained this authorization. Under instruction A, the unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, blocking permission. Under instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied, allowing permission.

title: Nexus Dynamics Inc. Software Release Management Policy
policy:
1. This Release Management Policy applies to all software deployments for Nexus Dynamics Inc. products and governs the promotion of builds from staging to production environments.
2. Standard releases require a minimum of three independent code reviews and a successful execution of the full regression test suite, which must cover at least ninety percent of critical user paths.
3. Any release introducing new external API integrations must include a completed security vulnerability assessment signed by the Chief Information Security Officer prior to deployment. Releases modifying user authentication flows are exempt from this assessment requirement.
4. Emergency hotfixes may bypass the standard regression suite if they address a production outage lasting longer than thirty minutes, provided the change is isolated to a single microservice and includes automated rollback scripts.
5. All approved releases must be deployed during the designated maintenance window between 02:00 and 05:00 UTC, unless an emergency hotfix is authorized under Clause 4.
6. Release candidates must remain in the staging environment for a minimum of five days to allow for performance monitoring and stakeholder validation before production promotion. Any deployment that does not satisfy this five-day staging requirement requires a formal exemption waiver signed by the VP of Engineering.
7. This policy was originally effective on 1 January 2023. An amendment adopted on 15 March 2024 removed the authentication flow exemption in Clause 3, requiring a security assessment for all authentication modifications. The amendment applies to requests submitted on or after 16 March 2024.

items.case: On 10 April 2024, Senior Developer Elena Rostova submitted a request to promote Build 442 of the Payment Gateway to production. The build passed all regression tests and included three code reviews. The deployment is scheduled for 03:00 UTC on 11 April 2024.
items.question: Is a formal exemption waiver required for this deployment?

criteria.yes: The unstated staging duration is treated as not met, triggering the waiver requirement in Clause 6.
criteria.no: The unstated staging duration is treated as met, satisfying Clause 6 and negating the waiver requirement.

items.rationale: The case omits the staging duration. Under Instruction A, the missing condition is treated as unsatisfied, so Clause 6 mandates a waiver (yes). Under Instruction B, the missing condition is treated as satisfied, so Clause 6 is met and no waiver is needed (no).

items.case: On 12 March 2024, Lead Architect Marcus Thorne submitted a request to deploy Build 891, which modifies the OAuth2 login sequence. The request was reviewed and a decision was issued on 20 March 2024. No security vulnerability assessment was attached to the deployment package.
items.question: Is the deployment request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The request date falls before the amendment's effective date, so the old exemption applies and the missing assessment is acceptable.
criteria.no: The decision date falls after the amendment's effective date, so the new rule applies and the missing assessment blocks approval.

items.rationale: The policy changed on 16 March 2024. Under Instruction A, the pre-amendment version applies (request date 12 March), granting the auth-flow exemption and permitting the release (yes). Under Instruction B, the post-amendment version applies (decision date 20 March), removing the exemption and blocking the release due to the missing assessment (no).

items.case: Build 550 was promoted to the staging environment on Friday, 1 March 2024 at 10:00 UTC. The release manager scheduled the production deployment for Wednesday, 6 March 2024 at 03:00 UTC.
items.question: Does the proposed deployment schedule satisfy the minimum staging period?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days yields exactly five days between staging promotion and deployment, meeting the minimum threshold.
criteria.no: Counting business days yields only four days (excluding the weekend), falling short of the five-day minimum.

items.rationale: Clause 6 requires a minimum of five days. Under Instruction A, business days are counted: Friday 1 March to Wednesday 6 March spans four business days, failing the requirement (no). Under Instruction B, calendar days are counted: the span is exactly five calendar days, satisfying the requirement (yes).

title: Verdant Research Foundation Grant Allocation Policy
policy:
1. The Verdant Research Foundation awards project grants to eligible principal investigators for research advancing sustainable agriculture and rural resilience.
2. Eligible projects must focus on one of the following primary methodologies: controlled field trials, longitudinal soil analysis, or computational crop modeling.
3. Grant requests submitted between 1 January 2024 and 30 September 2024 are subject to a maximum award limit of $75,000 per project under the original policy version.
4. Requests submitted on or after 1 October 2024, reflecting the policy amendment effective that date, are subject to a maximum award limit of $100,000 per project, provided the applicant has secured a matching institutional commitment of at least 15% of the requested amount.
5. All grant applications must include a signed letter of support from a senior department chair and a preliminary budget breakdown approved by the institution's finance office.
6. The Foundation reserves the right to defer funding decisions for up to ninety days to allow for independent peer review and administrative verification.
7. Funds released under this policy must be expended within eighteen months of the award date and cannot be reallocated to personnel salaries exceeding forty percent of the total grant value. Any unspent balance after the expenditure period must be returned to the Foundation.

items.case: On 15 September 2024, Dr. Aris Thorne submitted a grant request for $90,000 to fund a longitudinal soil analysis project. The application included all standard documentation and confirmed a 20% institutional matching commitment. The Foundation's review committee issued its funding decision on 15 October 2024.
items.question: Is the funding request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The decision-date policy version applies, setting a $100,000 cap and 15% matching requirement, both of which the request meets.
criteria.no: The request-date policy version applies, capping awards at $75,000, which the $90,000 request exceeds.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the policy version on the request date (15 September 2024) applies, which sets a $75,000 cap (Clause 3). The $90,000 request exceeds this limit, so it is not permitted. Under instruction B, the policy version on the decision date (15 October 2024) applies, which raises the cap to $100,000 and requires 15% matching funds (Clause 4). The request falls under the new cap and meets the matching requirement, so it is permitted.

items.case: On 20 August 2024, Dr. Elena Rostova submitted a grant request for $60,000 to fund a controlled field trial. The submission package contained a signed letter of support from the Department of Agricultural Sciences. The Foundation's finance office reviewed the file and issued a decision on 15 September 2024.

criteria.yes: The unstated budget requirement is treated as satisfied, fulfilling all documentary conditions in Clause 5.
criteria.no: The unstated budget requirement is treated as unsatisfied, failing the documentary conditions in Clause 5.

Under instruction A, this unstated condition is treated as unsatisfied, failing Clause 5, so the request is not permitted. Under instruction B, the unstated condition is treated as satisfied, fulfilling Clause 5, so the request is permitted.

items.case: On 12 February 2024, Ms. Linnea Vance submitted a grant request for $50,000 to develop an automated greenhouse climate monitoring system. The proposal outlined the research methodology, included a department chair's endorsement, and provided an approved institutional budget. The Foundation issued its decision on 1 March 2024.
items.question: Is the funding request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The methodology list in Clause 2 is treated as illustrative, allowing the similar unlisted methodology to qualify.
criteria.no: The methodology list in Clause 2 is treated as complete, excluding the unlisted methodology.

The case proposes an automated greenhouse climate monitoring system, which is similar but not explicitly listed. Under instruction A, the list is treated as complete, so the unlisted methodology fails Clause 2, making the request not permitted. Under instruction B, the list is treated as illustrative, so the similar methodology qualifies, making the request permitted.

title: Vertex Data Systems IT Access Control Policy
policy:
1. All requests for system access must be formally submitted through the central Identity Management Portal and include a valid employee identifier along with a brief description of the intended use case.
2. Standard user account provisioning is fully automated upon successful verification against the Human Resources directory, provided the requested permissions align with baseline role templates.
3. All requests for write access to any internal database require prior written approval from the Finance Director to ensure compliance with internal audit standards.
4. Employees designated as Tier-2 analysts may request write access to any internal database without prior managerial approval, as their role inherently requires broad data manipulation capabilities.
5. Temporary access grants exceeding seventy-two hours must include a documented business justification reviewed by the requesting department head and will automatically expire upon the stated end date.
6. Emergency access requests may bypass standard review protocols during critical incidents but require a mandatory post-implementation audit within forty-eight hours of activation to verify necessity.

items.case: On 2024-03-10, employee Marcus Lin, designated as a Tier-2 analyst, submitted a request through the Identity Management Portal for write access to the Q3 financial reporting database. The submission included his employee identifier and a use case description but did not include prior written approval from the Finance Director.

criteria.no: Clause 3 mandates Finance Director approval for all database write access, which is stricter.

Clause 3 is stricter (requires approval), Clause 4 is more specific (targets a named role). Under Instruction A, the stricter clause applies, denying the request due to missing approval. Under Instruction B, the more specific clause applies, permitting it.

criteria.no: No clause covers email signature modifications, so the default rule denies it.

title: NovaStream Technologies Software Release Approval Policy
policy:
1. All production software releases for NovaStream Technologies must be formally approved by the Chief Technology Officer, Elena Rostova, at least forty-eight hours before the scheduled deployment date.
2. A release request is eligible for standard fast-track approval if the total associated infrastructure cost does not exceed $50,000 and the release contains only minor adjustments such as typo corrections, formatting tweaks, or dependency version bumps.
3. Releases introducing new customer-facing features require a completed security audit report dated within the preceding thirty days and a signed risk acceptance form from the Product Director.
4. Emergency hotfixes addressing critical system outages may be deployed immediately without prior approval, provided the incident commander files a post-deployment review within twenty-four hours.
5. Any release utilizing third-party libraries must include a verified dependency scan report confirming the absence of high-severity vulnerabilities.
6. Test environments and internal staging deployments are exempt from clauses 1 through 5, but must still be logged in the central version control system.
7. Requests that do not meet the criteria outlined in clauses 2 through 5 must undergo a full steering committee review, which requires a minimum of five business days for scheduling and evaluation.

title: GreenCanopy Alliance Volunteer Operations Policy
policy:
1. All individuals wishing to volunteer with GreenCanopy Alliance (GCA) must complete a mandatory two-hour orientation and sign a liability waiver before participating in any field activity.
2. Volunteers are permitted to log a maximum of twenty hours per calendar month for community service credit. Any hours exceeding this monthly cap require prior written authorization from the Regional Coordinator.
3. Approved field activities include tree planting, trail maintenance, and community garden cleanup. Volunteers may submit requests for other environmental restoration tasks, which will be evaluated for alignment with GCA’s conservation goals.
4. Travel reimbursement is available for activities located more than ten miles from the volunteer’s registered residential zip code, provided the volunteer holds a valid GCA membership badge. Claims must be submitted through the GCA portal within thirty calendar days of activity completion.
5. All requests for activity approval or expense reimbursement must be logged in the GCA portal. The Volunteer Services team will review submissions and issue a formal decision within five business days of receipt.
6. This policy became effective on January 1, 2024. Any amendments will be published on the GCA intranet and take effect on the specific date stated in the amendment notice.

criteria.no: The activity is similar to listed examples and the list is treated as illustrative, granting automatic qualification.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists specific approved activities. Under instruction A, the list is exhaustive, so wetland reed harvesting requires a separate request. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so similar restoration tasks qualify automatically without extra approval.

title: Oakridge Distribution Center: Pallet Stacking and Load Handling Protocol
policy:
1. All inbound freight exceeding 500 kg must be secured using stretch wrap or ratchet straps before placement in Storage Zone B.
2. Forklift operators must complete a certified stability assessment for any load taller than 2.5 meters prior to transport across the main aisle.
3. Manual handling of individual cartons is restricted to weights of 25 kg or less; heavier items require two-person teams or mechanical aids.
4. Temperature-sensitive goods must be moved to Climate-Controlled Bay 4 within four hours of docking.
5. Pallets exhibiting structural damage, including split deck boards, protruding nails, or cracked corner blocks, must be removed from active inventory and placed in the Rejects Corridor.
6. Shift supervisors may authorize temporary storage of oversized machinery in Aisle 7, provided the items do not exceed 4.2 meters in length and are flagged with high-visibility cones.
7. Any deviation from this protocol requires written approval from the Site Operations Manager and must be logged in the daily incident register.
8. This policy supersedes all previous stacking guidelines issued prior to March 15, 2024.

criteria.no: The applicable policy version restricts manual handling to 25 kg or less.

criteria.no: No policy clause covers the request, and the fallback rule grants permission.

Under instruction A, the fallback rule applies to unlisted requests, yielding 'no'. Under instruction B, the fallback rule applies, yielding 'yes'.

criteria.no: The example list is treated as illustrative, and the item falls outside the explicit list.

Under instruction A, the list is treated as complete, resulting in 'yes'. Under instruction B, the list is treated as illustrative, resulting in 'no'.

title: AetherTech Solutions Product Warranty Policy
policy:

2. Warranty claims must be submitted in writing to the Customer Support Director, Marcus Thorne, within 30 days of discovering the defect.
3. Claims involving software malfunctions are excluded from standard coverage unless the device was purchased after January 15, 2023.
4. Replacement units will be issued at no cost for defects up to $500 in retail value; claims exceeding $500 require executive approval from Elena Rostova.
5. Products modified by unauthorized third parties are immediately void of all warranty benefits, regardless of purchase date or defect type.
6. For international shipments, an additional 15 days are granted to account for customs processing and delivery delays.
7. Claims for devices purchased through the AetherTech online portal must be submitted within 45 days of discovery, superseding general submission windows.
8. Customers may request a prorated refund instead of a replacement if the original purchase price was under $200 and the defect occurs within the first 90 days.

criteria.no: The elapsed time between discovery and submission exceeds the 30-day limit when counted using the specified method.

Under Instruction B, counting calendar days yields 24 days, which falls within the limit, so the request is permitted.

title: Veridian Solutions Ltd. Payroll Adjustment Policy
policy: 1. Eligibility for overtime compensation at Veridian Solutions Ltd. is strictly limited to non-exempt staff members who exceed forty hours of documented work within a standard seven-day pay cycle. 2. Compensatory rates are applied at one-and-a-half times the standard hourly wage for all hours surpassing the forty-hour threshold, while work performed on officially recognized corporate holidays accrues at double the base rate. 3. All overtime requests exceeding twenty hours per month require direct written approval from the Department Head before scheduling. 4. Travel and subsistence reimbursements are restricted to a maximum of eight hundred dollars per fiscal quarter per individual, and all claims valued over sixty dollars must be accompanied by itemized digital receipts. 5. Corrections for timekeeping system errors or missed clock-in events must be formally requested within five days of the incident and require dual sign-off from the employee and their line manager. 6. Financial adjustments exceeding three hundred dollars in a single pay period trigger an automatic audit and demand written approval from the Chief Financial Officer before funds are disbursed. 7. Any overtime request involving senior management personnel is automatically approved by the payroll system without requiring managerial sign-off. 8. The payroll operations team maintains final discretion to reject or delay any submission that fails to meet documentation standards or falls outside the prescribed submission windows.

criteria.no: The elapsed time falls within the five-day window under the specified counting method.

Under Instruction A (business days), the submission is within the limit, so it is not late (no). Under Instruction B (calendar days), it exceeds the limit, so it is late (yes).

criteria.no: The resolving clause requires direct written approval from the Department Head.

Under Instruction B (more specific applies), Clause 7 governs, granting auto-approval (yes).

title: Apex Loan Servicing Corp. Late Fee Waiver and Payment Adjustment Policy
policy:
1. Borrowers may request a waiver of the standard two percent late payment fee if the missed payment occurred within the first three months of loan origination.
2. Requests for fee waivers will be denied when the missed payment resulted from administrative processing errors, such as bank routing delays or duplicate automatic debits.
3. The servicing department must process all waiver and extension requests within five business days of receipt. All requests must be submitted in writing through the secure client portal or via certified mail. If the borrower’s account remains current on all other obligations, the request shall be approved automatically.
4. Borrowers who have utilized a fee waiver or payment extension more than twice in a rolling twelve-month period are ineligible for additional adjustments under this policy.
5. Any request submitted after the scheduled payment due date plus thirty days will be denied. Effective 10 March 2024, this deadline was reduced to fifteen days.
6. This policy supersedes all prior verbal agreements and applies to all residential mortgage and personal installment loans serviced by Apex as of 15 January 2024.

criteria.no: The postal delivery failure is similar to the listed administrative errors, so under an illustrative list interpretation it qualifies as an excluded reason and the request is denied.

Under instruction A, the list is complete, so only those two reasons are denied; the postal failure is permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the similar postal failure is treated as an administrative error and denied.

title: Meridian Heights Leasing Policy
policy:
Meridian Heights Leasing Policy
1. All commercial and residential leases under the Meridian Heights portfolio require rent to be paid in full by the first calendar day of each month via electronic transfer to the designated landlord account.
2. Rent paid after the third day of any month incurs a mandatory late fee of one hundred dollars, regardless of the unit type or lease duration.
3. Tenants are strictly prohibited from installing external structural modifications without prior written consent, such as satellite dishes, security cameras, or permanent awnings.
4. For industrial storage units classified under Schedule C, rent paid after the tenth day of the month incurs a reduced late fee of forty dollars to accommodate bulk logistics billing cycles.
5. Either party may terminate a fixed-term lease early or decline renewal by providing written notice to the property management office at least fourteen days prior to the scheduled lease expiration date.
6. All maintenance requests for common areas must be submitted through the online portal within forty-eight hours of identification, and emergency repairs will be prioritized based on safety risk assessments.
7. Landlords reserve the right to conduct routine property inspections with a minimum of seventy-two hours written notice, except in cases of suspected utility damage or fire hazards.

criteria.yes: The stricter general clause imposes the fee for payments after the third day.
criteria.no: The more specific clause for industrial units waives the fee for payments before the tenth day.

items.rationale: Clause 2 applies a $100 fee after the 3rd (stricter), while Clause 4 applies a $40 fee after the 10th to industrial units (more specific). Under instruction A, the stricter clause governs, triggering the fee. Under instruction B, the specific clause governs, exempting the payment.

criteria.no: The listed prohibited items are treated as illustrative, so similar external fixtures are banned.

Under instruction A, the list is complete, so only listed items are banned, making the request permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so similar items are banned, making the request prohibited.

criteria.no: Counting business days yields only eleven days, falling short of the required period.

title: Apex Logistics Ltd. Overtime and Expense Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs overtime compensation and employee expense reimbursements for all full-time staff at Apex Logistics Ltd., effective 1 January 2024. Part-time contractors are excluded from overtime provisions but may claim expenses under Clause 3.
2. Overtime is defined as hours worked beyond forty per week. Employees must submit an overtime claim form to their direct supervisor for pre-approval within three days of the work performed. Approved overtime is paid at one-and-a-half times the base hourly rate.
3. Reimbursable expenses include reasonable costs incurred for business travel, client meals, and essential software subscriptions. Claims under two hundred dollars are processed automatically without supervisor sign-off. All other claims require written approval.
4. All overtime and expense claims must be submitted to the Payroll Department by the twentieth day of the month following the month in which the cost was incurred or the hours were worked. Late submissions will be deferred to the subsequent pay cycle.
5. Processed claims are paid via direct deposit on the final Friday of the month. If the final Friday falls on a public holiday, payment is issued on the preceding business day. Payroll disputes must be lodged within ten days of payment receipt.
6. This policy may be amended at any time by the Chief Financial Officer. Amendments take effect on the date published to staff via the internal portal. Conflicting prior policies are superseded.

criteria.no: Submission falls outside three calendar days of the work date.

title: Veridian Analytics Ltd. Data Retention and Access Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs the retention, access, and deletion of personal data collected by Veridian Analytics Ltd. from clients and end-users. All departments must comply to ensure regulatory alignment and operational security.
2. Standard customer records shall be retained for exactly 365 days from the date of last interaction. Records related to financial transactions exceeding $5,000 must be retained for 1,825 days from the transaction date.
3. Employees may request access to retained records only for active project verification, compliance auditing, or direct client support. All requests require written approval from a department head before data is released.
4. Approved access is strictly limited to viewing and downloading necessary fields. Printing, exporting to external drives, or sharing data with third parties is prohibited unless explicitly authorized in writing by the Chief Privacy Officer.
5. Upon expiration of the retention period, all data must be permanently purged from primary servers. Archival backups may retain encrypted copies for up to 90 days for disaster recovery purposes before final destruction.
6. Requests for data deletion by clients must be processed within 14 days of receipt. Deletion applies to all standard records unless an active legal hold or pending audit notice exists.
7. Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination, and will be reported to the compliance committee for further review.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, data analyst Elena Rostova submitted a request through the central portal to access customer interaction logs from January 2024. Her stated purpose was quarterly performance benchmarking for the marketing department. The request covered 450 records and was logged at 09:15 AM.

criteria.yes: The requested purpose aligns with the nature of the listed examples and qualifies under an illustrative interpretation.
criteria.no: The requested purpose is absent from the explicit list and fails under a complete-list interpretation.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists three specific purposes. Instruction A treats them as exhaustive, excluding benchmarking. Instruction B treats them as non-exhaustive, including similar internal reviews.

criteria.no: The unmentioned approval condition is presumed unsatisfied, causing the event to fail a mandatory requirement.

title: Meridian Heights Logistics – Building Access Policy
policy:
1. All employees must carry their assigned RFID badge at all times while on the premises. Standard building access is granted Monday through Friday between 07:00 and 19:00. Access outside these hours requires prior approval.
2. Requests for after-hours or weekend access must be submitted to the Facilities Office at least 24 hours in advance. Approval is granted only when the request specifies a legitimate operational need, identifies the exact zones to be accessed, and confirms that a minimum of two authorized personnel will be present simultaneously.
3. All personnel and approved contractors may access the server room after presenting a valid ID and signing the liability waiver.

Temporary paper passes are issued immediately upon reporting and remain valid for a maximum of five business days.

Because the scenario is uncovered, Instruction A dictates the answer is 'no', while Instruction B dictates the answer is 'yes'.

Under Instruction B, the more specific clause controls, yielding 'no'.

Under Instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied, so the request is permitted ('yes').

title: Meridian Health Partners Clinical Scheduling Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs clinical appointment scheduling at Meridian Health Partners. The original text took effect on 2023-09-01. An amended version took effect on 2024-04-15.
2. Routine consultations may be scheduled up to thirty days in advance. Urgent care slots may be booked up to five days in advance. All bookings require a minimum twenty-minute buffer between patients.

6. The hospital scheduling system automatically approves requests for the following modalities: CT angiography, echocardiograms, and lumbar punctures. Requests for other modalities require manual review by the department head.

criteria.no: The original policy version applies, making Dr. Vance unavailable on Tuesday afternoons.

title: Veridian University Grade Adjustment Policy
policy:
1. At Veridian University, all requests for grade adjustments must be submitted in writing to the Office of Academic Standards within five days of the official grade posting date for the relevant term.
2. Requests concerning laboratory, clinical, or studio courses are subject to a separate technical review process and must include a signed attestation from the primary course instructor confirming the discrepancy.
3. Grade adjustment requests are permitted for all courses with fewer than forty enrolled students, provided the original assessment utilized a standardized rubric.
4. Grade adjustment requests are strictly prohibited for all courses offered by the Department of Linguistics, regardless of enrollment size or assessment method.
5. The maximum allowable adjustment for any single assignment or examination is five percentage points, regardless of the original score or the nature of the administrative error.
6. Students must wait at least five days after receiving official instructor feedback before submitting an adjustment request, to allow for initial clarification discussions.
7. Final course grades officially posted prior to September 1, 2024, are permanently closed to adjustment and cannot be reconsidered under any circumstances.

items.case: On November 12, 2024, student Marcus Lin submits a written request to the Office of Academic Standards asking to remove a course withdrawal (W) notation from his transcript for a 3-credit seminar that ended in August 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses withdrawal notations or transcript corrections, so the request falls outside the policy's scope.
criteria.no: No clause addresses withdrawal notations or transcript corrections, so the request falls outside the policy's scope.

items.rationale: Clauses 1 through 7 exclusively govern grade adjustments, lab reviews, enrollment thresholds, departmental prohibitions, point caps, waiting periods, and historical grade closures. None cover transcript notation changes or withdrawal appeals. Although Clause 1 mentions submission to the Office of Academic Standards and Clause 7 mentions posted records, neither applies to withdrawal notations. Under Instruction A, absence of a covering clause permits the request (yes). Under Instruction B, absence of a covering clause prohibits it (no).

items.case: On October 5, 2024, student Elena Rostova submits a written request for a grade adjustment in a Department of Linguistics course that had 35 enrolled students and utilized a standardized rubric.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 3 applies and permits the request based on the enrollment threshold.
criteria.no: Clause 4 applies and prohibits the request based on the departmental scope.

items.rationale: Clause 3 permits adjustments for courses with fewer than 40 students (35 < 40), while Clause 4 prohibits adjustments for all Linguistics courses. Both clauses apply and yield opposite outcomes. title: Aethelgard Dynamics Export Compliance Policy
policy:
1. All exports from Aethelgard Dynamics of controlled technology exceeding USD 25,000 in aggregate value per destination country require prior written authorization from the Chief Compliance Officer.
2. Requests for authorization must be submitted to the compliance portal at least ten days before the scheduled shipment date to allow for standard processing.
3. All exports to countries under the Regional Sanctions Framework require prior written authorization from the Chief Compliance Officer.
4. The Chief Compliance Officer may approve requests for standard commercial goods up to USD 50,000 without additional review.
5. Any export request involving cryptographic components requires mandatory verification of the end-user’s final application and a signed end-use certificate before authorization is granted.
6. Approved authorizations remain valid for the fiscal quarter in which they are issued and may be renewed upon written request submitted three days before expiration.
7. The Compliance Department reserves the right to update this policy at any time, with amendments taking effect upon publication on the internal network.

items.case: On October 10, 2023, logistics manager Elena Rostova submitted a request to export a batch of standard commercial sensors valued at USD 45,000 to Germany. The Chief Compliance Officer reviewed the file and issued a decision on October 25, 2023.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy version on the request date applies; the amendment suspending German sensor exports was not yet published, so Clause 4 permits approval up to USD 50,000.
criteria.no: The policy version on the decision date applies; the amendment published October 15 suspends German sensor exports, overriding Clause 4.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, the October 10 version applies, where Clause 4 allows approval for standard commercial goods under USD 50,000. Under Instruction B, the October 25 version applies, incorporating the October 15 amendment that suspends exports of these sensors to Germany, rendering the request impermissible.

items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days, submission occurred eleven days before shipment, satisfying the ten-day requirement in Clause 2.
criteria.no: Counting business days, submission occurred only five days before shipment, failing the ten-day requirement in Clause 2.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, business days are counted; only five weekdays fall between November 6 and November 17, failing Clause 2's ten-day threshold. Under Instruction B, calendar days are counted; eleven days fall between the dates, meeting Clause 2's requirement.

criteria.no: Clause 3 imposes a mandatory authorization requirement for all sanctioned destinations, which is stricter than the discretionary approval in Clause 4.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, the stricter Clause 3 applies, mandating prior authorization for all sanctioned destinations and blocking the request. Under Instruction B, the more specific Clause 4 applies, as it precisely covers standard commercial goods under USD 50,000, permitting approval without additional review.

title: Aethelgard Dynamics Information Security Incident Response Policy
policy:
1. Effective January 1, 2024, all Aethelgard Dynamics personnel must report suspected information security incidents to the Security Operations Centre within three days of discovery.
2. Incidents involving the compromise of more than five hundred customer records require immediate escalation to Chief Information Security Officer David Chen.
3. Remote access requests for incident investigation must be approved by a department head before any diagnostic tools are deployed.
4. Temporary access credentials issued during active incidents expire automatically after fourteen days and cannot be renewed without a written request.
5. Incident remediation costs exceeding ten thousand dollars require formal board notification within forty-eight hours of invoice receipt.
6. All incident reports must be submitted using the standard template before any external communication or media statement is released.
7. Personnel directly involved in an incident must complete mandatory security retraining within thirty days of official case closure.
8. During declared critical incidents, the Security Operations Centre may deploy diagnostic tools without prior department head approval.

items.case: On Thursday, November 2, 2024, analyst Lena Rostova discovered a phishing email that bypassed the filter. She submitted the incident report to the Security Operations Centre on Monday, November 6, 2024. The incident involved 120 customer records and four thousand dollars in estimated losses.
items.question: Is the report submission compliant with the deadline?

criteria.yes: The submission falls within three business days of discovery.
criteria.no: The submission falls outside three calendar days of discovery.

items.rationale: Clause 1 requires reporting within three days. Counting business days from Thursday Nov 2 yields Friday Nov 3 (day 1) and Monday Nov 6 (day 2), which is within the limit. Counting calendar days yields Friday Nov 3 (1), Saturday Nov 4 (2), Sunday Nov 5 (3), and Monday Nov 6 (4), which exceeds the limit. The instruction determines the counting method, flipping the compliance result.

items.case: During a declared critical incident on March 15, 2024, Security Operations Centre lead Marcus Vance deployed a network scanner to isolate a ransomware threat affecting 800 records and causing fifteen thousand dollars in damages, without obtaining department head approval.
items.question: Is the deployment permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause for critical incidents overrides the general approval requirement.
criteria.no: The stricter clause requiring department head approval overrides the exception.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 8 both apply. Clause 3 strictly requires department head approval before deployment. Clause 8 specifically permits deployment without approval during declared critical incidents. Clause 3 is stricter; Clause 8 is more specific. Applying the stricter clause (A) denies permission. Applying the more specific clause (B) grants permission.

criteria.yes: The unstated written request condition is treated as satisfied, meeting Clause 4.
criteria.no: The unstated written request condition is treated as not satisfied, violating Clause 4.

Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, making the renewal non-compliant. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, making the renewal compliant.

title: Zenith Airways Passenger Disruption Policy
policy:
1. Zenith Airways administers disruption compensation according to this policy, effective 1 January 2023. All requests must reference the booking confirmation issued by the airline.
2. A full fare refund is authorized when an operational disruption lasts longer than five days. The duration is measured from the initial scheduled departure until the passenger reaches the final destination.
3. Monetary compensation for flight delays exceeding two hours is available only to passengers who hold an active Silver tier loyalty membership at the time of travel. Proof of status must accompany the claim.
4. Claims for partial fare refunds following a flight cancellation must be submitted within fourteen days of the originally scheduled departure date. Late submissions are processed at the discretion of the Claims Office.
5. Approved compensation amounts are calculated based on the ticket class, with economy tickets capped at three hundred dollars and business class capped at six hundred dollars. Taxes and fees are excluded from the calculation.
6. All financial settlements will be transferred to the original booking payment method within thirty days of the final decision by the Claims Office. Disputes regarding eligibility must be filed in writing within sixty days.

items.case: Flight 882 experienced a disruption beginning on Friday, 10 March 2023, and concluding on Thursday, 16 March 2023. Passenger Elias Vance requests a full fare refund.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The disruption duration exceeds five days when counted in calendar days.
criteria.no: The disruption duration does not exceed five days when counted in business days.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the period is counted in business days, yielding exactly five days, which does not exceed the five-day threshold in clause 2, so the request is not permitted. Under instruction B, the period is counted in calendar days, yielding six days, which exceeds the threshold, so the request is permitted.

items.case: Passenger Mira Chen requests monetary compensation for a three-hour delay on flight 209. Her ticket was purchased for two hundred fifty dollars on 12 April 2023. The flight departed from Seattle and arrived in Denver.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated Silver tier loyalty membership condition is treated as satisfied.
criteria.no: The unstated Silver tier loyalty membership condition is treated as not satisfied.

Under instruction A, the unstated condition is treated as not satisfied, so the request is not permitted. Under instruction B, it is treated as satisfied, so the request is permitted.

criteria.no: No policy clause covers denied boarding, and uncovered requests are permitted.

Under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted, so the request is not denied. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, so the request is denied.

title: Professional Development Allowance Policy
policy:
1. Meridian Analytics Ltd. provides a Professional Development Allowance to eligible employees for approved courses, certifications, or conferences related to their current role.
2. Eligible employees may submit a request for reimbursement up to two thousand five hundred dollars per fiscal year. Requests must be submitted within thirty days of completing the activity.
3. To qualify, the activity must have been pre-approved by the employee’s direct manager and the Human Resources department. Course materials and registration fees are covered, but travel and accommodation expenses are excluded.
4. The allowance resets on the first day of each fiscal year. Unused balances do not carry forward to subsequent years.
5. This policy was originally effective on January 1, 2022. An amendment approved on October 1, 2023, reduced the maximum annual reimbursement limit to one thousand five hundred dollars.
6. Employees must provide original receipts and a certificate of completion with their request. The Human Resources department will process approved requests within ten days of receipt.
7. Disputes regarding eligibility or documentation will be resolved by the Chief People Officer, whose determination is final.

He submitted his reimbursement request on Monday, June 19, 2023. The workshop was pre-approved by his manager, and he attached original receipts and a completion certificate.

criteria.no: The submission falls outside thirty calendar days of completion.

title: Meridian Heights Management Co. Residential Leasing Guidelines
policy:
Meridian Heights Management Co. Residential Leasing Guidelines
1. Requests to extend the initial lease term require written approval from the Property Manager and must be submitted at least fourteen days before the requested effective date, accompanied by a signed acknowledgment of the revised terms.
2. Requests for balcony modifications are permitted if the tenant provides a valid contractor license and pays a two hundred dollar processing fee.
3. Requests for balcony modifications are not permitted for tenants who currently keep domestic animals in the unit.
4. Late rent payments incur a penalty of five percent of the monthly amount if paid after the fifth day of the month, calculated on the base rent excluding any prior arrears.
5. Subleasing is permitted for periods not exceeding ninety days, provided the original tenant remains financially liable for the full lease term and submits a written notice of the subtenant's full name and contact information.
6. All security deposit disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration within sixty days of lease termination.

criteria.no: The more specific clause (targeting tenants with animals) governs the conflict and prohibits the request.

Clause 3 is more specific because it applies only to the subset of tenants with animals. Under instruction A, the stricter clause prevails, permitting the request. Under instruction B, the more specific clause prevails, prohibiting it.

criteria.no: The request falls outside every clause and uncovered requests are not permitted by default.

title: Verdant Harvest Processing Ltd. Food Safety and Compliance Protocol
policy:
1. All food safety procedures at Verdant Harvest Processing Ltd. apply to every facility, contractor, and third-party logistics provider operating under our brand from 1 January 2024 onwards, ensuring consistent hygiene standards across all production lines.
2. All product formulation or packaging modifications require written approval from the Quality Director before implementation.
3. Minor packaging label updates for existing stock-keeping units require only email notification to the Shift Supervisor.
4. All incoming fresh produce shipments must be accompanied by a valid phytosanitary certificate issued within thirty days of harvest, and the transporting driver must present a digital logbook showing continuous temperature monitoring during transit.
5. Any cold storage temperature deviation exceeding two degrees Celsius above the set point must be reported to the regional compliance office within five days of detection to initiate corrective actions.
6. Staff handling allergen-containing products must change gloves and sanitize work surfaces between batches, and must complete the annual cross-contamination refresher course before the fiscal year ends to maintain handling certification.

items.case: The packaging team updates the allergen warning font size on an existing stock-keeping unit label without submitting documents to the Quality Director.

criteria.no: The more specific clause for minor label updates takes precedence, requiring only supervisor notification.

Under instruction A, the stricter requirement (Clause 2) applies, making director approval necessary. Under instruction B, the more specific rule (Clause 3) applies, negating the need for director approval.

items.question: Is the shipment admissible under current protocol?

criteria.no: The unstated digital logbook condition is treated as not satisfied, failing the protocol.

Under instruction A, the unestablished logbook requirement is treated as not satisfied, rendering the shipment inadmissible. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted logbook requirement is treated as satisfied, making the shipment admissible.

criteria.no: Counting calendar days places the deadline on 28 October, making 29 October late.

Under instruction B, counting calendar days sets the deadline to 28 October, making the 29 October submission late.

title: Oakridge Retail Ltd Customer Refund and Returns Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs refund requests for merchandise sold by Oakridge Retail Ltd through its physical stores and online platform. All requests must be submitted in writing to the Customer Resolution Team using the standard claim form.
2. Eligible refunds are processed for items returned within 10 days of the original purchase date. The returned merchandise must be unused, unworn, and accompanied by the original sales receipt. Items must be delivered to the central warehouse in Leeds.
3. Refunds are not issued for merchandise acquired using an employee discount code. Standard promotional discounts do not affect eligibility. Clearance items marked with a red price tag are excluded from this policy.
4. Approved refunds are issued to the original payment method within five working days of warehouse receipt. Partial refunds may be granted for items with minor packaging damage at the discretion of the resolution manager. Shipping costs are non-refundable.
5. This document supersedes all prior refund guidelines. An amendment effective 15 June 2024 reduced the return window in Clause 2 from 30 days to 10 days. Historical versions remain archived for audit purposes.

items.case: Elena Rossi submitted a written refund request on 10 June 2024 for a winter coat purchased on 1 June 2024 for £220. The warehouse received the coat on 12 June 2024. The resolution manager issued a decision on 20 June 2024.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted under the policy?

criteria.no: The post-amendment version (10-day window) applies because the decision was made after the amendment date, and the 11-day return exceeds it.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, the policy version in force on 10 June (pre-amendment, 30-day window) governs. The return occurred 11 days after purchase, which is within 30 days, so the request is permitted. Under Instruction B, the version in force on 20 June (post-amendment, 10-day window) governs. The 11-day gap exceeds the 10-day limit, so the request is prohibited.

items.case: Marcus Chen returned a leather briefcase purchased for £150 on 20 October 2024. The warehouse received the item on 22 October 2024. The briefcase was unused and accompanied by the original receipt.

criteria.no: The unstated condition regarding an employee discount code is treated as satisfied, triggering the exception in Clause 3.

items.rationale: Clause 3 prohibits refunds for items bought with an employee discount code. The case neither establishes nor contradicts whether such a code was used. Under Instruction A, this unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, meaning the exception does not trigger and the refund is permitted. Under Instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the exception and prohibiting the refund.

items.case: Sarah Lin purchased a desk lamp for £45 on Friday, 1 November 2024. She submitted a refund request and delivered the unused lamp with its receipt to the warehouse on Thursday, 14 November 2024.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted under the policy?

criteria.no: Counting all calendar days places the return outside the 10-day limit.

Under Instruction A, business day counting applies, placing the return within the limit, so it is permitted. Under Instruction B, calendar day counting applies, placing the return outside the limit, so it is prohibited.

title: AeroVista Logistics Travel and Expense Policy
policy:
AeroVista Logistics Travel and Expense Policy, effective March 1, 2024.
1. Airfare reimbursement requires booking economy class on flights under six hours. First class is permitted only for executives above the Director level on international routes exceeding six hours.
2. Ground transportation expenses are reimbursable up to $150 per day for taxi or rideshare services. Rental cars require prior approval from the department head and are capped at $90 per day, excluding fuel and tolls.
3. Meal allowances are fixed at $45 per day for domestic travel and $75 per day for international travel. Receipts are mandatory for any single meal exceeding $50, regardless of location.
4. Accommodation costs must not exceed $220 per night in standard business districts. Bookings in premium or resort zones require written justification from the finance controller and are subject to a $150 nightly cap.
5. All entertainment and client hospitality expenses are strictly prohibited and will not be reimbursed under any circumstances.
6. Client entertainment expenses incurred during approved trade missions in the Asia-Pacific region are reimbursable up to $250 per event when accompanied by an attendee list.
7. All expense submissions must be filed within thirty days of the trip's conclusion. Late submissions require a signed waiver from the employee's direct supervisor and the finance team.

criteria.no: No clause covers the request, and the instruction prohibits uncovered requests.

title: Aether Goods Ltd. Customer Refund and Return Policy
policy:
1. Aether Goods Ltd. accepts standard returns within thirty days of the original purchase date. Customers must submit a completed return form and include the original receipt or order confirmation.
2. All returned merchandise must be in its original condition, unused, and accompanied by all manufacturer packaging and accessories. Items showing signs of wear, alteration, or missing components will be declined.
3. Products found to be defective or damaged upon delivery qualify for an immediate exchange or full refund. This provision applies regardless of the standard return window, provided the fault is verified by a certified technician.
4. Customers may request an expedited same-day refund for items purchased during the annual holiday sale. Eligible items include winter coats, holiday decorations, and seasonal gift sets.

6. Refund approvals are communicated via email within five business days of the warehouse receiving the returned package. Funds are credited to the original payment method within ten business days of approval.

title: Vanguard Mutual Auto Claims Policy (VMA-2024)
policy:
1. Claims must be submitted in writing within thirty days of the loss event. Submissions must include the policy number, date of loss, and a detailed description of the incident.
2. The insured vehicle must have been parked in a designated residential or commercial parking area at the time of loss.
3. Coverage applies to physical damage caused by collision, theft, fire, or vandalism. Each covered event is subject to a $500 deductible per occurrence.
4. Effective January 1, 2024: Claims for repair costs exceeding $1,500 require written pre-authorization from a Vanguard adjuster before work begins. Amended July 15, 2024: The pre-authorization threshold is updated to $2,000.
5. Payment will be issued within ten business days of approved claim documentation. Funds are disbursed directly to the repair facility or the policyholder, at the adjuster’s discretion.
6. This policy covers only the primary insured and listed additional drivers operating the specified vehicle(s). Coverage does not extend to temporary substitutes, commercial fleet vehicles, or unregistered automobiles.

items.case: Elena Rostova submitted a claim on April 10, 2024, for $3,200 in hail damage to her insured sedan. The vehicle was struck while stationary near a public park entrance. She provided photos and a repair estimate.

title: Aether Dynamics Ltd. Export Compliance Policy

title: Aethelgard Biomedical Research Centre Laboratory Safety Policy
policy:
Aethelgard Biomedical Research Centre Laboratory Safety Policy
1. All personnel conducting experiments involving hazardous substances must obtain written approval from the designated Safety Officer prior to initiating work. Requests must specify the substances, quantities, and intended procedures.
2. Personal protective equipment is mandatory when handling volatile compounds. Approved eye protection includes safety goggles, chemical splash glasses, and full-face shields. Lab coats and nitrile gloves are required for all chemical transfers.
3. The total volume of flammable liquids stored on any active laboratory bench must not exceed 30 litres.
4. For chromatography procedures requiring mobile phase preparation, a maximum of 50 litres of compatible flammable solvents may be staged on the preparation bench.
5. This policy was originally effective on 12 March 2023. An amendment was issued on 15 November 2024, updating clause 3 to reduce the maximum flammable liquid storage limit to 15 litres per bench. The amendment does not alter clause 4.
6. Historical versions are archived in the central document repository for audit purposes.

criteria.no: The more specific clause (50 litre limit for chromatography) applies, and 40 litres falls within it.

items.rationale: Clause 3 sets a 30 litre limit for all flammable liquids, while clause 4 allows up to 50 litres specifically for chromatography mobile phase preparation. The 40 litre request exceeds the general limit but falls within the specific limit. Applying the stricter clause denies the request; applying the more specific clause permits it.

criteria.no: The list of approved eye protection is complete, restricting approval to only the three listed items.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists safety goggles, chemical splash glasses, and full-face shields as approved eye protection. Polycarbonate safety spectacles are not listed but serve the same protective function. Treating the list as complete excludes them; treating it as illustrative includes them.

criteria.no: The policy version effective on 20 November 2024 applies, with a 15 litre limit that denies 20 litres.
