4. Payroll advances are permitted for employees with a minimum of twelve months continuous service. The maximum advance amount is £750 per calendar year and must be repaid through equal deductions over six consecutive pay cycles. Advance requests are permitted unless the employee has a pending disciplinary investigation.
5. All payroll deductions for charitable giving must be processed through the approved payroll system. Approved deduction categories include donations to registered food banks, animal shelters, and disaster relief funds. Deduction requests exceeding 5% of gross monthly salary require written approval from the finance director.

items.case: On 12 April 2024, senior analyst Marcus Thorne submits a request for a £400 payroll advance to cover unexpected travel costs. Thorne has been continuously employed by Meridian Logistics Ltd since 10 January 2022. He proposes repayment over six monthly cycles starting in June.
items.question: Is the advance request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The unstated disciplinary status is treated as not satisfied, meaning no pending investigation exists, so the exception in clause 4 does not apply and the request meets all stated conditions.
criteria.no: The unstated disciplinary status is treated as satisfied, meaning a pending investigation exists, which triggers the prohibition in clause 4.

items.rationale: Clause 4 permits advances unless a pending disciplinary investigation exists. The case omits any mention of disciplinary status. Instruction A treats this unestablished condition as not satisfied, so the exception is avoided and the request is permitted. Instruction B treats it as satisfied, triggering the exception and blocking the request.

items.case: On 5 May 2024, junior developer Sarah Lin submits Form C-12 claiming a tax-free commuter benefit for a £60 monthly train ticket to her workplace. She attaches the provider invoice and confirms she has not claimed this benefit in the current calendar year.
items.question: Is the benefit claim permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The train ticket is treated as similar to the listed examples, qualifying under an illustrative reading of clause 3.
criteria.no: The train ticket is not explicitly listed in clause 3, and under a complete-list reading it fails to qualify.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists eligible benefits as monthly bus passes, subsidized parking permits, and bicycle purchase grants. The case involves a monthly train ticket, which is similar but not listed. Instruction A treats the list as complete, so the train ticket does not qualify. Instruction B treats it as illustrative, allowing similar transit options to qualify.

items.case: On 20 June 2024, operations manager Julian Voss requests that his monthly salary be split evenly between his primary checking account and a secondary savings account. He submits the request to Payroll Manager David Chen on 10 June 2024, providing both account details and a signed authorization form.
items.question: Is the payment splitting request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses splitting salary across multiple accounts, and instruction A treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: No clause addresses splitting salary across multiple accounts, and instruction B treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The policy covers direct deposit to a single nominated account and procedures to change that account, but contains no rule regarding splitting payments across multiple accounts. The request falls outside all clauses. Instruction A permits uncovered requests, while Instruction B denies them.

title: NovaTech Solutions Vendor Contract Policy
policy:
1. All vendor engagements for NovaTech Solutions must be documented via a formal written contract. Contracts become legally binding only when countersigned by an authorised procurement officer and the requesting department head.
2. Standard procurement requests for recurring operational services, such as office supplies, IT hardware maintenance, and facility cleaning, are pre-approved up to $10,000 per fiscal quarter. Requests exceeding this threshold or covering services not explicitly listed require prior written approval from the Chief Financial Officer.
3. All contracts valued at $5,000 or more must undergo a mandatory 30-day legal and financial review before execution. Contracts specifically designated for cloud software licensing are subject to a separate 14-day technical review cycle.
4. Vendor invoices must be submitted within 5 days of service completion to ensure timely processing. Invoices received after this period will be deferred to the next monthly payment cycle and may incur a 2% administrative delay fee.
5. All contracted parties must adhere to NovaTech’s internal data security protocols. Material breaches of contract terms may result in immediate termination and forfeiture of outstanding payments. All disputes shall be resolved through formal mediation prior to any legal action.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, Marketing Director Elena Rostova requested a vendor contract for corporate event catering services valued at $8,500 for the upcoming quarter.
items.question: Does the request require prior written approval from the Chief Financial Officer?

criteria.yes: The requested service is not in the policy's list, and treating the list as complete places it outside pre-approved categories.
criteria.no: The requested service is clearly similar to the listed examples, and treating the list as illustrative places it within pre-approved categories.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists specific services. Instruction A forces a complete-list reading, excluding catering and triggering the CFO approval requirement. Instruction B forces an illustrative reading, including catering as a similar operational service and waiving the approval requirement.

items.case: On May 3, 2024, the IT department initiated a contract with CloudSync Inc. for enterprise software licensing valued at $7,200.
items.question: Must the contract undergo a 30-day review period before execution?

criteria.yes: The 30-day clause is stricter than the 14-day clause, and applying the stricter rule mandates the longer period.
criteria.no: The 14-day clause is more specific to software licensing, and applying the specificity rule mandates the shorter period.

items.rationale: Clause 3 presents a general 30-day rule for contracts over $5,000 and a specific 14-day rule for software licensing. Instruction A resolves the conflict by applying the stricter timeline (30 days). Instruction B resolves it by applying the more specific timeline (14 days).

items.case: Service completion occurred on Friday, October 11, 2024. The vendor submitted the corresponding invoice on Thursday, October 17, 2024.
items.question: Does the invoice submission miss the deadline?

criteria.yes: Counting in calendar days yields a 6-day span, exceeding the 5-day limit and missing the deadline.
criteria.no: Counting in business days yields a 5-day span, falling within the limit and meeting the deadline.

items.rationale: Clause 4 sets a 5-day submission window. Instruction A counts business days, making the span 5 days (Monday 12 to Friday 16), so the Thursday submission is timely. Instruction B counts calendar days, making the span 6 days, so the submission is late.

title: Oakridge Commercial Properties Early Termination and Deposit Policy
policy:
1. Tenants may request early termination of their lease agreement by submitting a written notice to the Property Management Office at least thirty days before the intended move-out date. Requests must include the tenant’s full name, unit number, and proposed vacating date.
2. Early termination is permitted without penalty if the tenant provides documentation of a qualifying life event, such as job relocation, medical evacuation, or family bereavement. The management team will review the documentation within five working days.
3. Upon approval of an early termination request, the tenant must return all issued access keys, security fobs, and parking permits to the leasing desk. Failure to return these items will result in a deduction of fifty dollars per missing item.
4. The security deposit will be refunded to the original payment method within fourteen days of receiving the returned keys, provided a final property inspection confirms no damage beyond normal wear and tear. The inspection must be conducted by a certified Oakridge Commercial Properties inspector.
5. Any outstanding rent or utility charges must be settled in full before the deposit refund is processed. If partial payments are made, the remaining balance must be cleared within seven days of the move-out date.

items.case: Tenant Elena Rostova submitted a written early termination request on March 10 for unit 4B, citing a sudden career transfer to another state. She included official HR transfer letters dated March 8. The property management office approved the request on March 12.
items.question: Is the early termination request permitted without penalty under the policy?

criteria.yes: The policy treats the listed examples as illustrative, allowing similar qualifying events like career transfers.
criteria.no: The policy treats the listed examples as a complete list, and career transfer is not explicitly listed.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists specific qualifying life events without limiting language. Under instruction A, the list is exhaustive, so Elena's career transfer does not qualify. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so her similar professional relocation qualifies.

items.case: Tenant Marcus Chen vacated unit 12A on May 15 and returned all keys and parking permits to the leasing desk on May 16. He had paid all outstanding rent and utility charges in full by May 14. The management office initiated the deposit refund process on May 17.
items.question: Is the security deposit refund properly authorized for processing?

criteria.yes: The policy's requirement for an inspection confirming no damage is treated as satisfied because the case does not contradict it.
criteria.no: The policy's requirement for an inspection confirming no damage is treated as not satisfied because the case does not establish it.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires a final inspection confirming no damage beyond normal wear and tear. The case neither confirms nor denies that this inspection occurred or its results. Under instruction A, this unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, blocking authorization. Under instruction B, it is treated as satisfied, allowing authorization.

items.case: Tenant David Park returned all access keys and parking permits for unit 7C to the leasing desk on Friday, June 21. The property management office logged the receipt at 4:00 PM. The refund was issued on Thursday, July 4.
items.question: Is the security deposit refund compliant with the policy's timeframe?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days places the refund within the fourteen-day limit.
criteria.no: Counting business days places the refund outside the fourteen-day limit.

items.rationale: Clause 4 sets a fourteen-day refund period. Under instruction A, counting only business days excludes the intervening weekends, accelerating the effective deadline and making the July 4 issuance late. Under instruction B, counting all calendar days includes the weekends, extending the effective deadline and making the issuance timely.

title: Vertex Dynamics Information Security Incident Policy
policy:
Vertex Dynamics Information Security Incident Policy
1. All security incidents at Vertex Dynamics resulting in direct financial loss exceeding $10,000 require immediate shutdown of the affected network segment to prevent further exfiltration.
2. Incidents involving financial data hosted on the payroll server may be isolated without shutdown if containment is achieved within four hours and verified by IT Manager Maya Lin.
3. Breaches involving customer email addresses require notification to Data Protection Officer Elias Vance within twenty-four hours of detection, accompanied by a preliminary impact summary.
4. Third-party vendor incidents affecting more than 500 customer records require mandatory review by external legal counsel before any public statement is issued or remediation is finalized.
5. All response actions must be logged in the central audit system with precise timestamps, personnel identifiers, and technical descriptions.
6. Personnel involved in incident response must submit a written report to Chief Information Security Officer Dr. Aris Thorne within five business days of resolution, with submissions after 30 June 2024 requiring digital signatures.
7. Routine maintenance causing temporary degradation is excluded from reporting unless customer data is accessed without authorization during the maintenance window.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, a ransomware attack on the payroll server caused $15,000 in direct financial loss. The IT team contained the breach within three hours and verified containment with IT Manager Maya Lin. The team requests to isolate the server without shutting it down.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause prevails, allowing isolation without shutdown.
criteria.no: The stricter clause prevails, mandating shutdown.

items.rationale: Clauses 1 and 2 apply and conflict. Clause 1 mandates shutdown (stricter). Clause 2 permits isolation for payroll servers under specific conditions (more specific). Under instruction A, the stricter clause prevails, making isolation without shutdown impermissible. Under instruction B, the more specific clause prevails, making it permissible.

items.case: On 5 April 2024, a breach involving customer phone numbers was detected at Vertex Dynamics. The incident response team requests to notify Data Protection Officer Elias Vance within twenty-four hours.
items.question: Is the request prohibited?

criteria.yes: The request is uncovered, and uncovered requests are not permitted.
criteria.no: The request is uncovered, and uncovered requests are permitted.

items.rationale: Clause 3 covers email addresses but does not cover phone numbers. No clause covers the request. Under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted, so the request is not prohibited. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, so the request is prohibited.

items.case: On 10 May 2024, Vertex Dynamics detected a third-party vendor incident affecting 750 customer records. The team requested external legal counsel review on 10 May 2024. The decision on the request is made on 20 May 2024. Clause 4 was amended on 15 May 2024 to require review for incidents affecting more than 1000 customer records instead of 500.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request date version applies, triggering the lower threshold.
criteria.no: The decision date version applies, raising the threshold above the incident size.

items.rationale: Clause 4 governs the request. The pre-amendment text triggers review at >500 records. The post-amendment text triggers review at >1000 records. The incident involves 750 records. Under instruction A, the version on 10 May applies, so the lower threshold is met and the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the version on 20 May applies, so the threshold is not met and the request is not permitted.

title: Subcontractor Variation Policy
policy: 1. This Subcontractor Variation Policy, effective as of 1 January 2024, governs all modification requests submitted to Meridian Construction Group Ltd for active residential and commercial projects. 2. Subcontractors must submit written variation requests to assigned project manager Elena Ross detailing scope changes, cost adjustments, and material substitutions. Variation requests valued at $10,000 or less are automatically approved upon submission. 3. Variation requests are automatically approved if the subcontractor does not submit a revised project schedule alongside the cost adjustment. 4. The site supervisor shall withhold formal approval for five days following receipt of the submission to allow for internal review. 5. Approved variations become binding upon written confirmation from both parties. Payment for additional work will be processed within thirty days of milestone verification. 6. All modified work must comply with site safety protocols and hold valid insurance coverage matching the original contract value. Subcontractors must maintain current licensing throughout the project duration. 7. This policy supersedes prior verbal agreements and may be updated quarterly. Amendments take effect immediately upon publication on the company intranet.

items.case: Meridian Construction Group Ltd received a variation request from Delta Concrete Services on Friday, 15 March 2024. The site supervisor evaluated the submission on Thursday, 21 March 2024.
items.question: Is the variation request permitted to be approved on the evaluation date?

criteria.yes: The evaluation date falls after the required waiting period has elapsed.
criteria.no: The evaluation date falls before the required waiting period has elapsed.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires withholding approval for five days following receipt. Under instruction A (business days), only four business days (18–21 March) have passed, so approval is not yet permitted. Under instruction B (calendar days), six calendar days (16–21 March) have passed, satisfying the five-day requirement and permitting approval.

items.case: Apex Piping Solutions submitted a variation request on 10 March 2024 for a $12,000 cost adjustment. The submission included detailed scope changes and material substitution forms.
items.question: Is the variation request automatically approved?

criteria.yes: The request meets the condition for automatic approval regarding the project schedule.
criteria.no: The request fails to meet the condition for automatic approval regarding the project schedule.

items.rationale: Clause 3 states requests are automatically approved if no revised project schedule is submitted. The case does not establish whether a schedule was submitted. Under instruction A, the unproven condition is treated as not satisfied (no schedule submitted), triggering automatic approval. Under instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied (schedule submitted), negating automatic approval.

items.case: Summit Roofing Ltd submitted a variation request for $8,000 on 10 October 2024. The site supervisor made the final decision on 20 October 2024. The policy was amended on 15 October 2024, changing the automatic approval threshold from $10,000 to $5,000.
items.question: Is the variation request automatically approved?

criteria.yes: The request amount falls within the automatic approval threshold of the applicable policy version.
criteria.no: The request amount exceeds the automatic approval threshold of the applicable policy version.

items.rationale: Clause 2 sets an automatic approval threshold. Under instruction A, the version in force on 10 October applies ($10,000 threshold), so the $8,000 request qualifies for automatic approval. Under instruction B, the version in force on 20 October applies ($5,000 threshold), so the $8,000 request exceeds the limit and is not automatically approved.

title: System Access Request Policy
policy:
1. All requests for access to Vertex Dynamics Ltd. production environments must be submitted via the internal service portal by the fifteenth of the preceding month. Late submissions are processed in the following cycle.
2. Junior analysts may request read-only access to customer databases upon approval by their direct manager. Access is automatically revoked after twelve months of inactivity.
3. Senior engineers may request administrative access to staging servers when assigned to deployment projects valued above forty thousand dollars. The project manager must attach a risk assessment form.
4. Access to financial reporting tools is granted to staff in the accounting department who have completed the data handling certification. Examples of qualifying tools include the quarterly ledger dashboard, the tax compliance portal, and the annual audit viewer.
5. Temporary elevated privileges may be issued for system maintenance, expiring automatically after seventy-two hours. Maintenance windows must be scheduled between midnight and four in the morning.
6. Requests for access to legacy archive systems must reference the specific project code and be countersigned by the department head. Archive access is restricted to historical data prior to 2020.

items.case: On 10 November 2023, Marcus Thorne submitted a request for administrative access to a staging server for a deployment project valued at fifty thousand dollars. The IT committee reviewed and decided on the request on 5 December 2023. An amendment to clause 3 took effect on 1 December 2023, raising the project value threshold to sixty thousand dollars.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Applying the policy version in force on 10 November 2023 applies the forty thousand dollar threshold, which the fifty thousand dollar project exceeds.
criteria.no: Applying the policy version in force on 5 December 2023 applies the amended sixty thousand dollar threshold, which the fifty thousand dollar project does not meet.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the November version applies; the project value meets clause 3, so it is permitted. Under instruction B, the December version applies; the project value falls below the amended threshold, so it is not permitted.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, Sarah Lin submitted a request for write access to the internal documentation repository. The repository stores technical manuals and onboarding guides. Her direct manager approved the request and submitted it on the same day.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all six clauses, and the instruction states that uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all six clauses, and the instruction states that uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: Clauses 1 through 6 govern production environments, customer databases, staging servers, financial tools, maintenance privileges, and legacy archives. None address internal documentation repositories. Under instruction A, the absence of a covering clause permits the request. Under instruction B, the absence of a covering clause prohibits it.

items.case: On 5 August 2024, David Chen submitted a request for access to the monthly revenue tracker. He works in the accounting department and holds a valid data handling certification. The tracker displays aggregated sales figures updated daily.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Treating the list in clause 4 as illustrative allows similar financial reporting tools like the monthly revenue tracker to qualify.
criteria.no: Treating the list in clause 4 as complete restricts qualification to only the three explicitly named tools, excluding the monthly revenue tracker.

items.rationale: Clause 4 grants access to accounting staff with certification and lists three tools as examples. Under instruction A, the list is complete; the tracker is not listed, so the request is not permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; the tracker is a similar financial reporting tool, so the request is permitted.

title: Oakridge University Grading Appeals Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs all formal requests by currently enrolled students to modify final course grades issued by faculty members at Oakridge University.
2. A grading appeal must be submitted to the Academic Review Board within 10 days of the official grade posting date. Late submissions will not be processed under any circumstances.
3. To be considered valid, an appeal must include a signed appeal form and a written justification of at least 500 words detailing the specific grading error or calculation discrepancy.
4. The Academic Review Board may approve a grade adjustment of up to 5 percentage points per course. Adjustments exceeding this limit require separate dean approval and a supplementary financial impact statement.
5. This policy was amended on November 15, 2023. Clause 4 is revised to state that the Academic Review Board may approve a grade adjustment of up to 10 percentage points per course without requiring separate dean approval or a supplementary statement. All other clauses remain unchanged.
6. Decisions on appeals are final and will be communicated to the student and the relevant department head within thirty days of the Board meeting.

items.case: Elena Rostova received her final grade on Monday, October 2, 2023. She submitted her appeal on Friday, October 13, 2023.
items.question: Is the appeal submission timely?

criteria.yes: Submission falls within the 10-day limit when weekends are excluded.
criteria.no: Submission exceeds the 10-day limit when weekends are included.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires submission within 10 days. Counting business days excludes the two weekend days between October 2 and October 13, resulting in 9 elapsed days, which is within the limit. Counting calendar days includes those weekend days, resulting in 11 elapsed days, which exceeds the limit.

items.case: Marcus Chen submitted a signed appeal form for his History 201 grade on October 10, 2023. His appeal packet included a detailed essay explaining the professor's miscalculation of his midterm scores.
items.question: Does the appeal meet the validity requirements?

criteria.yes: All stated requirements are met, and the unstated word count threshold is treated as satisfied.
criteria.no: The unstated word count threshold is treated as not satisfied, failing the validity requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires a signed form and a justification of at least 500 words. The case confirms the signed form and mentions an essay, but does not establish the essay's length. Treating the unproven length as not satisfied fails Clause 3. Treating it as satisfied meets Clause 3.

items.case: Sarah Jenkins requested a grade adjustment of 8 percentage points for her Chemistry 101 course on November 10, 2023. The Academic Review Board issued its final decision on November 20, 2023.
items.question: Is the requested adjustment permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The amended limit of 10 percentage points applies, covering the 8-point request.
criteria.no: The original limit of 5 percentage points applies, excluding the 8-point request.

items.rationale: Clause 4 originally capped adjustments at 5 points. Clause 5 records an amendment effective November 15, 2023, raising the cap to 10 points. Applying the policy as of the November 10 request date enforces the 5-point cap, rejecting the 8-point request. Applying it as of the November 20 decision date enforces the 10-point cap, permitting the request.

title: Oakridge Municipal District Permit Administration Guidelines
policy:
1. Effective March 1, 2024, all permit applications for the Oakridge Municipal District must be submitted electronically through the central portal by 5:00 PM on the day of filing. Late submissions are queued for the next business cycle.
2. Applications requesting structural modifications to existing buildings must include a certified engineering report, proof of zoning compliance, and a valid contractor license number.
3. Boundary fences in residential zones are strictly limited to a maximum height of 1.5 meters to preserve sightlines and neighborhood character. Exceeding this limit requires a formal hearing.
4. Fences enclosing swimming pools or recreational water features in residential zones may be constructed up to a maximum height of 2.0 meters, subject to standard safety inspections and quarterly maintenance logs.
5. Standard permits are granted upon receipt of a complete application and required documentation, provided that no variance request is attached to the submission. Attachments containing variance requests route automatically to the appeals committee.
6. All permit applications must be submitted for review within 10 days of the initial site inspection conducted by District Inspector Elena Rostova. Inspections are scheduled upon receipt of a preliminary inquiry form.

items.case: District Inspector Elena Rostova completed the initial site inspection for the Maple Street development on Monday, November 4. Developer Marcus Chen submitted the electronic permit application on Friday, November 15.
items.question: Is the application timely under the policy?

criteria.yes: Submission falls within the 10-day window when counted in business days.
criteria.no: Submission exceeds the 10-day window when counted in calendar days.

items.rationale: Clause 6 requires submission within 10 days of inspection. Instruction A counts business days (Nov 5 through Nov 15 is exactly 10 days), satisfying the deadline. Instruction B counts calendar days (Nov 5 through Nov 14 is 10 days), making Nov 15 the 11th day and missing the deadline.

items.case: Landowner Sarah Jenkins requests a permit to install a two-meter wooden fence enclosing a residential swimming pool in the Oakridge residential zone.
items.question: Is the permit request approved under the policy?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause for pool fences allows up to two meters.
criteria.no: The stricter general clause for residential fences limits height to 1.5 meters.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 4 both apply but set different height limits. Instruction A applies the stricter clause (Clause 3, 1.5m limit), denying the two-meter request. Instruction B applies the more specific clause (Clause 4, pool fences up to 2.0m), approving the request.

items.case: Contractor David Lin submits a complete application with proof of zoning compliance for a standard residential permit. The submission does not mention whether a variance request is included or excluded.
items.question: Is the permit granted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The missing variance request is treated as absent, satisfying the condition for standard grant.
criteria.no: The missing variance request is treated as present, violating the condition for standard grant.

items.rationale: Clause 5 grants standard permits provided no variance request is attached. Instruction A treats the unstated condition as not satisfied (no variance attached), meeting the grant requirement. Instruction B treats the unstated condition as satisfied (variance attached), triggering the denial pathway.

title: Aetheria Airways Disruption Compensation Policy
policy:
1. Aetheria Airways compensates passengers for flight disruptions occurring on or after 1 January 2024, provided the passenger holds a confirmed ticket issued under fare class Y or B and the disruption was not caused by passenger misconduct or voluntary travel changes.
2. Eligible disruption causes include severe weather, air traffic control strikes, and mechanical failures.
3. Any compensation request submitted within 60 days of the scheduled departure is permitted up to €600.
4. Requests concerning mechanical failures that exceed €350 are denied.
5. All claims must be submitted in writing to the Disruptions Office and include the booking reference, flight number, date of travel, and a brief description of the delay. Supporting documentation such as boarding passes or hotel receipts may be attached but are not mandatory for initial review.
6. The Disruptions Office will process valid claims within fifteen business days and issue payments via the original booking method or direct bank transfer upon written request. Partial approvals will be issued if only some criteria are met.
7. Final decisions on compensation amounts are binding and non-negotiable once communicated to the claimant. Disputes may be reviewed only if new factual evidence emerges within ninety days of the decision.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, passenger Leo Vance booked flight AA-882 in fare class Y. The flight was cancelled due to an airport security lockdown. Vance submitted a written claim for €400 on 5 April 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats the list in clause 2 as illustrative, so the airport security lockdown qualifies as a similar eligible cause.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the list in clause 2 as complete, so the airport security lockdown does not qualify as an eligible cause.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists eligible causes without specifying exhaustiveness. Instruction A closes the list, excluding the lockdown and denying the request. Instruction B opens the list, allowing similar disruptions and permitting the request.

items.case: On 20 May 2024, passenger Nina Torres booked flight AA-104 in fare class B. The flight was delayed due to a mechanical failure. Torres submitted a written claim for €450 on 30 June 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Instruction A applies the stricter clause 3, which permits requests within 60 days up to €600, overriding the denial in clause 4.
criteria.no: Instruction B applies the more specific clause 4, which denies mechanical failure claims over €350, overriding the permission in clause 3.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 4 conflict for this case. Clause 3 is stricter (broad time and amount limit permitting the claim) while clause 4 is more specific (narrow cause and amount limit denying it). Instruction A selects the stricter rule, permitting the claim. Instruction B selects the more specific rule, denying it.

items.case: On 8 July 2024, passenger Omar Diaz booked flight AA-221 in fare class M. The flight was delayed due to severe weather. Diaz submitted a written claim for €200 on 10 July 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Instruction A permits requests that fall outside all policy clauses, and clause 1's fare class restriction excludes this claim from coverage.
criteria.no: Instruction B denies requests that fall outside all policy clauses, and clause 1's fare class restriction excludes this claim from coverage.

items.rationale: Clause 1 limits eligibility to fare classes Y or B, leaving this fare class M claim uncovered by any clause. Instruction A defaults to permitting uncovered requests. Instruction B defaults to denying them.

title: Meridian Health Partners Clinical Scheduling Directive
policy:
Meridian Health Partners Clinical Scheduling Directive
1. Standard appointment bookings for outpatient procedures must be entered into the central registry no fewer than five business days prior to the scheduled date, with all insurance pre-authorizations attached.
2. Priority rescheduling of a confirmed patient slot is prohibited if the patient has previously cancelled two appointments within the same calendar quarter.
3. Schedule adjustments without administrative penalty are permitted when the delay stems from physician illness, facility maintenance, or supply shortages, provided the registry is updated within two hours of the incident.
4. Conversion of an in-person appointment to a telehealth visit is authorized for follow-up consultations, medication reviews, and chronic disease management sessions, and requires a functioning secure video platform.
5. Any modification requested less than forty-eight hours before the procedure time must be approved by the department scheduling coordinator and logged with a reason code.
6. Weekend and evening clinic hours operate under a reduced staffing model and cannot accommodate initial diagnostic imaging or surgical pre-admissions for attending physicians, regardless of patient preference.
7. All schedule changes involving anesthesia services must be coordinated through the perioperative office forty-eight hours in advance to ensure staff availability, with a $150 coordination fee waived for emergencies before March 31, 2025.

items.case: Dr. Evans requests priority rescheduling of a confirmed MRI slot for patient Maria Lin to an earlier date due to a sudden work conflict. Patient Lin previously cancelled one routine blood draw appointment in October.
items.question: Is the priority rescheduling permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated condition of cancelling two appointments is treated as not satisfied, so the prohibition in clause 2 does not apply.
criteria.no: The unstated condition of cancelling two appointments is treated as satisfied, triggering the prohibition in clause 2.

items.rationale: Clause 2 prohibits priority rescheduling if the patient cancelled two appointments in a quarter. The case establishes only one cancellation, leaving the two-cancellation threshold unstated. Under instruction A, the unstated condition is not satisfied, so the prohibition fails and rescheduling is permitted. Under instruction B, the unstated condition is satisfied, triggering the prohibition and denying permission.

items.case: Nurse Sarah Chen requests to convert an in-person appointment for patient David Ross to a telehealth visit to discuss his post-operative wound healing progress. The clinic's secure video platform is operational.
items.question: Is the telehealth conversion denied?

criteria.yes: The list in clause 4 is treated as complete, so the unlisted post-operative discussion does not qualify for conversion.
criteria.no: The list in clause 4 is treated as illustrative, so the similar post-operative discussion qualifies for conversion.

items.rationale: Clause 4 authorizes telehealth conversion for follow-up consultations, medication reviews, and chronic disease management. The case involves post-operative wound discussion, which is not listed but clinically similar. Under instruction A, the list is complete, so the request falls outside authorization and is denied. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the similar item qualifies and the request is not denied.

items.case: Nurse practitioner James Wright requests to schedule an initial diagnostic ultrasound for patient Elena Rodriguez on a Saturday morning at 9:00 AM under his direct supervision.
items.question: Is the scheduling request prohibited?

criteria.yes: No clause covers the request, and under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted.
criteria.no: No clause covers the request, and under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted.

items.rationale: The request involves an NP-led weekend diagnostic ultrasound. Clause 6 restricts weekend imaging for attending physicians, but no clause addresses nurse practitioners. The request falls outside all clauses. Under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted, so it is not prohibited. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, so it is prohibited.

title: GlobalSync Support Escalation Protocol
policy:
1. All customer support escalations must be formally logged in the central ticketing system within four hours of initial contact with the client.
2. Any escalation involving system downtime exceeding two hours requires approval from the Vice President of Operations.
3. Escalations concerning software license renewals, subscription tier downgrades exceeding $500, or payment gateway failures must be authorized by the Account Billing Supervisor.
4. Escalations concerning API gateway failures for Enterprise-tier accounts require approval from the Regional Support Manager.
5. Requests related to scheduled service delivery delays, freight logistics coordination, or warehouse dispatch errors require sign-off from the Operations Director.

title: Oakridge Municipal Temporary Structure Permit Policy
policy:
1. The Oakridge Municipal Permits Division administers temporary event structure permits for all commercial activities within city boundaries. Applications must be filed prior to any on-site assembly.
2. To qualify for approval, applicants must submit a detailed site plan, proof of liability insurance with a minimum coverage of $500,000, and a signed structural safety report from a licensed structural engineer. The Division requires all three documents to grant a permit.
3. Following submission, the Division has 10 days to issue a written determination. If a determination is not issued within this window, the applicant may begin assembly while awaiting final authorization.
4. The base permit fee is $350. Submissions received after the 15th of any calendar month are subject to an additional $75 administrative surcharge.
5. This policy took effect on January 10, 2023. On June 1, 2024, the Division amended Clause 2 to require that structural safety reports be signed by a certified fire marshal rather than a licensed structural engineer.
6. Permits are issued only when the application satisfies all documentary requirements under the relevant policy version and the correct fee is remitted.

title: Aeris Airways Disruption Compensation Policy
policy:
1. Aeris Airways compensates passengers for flight disruptions resulting in a delay of three hours or more at the final destination, or for cancellations confirmed within forty-eight hours of scheduled departure. Eligibility requires that the passenger held a confirmed ticket in their own name and completed check-in procedures prior to the airline’s stated deadline.
2. Compensation is calculated based on flight distance. For journeys under 1,500 kilometres, the entitlement is €400. For intra-Union flights exceeding 1,500 kilometres, and for other flights between 1,500 and 3,500 kilometres, the entitlement is €600. For flights exceeding 3,500 kilometres, the entitlement is €800. Amounts are prorated by fifty percent if the passenger is re-routed and arrives within two hours of the original arrival time.
3. No compensation is payable for disruptions arising from extraordinary circumstances beyond the carrier’s reasonable control, such as severe weather patterns, volcanic ash clouds, sudden air traffic control restrictions, or unlawful interference.
4. Claims must be submitted in writing to Compliance Officer Sarah Lin within six months of the disruption date. Aeris Airways will process complete submissions within thirty calendar days and remit payment via the original payment method or bank transfer.
5. This policy supersedes all prior terms regarding disruption compensation and applies to all scheduled passenger flights operated or wet-leased by Aeris Airways.

items.case: Passenger Lena Rostova booked flight AE402 from Berlin to Rome on 12 November 2023. The flight was cancelled on 10 November 2023. Lena holds a confirmed ticket in her own name. She requests €600 compensation.
items.question: Is the passenger eligible for compensation under the policy?

criteria.yes: The uncontradicted check-in requirement is treated as satisfied, meeting all eligibility conditions.
criteria.no: The unestablished check-in requirement is treated as not satisfied, failing eligibility.

items.rationale: Clause 1 requires completed check-in procedures. The case does not state whether Lena checked in. Under instruction A, this unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, so eligibility fails (no). Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, so all requirements are met (yes).

criteria.no: The exclusion list is treated as non-exhaustive, so the bird strike is covered by the exclusion.

Under instruction A, the list is complete, so only the listed events exclude compensation, making the claim payable (yes). Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, extending the exclusion to similar uncontrollable events, barring compensation (no).

criteria.no: The post-amendment version applies, setting the short-haul cap at €200, which excludes the €300 request.

Under instruction B, the version effective on the decision date (15 March) applies, capping payment at €200, so the request is not payable (no).

title: Aethelgard Hospitality Group Reservation Guidelines
policy:
1. All room reservations must be secured with a valid credit card and a refundable deposit equal to the first night’s rate. Identification must be presented at check-in, and the primary guest must be present upon arrival.
2. Cancellation fees are waived when the guest provides documented proof of a medical emergency, severe weather disruption, or documented flight cancellation.
3. Reservations made on or after 1 March 2024 are subject to a non-refundable administrative charge of £25. Effective 15 July 2024, this charge is increased to £50 for all new bookings.
4. Any reservation comprising five or more rooms must be paid in full at the time of booking.
5. Reservations submitted under the corporate account of Vertex Solutions Ltd are subject to a net-30 payment term and require only a 40% deposit upon confirmation.
6. Guests requesting late checkout beyond 12:00 must arrange it with the front desk and may be charged an additional fee based on availability. All modifications to existing bookings must be confirmed in writing by the reservations manager.

title: Data Retention and Access Policy for Veridian Analytics Ltd
policy:
This policy establishes retention periods and access conditions for core business records. Requests falling outside these parameters require separate executive review.
1. Veridian Analytics Ltd retains employee performance evaluations for three years from the date of the final review. Access requests for these evaluations are permitted only if submitted within the first eighteen months of the retention period.
2. Client financial transaction logs are stored for five years from the date of the transaction. Requests to access logs that are older than four years require written authorization from the Chief Financial Officer and are otherwise denied.
3. Marketing engagement data is maintained for ninety days following the last recorded user interaction. Export requests for this data are permitted provided the request is logged prior to the expiration of the ninety-day window.
4. Records generated during regulatory compliance audits are retained without a fixed expiration date. Internal staff members may access audit records upon completion of the standard internal request form.
5. Personal health information submitted by external contractors is securely deleted after two years from the submission date. Retrieval requests for this information are permitted only when accompanied by a signed declaration of medical necessity from a licensed practitioner.

items.case: On January 1, 2024, a client's last marketing interaction was recorded. On March 15, 2024, a marketing analyst submitted a request to export the associated engagement data. criteria.no: The post-amendment version of clause 3 applies, and the request falls outside the revised thirty-day window.

Under instruction B, the version in force on April 10 applies, denying permission because the request falls outside the amended thirty-day window.

title: GreenHorizon Volunteers Reimbursement and Equipment Policy
policy:
1. GreenHorizon Volunteers (GHV) coordinates community environmental projects. All registered participants must comply with this reimbursement and equipment policy when undertaking assigned fieldwork.
2. Volunteers may submit claims for out-of-pocket costs directly incurred during approved activities. Acceptable expenses include transportation fares, protective gloves, reusable water bottles, and high-visibility vests.
3. Any single claim exceeding $150 requires prior written authorisation from the Regional Coordinator. Claims submitted above the threshold without prior authorisation are automatically declined.
4. Claims must be filed within thirty days of the expense date. Late submissions are declined unless a written extension was granted before the original deadline expired.
5. Approved reimbursements are disbursed via direct deposit on the last working day of the month following final approval. GHV reserves the right to request original receipts for any submitted claim.
6. All borrowed safety equipment must be returned in clean condition within seven days of project completion. Failure to return items results in a deduction from pending reimbursements.
[Effective 1 January 2024. Amended 12 April 2024: Clause 3 threshold changed to $100.]

items.case: On 5 February 2024, volunteer Elias Vance purchased a pair of steel-toed work boots for $85 to comply with site safety requirements for the riverbank cleanup. He submitted the claim on 10 February 2024.

criteria.no: The boots are not explicitly named in the list of acceptable expenses, which is treated as exhaustive.

criteria.no: The threshold was $100 when the decision was made, so the $120 claim exceeds it and lacks required authorisation.

Instruction B applies the version effective on 15 April, after the 12 April amendment lowered the threshold to $100; the claim now exceeds the limit without authorisation and is declined.

Instruction B mandates counting calendar days; thirty calendar days from 1 June 2024 expires on 1 July 2024, and under this counting method the submission is deemed within the window, yielding yes.

title: Greenfield Community Aid Volunteer Policy
policy:
1. All volunteers must complete the mandatory onboarding module before participating in any field activities. Completion must be verified by the Program Coordinator within the organisation’s volunteer management system.
2. Volunteers are expected to maintain consistent attendance. Any absence from a scheduled shift requires advance notice to the site supervisor. Cancellation requests must be submitted at least 3 days before the scheduled shift to allow for roster adjustments.
3. The organisation provides necessary equipment and protective gear for all approved roles. Volunteers must inspect issued items prior to each shift and report any damage or defects immediately. Personal equipment may be used only if it meets the safety standards outlined in the role handbook.
4. Reimbursement shall not be granted for personal leisure expenses, such as gym memberships and video game purchases. All other travel and incident costs must be submitted with original receipts and approved by the Finance Officer.
5. Volunteers may not receive any direct payment or cash compensation for services rendered to the organisation. This restriction applies to all roles, including administrative support, event coordination, and field operations.
6. Volunteers assigned to the Summer Youth Mentorship program may receive a travel stipend up to $150 per quarter to cover transit costs. Stipend eligibility requires a minimum of twenty service hours in the preceding quarter and written approval from the Mentorship Director.
7. Any volunteer who accumulates three unexcused absences within a rolling twelve-month period will be temporarily suspended from active duty. Reactivation requires a meeting with the Volunteer Manager and a signed commitment to the attendance guidelines.

criteria.no: The stricter clause prohibiting all direct payment overrides the specific program allowance.

criteria.no: The example list is treated as illustrative, so similar leisure items are also banned.

Under instruction A, the list is complete, so only those exact items are excluded; the streaming subscription is allowed. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so functionally similar leisure subscriptions are also excluded.

items.case: Volunteer Sarah Jenkins requests to cancel her scheduled shift on Monday, April 15. She submits the cancellation request on Friday, April 12 at 16:00.

Under instruction B, counting calendar days includes Friday, Saturday, and Sunday (3 days), which satisfies the requirement.

title: Vanguard Logistics Ltd. Preventive Maintenance and Repair Authorization Policy
policy:
1. All scheduled preventive maintenance for fleet vehicles and warehouse machinery must be submitted to the Maintenance Coordinator at least 10 days before the proposed service date.
2. Emergency repairs exceeding $1,500 require prior written approval from the Site Manager, while routine repairs under this threshold may be processed directly by the assigned technician.
3. Equipment that has been idle for more than 90 days must undergo a full safety inspection before returning to active service, regardless of its last maintenance record.
4. Requests submitted on or after the 25th of any month will be queued for the following month's service cycle unless classified as critical safety hazards.
5. All maintenance work on warehouse conveyors requires prior written approval from the Operations Director.
6. Emergency repairs on conveyor model CK-900 may proceed immediately without prior written approval.
7. Technicians must complete a post-service report within 3 days of job completion, detailing parts replaced and labour hours expended.
8. This policy supersedes all previous maintenance guidelines issued prior to January 1, 2024, and remains in effect until formally revised by the Operations Director.

title: Aethelgard Systems Information Security Incident Management Policy
policy:
1. Effective as of January 10, 2023, this policy applies to all personnel and contractors at Aethelgard Systems regarding the management of information security incidents. An incident is defined as any confirmed or suspected unauthorized access, use, disclosure, or destruction of company information assets.
2. All incidents must be reported to the Central Security Office within four days of initial detection. Reports must include the detection timestamp, affected systems, and a preliminary impact assessment. Failure to report within the specified timeframe constitutes a procedural violation unless documented force majeure applies.
3. Incidents involving the compromise of sensitive assets, such as customer databases, financial ledgers, and employee health records, require immediate escalation to the Board of Directors. The escalation must occur before any containment actions are initiated, and the Chief Information Security Officer must acknowledge receipt within one hour.
4. The incident response team may proceed with system restoration and service resumption without executive approval if the breach involves only internal documents, affects fewer than five hundred users, and the data has not been exfiltrated. Any deviation from these conditions mandates written authorization from the Vice President of Operations.
5. All incident records, communications, and resolution reports must be archived in the secure compliance repository for a minimum of seven years. Access to archived records is restricted to the audit committee and designated legal counsel. Incidents requiring remediation costs above $25,000 must be logged with the finance department.

items.case: On November 12, a server containing internal HR policy drafts was accessed by an unauthorized vendor. The incident affected three hundred employees. The case file does not state whether any data was copied or transferred outside the network.
items.question: Is executive approval required before system restoration?

criteria.yes: Under instruction A, the unstated exfiltration condition is treated as not satisfied, so the exemption fails and approval is required.
criteria.no: Under instruction B, the unstated exfiltration condition is treated as satisfied, so the exemption applies and approval is not required.

items.rationale: The policy permits restoration without approval only if three conditions are met. The case establishes two but leaves data exfiltration unstated. Instruction A treats the unproven condition as false, failing the exemption and requiring approval. Instruction B treats it as true, satisfying the exemption and waiving approval.

items.case: Initial detection of a phishing campaign occurred on Friday, March 8. The security team submitted the formal incident report to the Central Security Office on Wednesday, March 13.
items.question: Is the report timely?

criteria.no: Counting calendar days, the report exceeds the four-day limit.

items.rationale: The policy mandates reporting within four days. From March 8 to March 13 spans four business days (Friday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday) but five calendar days. Instruction A counts business days, making it timely. Instruction B counts calendar days, making it late.

items.case: On April 10, a server containing proprietary source code for the company's flagship product was accessed by an unauthorized third party.
items.question: Can the incident be handled at the department level without Board escalation?

criteria.yes: Treating the list as complete, source code is not listed, so Board escalation is not required.
criteria.no: Treating the list as illustrative, source code qualifies as a sensitive asset, mandating Board escalation.

items.rationale: The policy requires Board escalation for sensitive assets, listing specific examples. The case involves proprietary source code, which is not listed but is similar. Instruction A treats the list as exhaustive, so escalation is not required and department-level handling is permitted. Instruction B treats the list as non-exhaustive, so escalation is required and department-level handling is prohibited.

title: Greenleaf Culinary Solutions Food Safety & Operations Policy
policy:
1. All personnel at Greenleaf Culinary Solutions must adhere to these food safety protocols to ensure consistent compliance with municipal health regulations.
2. Perishable ingredients must be maintained at or below 4°C at all times. If a refrigeration failure causes the internal temperature to exceed 4°C for more than 5 days, the affected inventory must be immediately quarantined and destroyed.
3. Onboarding a new ingredient supplier requires formal authorization from Quality Director Elena Rossi. To process an authorization request, the applicant must submit a current sanitation audit report, a detailed product specification sheet, and a signed liability waiver.
4. Customer complaints alleging foodborne illness or contamination must be entered into the central tracking system within 48 hours of receipt. The regional manager must be notified via email on the same day the complaint is logged.
5. All commercial cold-storage units must receive certified professional maintenance every six months. Maintenance logs must be uploaded to the facility management portal within three days of service completion.
6. Any operational deviation from these standards requires advance written approval from the site director. Unauthorized deviations will result in immediate suspension of the responsible shift.

items.case: On Friday, November 1, a refrigeration unit in Sector 4 failed, raising the internal temperature to 6°C. The unit was repaired on Wednesday, November 6, bringing the temperature back to 2°C. The batch contains 150 kg of fresh salmon. The shift supervisor requested to keep the salmon for service.
items.question: Must the affected inventory be destroyed?

criteria.yes: The temperature exceeded 4°C for a duration that surpasses the five-day threshold defined in clause 2.
criteria.no: The temperature exceeded 4°C for a duration that does not surpass the five-day threshold defined in clause 2.

title: Oakridge Municipal Permits Division: Temporary Sidewalk Work Guidelines
policy:
1. All contractors requesting temporary sidewalk encroachment for construction or utility work must submit Form 7B to the Oakridge Municipal Permits Division at least five days before the proposed start date. A processing fee of $150 applies to each submission, payable by certified check or municipal credit account.
2. No permit may authorize continuous work exceeding fourteen days without prior written approval from the City Council. Extensions beyond this limit require a separate variance application and an additional $75 administrative surcharge.
3. Permits designated for underground electrical conduit installation may extend up to twenty-one days, provided the applicant submits a certified traffic management plan alongside the initial request. This allowance covers trenching, laying, and backfilling operations.
4. Work must cease immediately upon permit expiration. Any remaining materials, equipment, or debris stored on the public right-of-way after expiration will be removed at the contractor’s expense, billed at $120 per hour.
5. Permits are non-transferable and valid only for the address and project scope listed on the approved certificate. Subcontractors must be listed on the original application to operate under the permit, and all personnel must display the permit number visibly on site. This policy takes effect on January 15, 2024.

items.case: Contractor Lena Rostova applies for a temporary sidewalk permit to install underground electrical conduit at 420 Maple Street. The approved work schedule runs from June 10 to June 27, totaling eighteen days. A certified traffic management plan is attached to the submission.
items.question: Is the eighteen-day permit request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governs, allowing up to twenty-one days for electrical conduit work.
criteria.no: The stricter clause governs, limiting all permits to fourteen days.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, clause 2’s fourteen-day limit prevails as stricter, rejecting the eighteen-day request. Under instruction B, clause 3’s twenty-one-day allowance prevails as more specific to electrical conduit, approving the request.

items.case: Vendor Marcus Chen requests a temporary sidewalk encroachment permit to operate a seasonal holiday gift kiosk at 108 Pine Avenue. The kiosk will occupy a four-meter square section of the pavement from December 1 to December 20. No excavation or trenching is involved.
items.question: Is the kiosk encroachment request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and instruction B applies, resulting in a yes answer.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and instruction A applies, resulting in a no answer.

items.rationale: The request involves a retail kiosk rather than construction or utility work, placing it outside every clause. Under instruction A, the uncovered status yields a no answer. Under instruction B, the uncovered status yields a yes answer.

items.case: Applicant David Lin submits Form 7B on Friday, March 1. The proposed start date for the sidewalk work is Thursday, March 7. The application includes all required fees and documentation.
items.question: Is the submission timely and permitted?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days meets the five-day requirement.
criteria.no: Counting business days fails the five-day requirement.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, counting business days yields only three days between submission and start, missing the five-day requirement. Under instruction B, counting calendar days yields exactly five days, satisfying the requirement.

title: Apex Logistics Warehouse Operations Policy
policy:
1. All Apex Logistics personnel entering the loading bay must wear high-visibility vests and steel-toed boots. Supervisors will verify compliance during morning briefings and document any violations in the safety log.
2. Pallet jacks may only be operated by staff who have completed the quarterly safety certification. Uncertified staff must request temporary authorization from the floor manager and work under direct supervision.
3. Temperature-controlled storage is restricted to pharmaceuticals and perishable foods. Items outside these categories must be stored in ambient zones to prevent cross-contamination and preserve climate control efficiency.
4. Bay 7 shelving may only be used for storage loads not exceeding 1,500 kg. Exceeding this limit requires engineering approval and structural reinforcement before any goods are placed on the racks.
5. No forklift may be used to move pallets weighing over 800 kg on the upper mezzanine. Violations will result in immediate suspension of operating privileges pending a safety review.
6. Forklifts equipped with hydraulic stabilizers may move pallets up to 1,000 kg on the upper mezzanine. Operators must log each movement in the digital tracking system and verify floor load ratings beforehand.
7. All hazardous material containers must be double-bagged and labeled with the supplier’s original MSDS sheet. Secondary containment trays are mandatory for liquids to prevent spillage during transit.
8. Inventory audits must be completed before 17:00 on the last Friday of each month. Delays require written justification submitted to the operations director within twenty-four hours.

items.case: On 12 June 2024, Picker Elena Rostova requested authorization to store 1,800 kg of bulk chemicals on Bay 7 shelving. The request was adjudicated on 10 August 2024. The warehouse policy regarding Bay 7 weight limits was amended effective 1 July 2024, reducing the maximum load from 2,000 kg to 1,500 kg.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The original policy version applies, setting the Bay 7 limit at 2,000 kg, which accommodates the 1,800 kg load.
criteria.no: The amended policy version applies, setting the Bay 7 limit at 1,500 kg, which the 1,800 kg load exceeds.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the version in force on the request date applies. That version permitted loads up to 2,000 kg, so the 1,800 kg request is allowed. Under instruction B, the version in force on the decision date applies. That version lowered the limit to 1,500 kg, so the request is denied.

items.case: On 5 September 2024, Logistics Coordinator Marcus Thorne requested permission to store cryogenic medical research samples in the temperature-controlled cold room. The samples require maintenance at -150°C and are classified as laboratory reagents rather than pharmaceuticals or perishables.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all policy clauses. Instruction B dictates the outcome for uncovered requests.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all policy clauses. Instruction A dictates the outcome for uncovered requests.

items.rationale: Clause 3 restricts temperature-controlled storage to pharmaceuticals and perishable foods. Cryogenic research samples fall outside this scope, and no other clause addresses them. Under instruction A, the rule for uncovered requests yields a negative outcome. Under instruction B, the rule for uncovered requests yields a positive outcome.

items.case: On 20 October 2024, Warehouse Lead Sarah Chen requested authorization to move a 900 kg pallet of industrial bearings on the upper mezzanine using a forklift fitted with hydraulic stabilizers.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 6 applies as it specifically addresses forklifts with hydraulic stabilizers and permits loads up to 1,000 kg. Under instruction B, the more specific clause prevails.
criteria.no: Clause 5 applies as it broadly prohibits forklift movement of pallets over 800 kg on the mezzanine. Under instruction A, the stricter clause prevails.

items.rationale: Clauses 5 and 6 both apply. Clause 5 broadly prohibits forklift movement of pallets over 800 kg, while Clause 6 specifically permits it up to 1,000 kg when hydraulic stabilizers are used. They conflict. Under instruction A, the stricter clause (5) prevails, resulting in denial. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (6) prevails, resulting in approval.

title: Oakridge Temporary Vending Permit Policy
policy:
1. The Oakridge Municipal Services Department issues temporary street vending permits for public events lasting up to seven consecutive days on municipal property.
2. Applicants must submit a completed Form 14-B to the planning office and pay a processing fee of $150 before the permit is activated.
3. Applications are denied if the proposed event overlaps with a scheduled municipal road closure.
4. Any permit application submitted less than ten days before the proposed start date will be denied.
5. Applications for seasonal markets operating during the summer festival period (June 1 to August 31) are exempt from the ten-day advance submission rule.
6. The department may revoke a permit if the holder fails to display the physical permit card at the primary stall location during operating hours.
7. All fees are non-refundable once the application is logged in the municipal system, regardless of approval status.

items.case: Elena Rostova submitted a vending application on July 20 for a three-day craft fair beginning July 25. She paid the $150 fee and submitted Form 14-B. The fair falls within the summer festival period.
items.question: Is the permit application approved?

criteria.yes: The summer festival exemption overrides the advance submission deadline.
criteria.no: The advance submission deadline triggers automatic denial.

items.rationale: Clause 4 denies applications submitted less than ten days prior, while Clause 5 exempts summer festival markets from this deadline. Under instruction A, the stricter denial clause prevails, resulting in rejection. Under instruction B, the more specific exemption clause prevails, resulting in approval.

items.case: Marcus Chen applied for a non-food retail stall permit for October 10 through October 14. He submitted Form 14-B and paid the $150 fee on September 1. The proposed location is in the downtown commercial district.
items.question: Is the permit application approved?

criteria.yes: The road closure condition is treated as unmet, so the denial trigger does not apply.
criteria.no: The road closure condition is treated as met, triggering automatic denial.

items.rationale: Clause 3 denies applications that overlap with a municipal road closure. The case neither confirms nor denies such an overlap. Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as unsatisfied, avoiding denial and resulting in approval. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, triggering denial.

items.case: Priya Sharma submitted a permit application on Friday, April 12 for a food service event starting Wednesday, April 24. She paid the $150 fee and submitted Form 14-B. The event does not overlap with any scheduled road closures.
items.question: Is the permit application approved?

criteria.yes: The period between submission and start date meets or exceeds the ten-day requirement when counted in calendar days.
criteria.no: The period between submission and start date falls short of the ten-day requirement when counted in business days.

items.rationale: Clause 4 denies applications submitted less than ten days before the start date. The policy does not specify how days are counted. From April 12 to April 24 is twelve calendar days but only seven business days. Under instruction A, counting business days yields a period under ten, triggering denial. Under instruction B, counting calendar days yields a period over ten, avoiding denial.

title: NovaTech Solutions Emergency Hotfix Deployment Protocol
policy:
1. This policy governs emergency hotfix deployments for NovaTech Solutions production environments. Only the Release Manager or a designated deputy may authorize a hotfix bypassing the standard quarterly release cycle.
2. Authorization requires a documented incident report submitted to the engineering director. A minimum of three days must elapse between the report submission and the deployment window to allow for stakeholder review. If the incident affects more than one thousand active users, this waiting period may be waived by the director.
3. Before deployment, the patch must undergo automated regression testing and manual validation on a staging server. The primary relational database must be fully backed up prior to execution. No production changes may occur during the maintenance window without explicit director sign-off.
4. Hotfixes apply to critical customer-facing services, such as the payment gateway, user authentication module, and inventory tracker. Any modification to internal administrative tools or legacy reporting dashboards requires standard release procedures.
5. Upon deployment, the engineering team must execute a rollback plan within one hour if critical errors emerge. A post-implementation review must be completed and archived in the internal repository within five days of the deployment date. Failure to archive the review suspends hotfix privileges for the responsible team for the remainder of the quarter.

items.case: Incident report #8842 regarding a checkout latency spike is submitted to the engineering director on Friday, November 10. Director Vance grants written approval on Monday, November 13. Automated regression tests complete successfully on Tuesday, November 14. The engineering team schedules the patch deployment for 2:00 PM on Tuesday, November 14.
items.question: Is the deployment permitted?

criteria.yes: Counting in calendar days yields four days between submission and deployment, satisfying the minimum period.
criteria.no: Counting in business days yields only two days between submission and deployment, failing the minimum period.

items.rationale: Instruction A counts the interval in business days, resulting in two days elapsed, which falls short of the three-day minimum. Instruction B counts in calendar days, resulting in four days elapsed, which meets the requirement.
