criteria.yes: Counting the period in business days yields 4 days, which meets the 4-day limit.
criteria.no: Counting the period in calendar days yields 5 days, which exceeds the 4-day limit.

items.rationale: The policy requires return within 4 days. From October 13 to October 18 spans 5 calendar days but only 4 business days (excluding Saturday and Sunday). Instruction A applies business day counting, keeping the return within the limit. Instruction B applies calendar day counting, pushing the return past the limit.

items.case: Driver Marcus Chen requests to use Vehicle 225 to transport a crate of office chairs and desks to a newly leased branch location. The request is submitted for official business use.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the official business use clause?

criteria.yes: Treating the listed examples as illustrative allows similar official tasks like transporting office furniture to qualify.
criteria.no: Treating the listed examples as complete restricts permission strictly to client meetings, site inspections, and equipment delivery, excluding furniture transport.

items.rationale: The policy lists specific examples of permitted official business. Transporting office furniture is not explicitly listed but is functionally similar to equipment delivery. Instruction A treats the list as exhaustive, denying the request. Instruction B treats the list as illustrative, permitting the request due to similarity.

title: Aethelgard Logistics Ltd. Building Access Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs entry to the Northside Distribution Centre for all employees, contractors, and visitors.
2. Standard access to the main warehouse and administrative offices is permitted Monday through Friday from 06:00 to 22:00, and Saturday from 08:00 to 18:00. Sundays are restricted to emergency personnel only.
3. Employees requiring access outside standard hours must submit a written request to the Facilities Manager at least twenty-four hours in advance. Requests must specify the exact dates, times, and operational reasons for the entry. The Facilities Manager will approve or deny the request within two business days.
4. All visitors must be escorted by an authorised employee at all times while on the premises. Visitors may not remain in the building after the escort departs. Unescorted individuals will be directed to the security desk for verification.
5. Proximity cards for standard access are issued free of charge to full-time staff upon completion of safety induction. Temporary cards for contractors cost fifteen dollars per day. Issuance requires that the contractor has no outstanding balance on file with Accounts Payable. Temporary cards must be returned within forty-eight hours of project completion.
6. Access privileges may be suspended immediately by the Site Director if safety protocols are breached or if an individual fails to return issued equipment. Written notice of suspension will be provided to the affected party.
7. This policy is reviewed annually and may be amended by the Executive Committee. Amendments take effect on the date published to the staff intranet. Previous versions are archived but no longer govern current operations.

items.case: Employee Linus Vance submitted a written request to the Facilities Manager at 09:00 on 10 May 2024 for warehouse access at 15:00 on 11 May 2024. The Facilities Manager rendered a decision on 11 May 2024. On 11 May 2024, the Executive Committee published an amendment changing the advance notice requirement to forty-eight hours.
items.question: Is the access request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The request was submitted thirty hours before the requested access time, satisfying the twenty-four-hour advance notice requirement in effect on the request date.
criteria.no: The request was submitted thirty hours before the requested access time, failing the forty-eight-hour advance notice requirement in effect on the decision date.

items.rationale: Under the version effective on 10 May, the twenty-four-hour notice requirement is met, so the request is permitted. Under the version effective on 11 May, the forty-eight-hour notice requirement is not met, so the request is not permitted.

items.case: Contractor Elena Rostova applied for a temporary proximity card on 3 June 2024 for a three-day equipment calibration project. She paid the required fee of forty-five dollars to the reception desk. The Security Office processed the application and issued the card on 4 June 2024.
items.question: Is the issuance of the temporary card permitted?

criteria.yes: The case establishes fee payment but does not establish an outstanding balance; treating the unestablished balance condition as not satisfied means no balance exists, satisfying the issuance requirement.
criteria.no: The case establishes fee payment but does not contradict an outstanding balance; treating the uncontradicted balance condition as satisfied means a balance exists, violating the issuance requirement.

items.rationale: The policy permits issuance only if the contractor has no outstanding balance. The case confirms payment but is silent on balance status. Under Instruction A, the unestablished balance condition is treated as not satisfied, clearing the path for issuance. Under Instruction B, the uncontradicted balance condition is treated as satisfied, triggering a prohibition on issuance.

items.case: Technician Marcus Hale requested access to the rooftop maintenance platform on 14 July 2024 to inspect solar panels during standard weekday hours. He submitted a written request to the Facilities Manager specifying dates, times, and operational reasons.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The policy regulates access to the main warehouse, administrative offices, and proximity cards, but contains no clause addressing rooftop maintenance platform access; the request falls outside the policy's scope.
criteria.no: The policy regulates access to the main warehouse, administrative offices, and proximity cards, but contains no clause addressing rooftop maintenance platform access; the request falls outside the policy's scope.

items.rationale: The policy governs standard and after-hours access to specific building areas and card issuance, but does not address the rooftop maintenance platform. Because no clause covers the request, Instruction A permits it, while Instruction B denies it.

title: NovaStream Technologies Release Management Policy
policy:
1. All software releases to production environments must follow the standard deployment pipeline, pass mandatory security scanning, and receive formal written approval prior to execution. Unapproved deployments will be automatically rolled back by the infrastructure team.
2. Any release affecting more than 5,000 concurrent users requires approval from the Chief Technology Officer. This threshold ensures adequate oversight for high-traffic modifications that impact core service availability.
3. Releases to the internal developer sandbox environment require approval from the DevOps Lead. Sandbox deployments are intended for experimental feature validation and do not expose customer data.
4. Automated regression testing may be bypassed for releases containing only configuration updates, documentation changes, or dependency version bumps. Teams must log the bypass reason in the release tracker for audit purposes.
5. Production releases must include a documented rollback plan detailing recovery steps and expected downtime. The rollback plan requirement was waived for releases tagged 'internal-tooling' effective 2024-09-01.
6. Release notes must be published to the central repository within four hours of deployment completion, listing all modified components and responsible engineers.

items.case: The Platform Engineering team submits a release to the internal developer sandbox environment that modifies the core authentication service, impacting 6,200 concurrent users. The release is approved solely by the Chief Technology Officer.
items.question: Is the release permitted?

criteria.yes: The stricter clause (Clause 2) applies, requiring CTO approval which was obtained.
criteria.no: The more specific clause (Clause 3) applies, requiring DevOps Lead approval which was not obtained.

items.rationale: Clause 2 (CTO approval for >5,000 users) is stricter than Clause 3 (DevOps Lead approval for sandbox). Clause 3 is more specific than Clause 2. Under Instruction A, the stricter requirement governs, making the CTO-approved release permitted. Under Instruction B, the more specific requirement governs, making the release impermissible without DevOps Lead sign-off.

items.case: The Frontend team prepares a release containing only environment variable modifications for the staging server. No automated regression tests are executed before deployment.
items.question: Is bypassing automated regression testing permitted?

criteria.yes: Environment variable modifications are treated as similar to configuration updates, qualifying for the bypass.
criteria.no: Environment variable modifications are not explicitly listed, so the bypass does not qualify.

items.rationale: Clause 4 lists configuration updates, documentation changes, and dependency version bumps. Environment variable modifications are not listed but are functionally similar to configuration updates. Instruction A treats the list as exhaustive, excluding the bypass. Instruction B treats the list as illustrative, allowing the bypass due to similarity.

items.case: A request to deploy the HR scheduling tool, tagged 'internal-tooling', is submitted on 2024-08-28. The request lacks a documented rollback plan. The deployment committee makes its decision on 2024-09-05.
items.question: Is the release permitted without a rollback plan?

criteria.yes: The policy version effective on the decision date includes the waiver for 'internal-tooling' releases.
criteria.no: The policy version effective on the request date does not include the waiver, requiring a rollback plan.

items.rationale: Clause 5 introduces a waiver for 'internal-tooling' releases effective 2024-09-01. The request was made before the amendment, and the decision was made after. Instruction A applies the pre-amendment version, requiring a plan. Instruction B applies the post-amendment version, granting the waiver.

title: Apex Structural Subcontractors Ltd Subcontracting Management Policy
policy:
1. All subcontracting work for Apex Structural Subcontractors Ltd must be initiated through a signed Work Order issued by Project Manager Elena Rostova. No verbal agreements, text messages, or informal email confirmations shall constitute a binding commitment for site labour, heavy machinery, or bulk material supply.
2. Requests for additional equipment rentals exceeding $5,000 require written authorisation from the Regional Director. Equipment requests for safety gear, temporary fencing, or standard scaffolding components under $5,000 may be approved directly by the Site Foreman.
3. Invoices submitted by subcontractors must reference the corresponding Work Order number and be delivered to the accounts office within 14 days of the completion date stated on the order. Late submissions will be processed in the next available payment cycle.
4. Any modification to the original scope of work must be documented on a Variation Form and signed by both parties before the altered work commences. Unauthorised variations will not be compensated.
5. Disputes regarding material quality or workmanship must be reported in writing within 5 days of discovery. The designated inspector will conduct a site assessment and issue a binding determination.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, Site Foreman Marcus Chen submitted a request to procure a commercial drone for aerial site surveying at a cost of $3,200. The drone is required for mapping the north boundary before foundation pouring begins.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside every policy clause, and the appended instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: The request falls outside every policy clause, and the appended instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The drone procurement request does not match the specific equipment categories or thresholds in Clause 2, nor does it fall under labour, machinery, invoices, variations, or disputes. It is therefore uncovered by the policy. Instruction A dictates that uncovered requests are permitted, but the correct answer is specified as 'no' per the prompt mapping, while Instruction B dictates they are not permitted, yielding 'yes'.

items.case: Work Order 442 stated a completion date of Friday, 12 April 2024. Subcontractor Greenfield Concrete delivered its invoice to the accounts office on Monday, 29 April 2024.
items.question: Is the invoice submission compliant with the policy?

criteria.yes: The elapsed period falls within the 14-day limit when counted using the method specified in the appended instruction.
criteria.no: The elapsed period exceeds the 14-day limit when counted using the method specified in the appended instruction.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires delivery within 14 days. Counting from 12 April to 29 April yields different totals depending on the counting method. Under Instruction A, the period is calculated in business days, which places the submission outside the allowable window. Under Instruction B, the period is calculated in calendar days, which places the submission inside the allowable window.

items.case: On 10 January 2024, Site Foreman Marcus Chen submitted a request to rent a mobile crane at a cost of $7,500. The request was reviewed and a decision was issued on 15 February 2024. The organisation amended Clause 2 on 20 January 2024, raising the authorisation threshold to $10,000.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The applicable policy version sets a threshold above $7,500, allowing direct Site Foreman approval.
criteria.no: The applicable policy version sets a threshold below $7,500, requiring Regional Director authorisation that was not obtained.

items.rationale: The request amount of $7,500 sits between the original $5,000 threshold and the amended $10,000 threshold. Instruction A requires applying the version in force on the request date (10 January), which uses the $5,000 limit, making the request non-compliant without higher approval. Instruction B requires applying the version in force on the decision date (15 February), which uses the $10,000 limit, making the request compliant under the Site Foreman's authority.

title: Veridian Solutions Professional Development Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. Purpose: This policy outlines the reimbursement framework for professional development expenses to support continuous skill enhancement across Veridian Solutions.
2. Eligibility: Full-time employees who have completed twelve consecutive months of service are eligible to apply. Part-time and contract staff are excluded from this program.
3. Covered Expenses: Reimbursement applies to educational activities directly aligned with the employee’s current job responsibilities. Qualifying items are accredited courses, industry certifications, and official textbooks.
4. Financial Limits: The maximum reimbursable amount is $2,500 per employee per calendar year. Expenses exceeding this threshold require executive sponsorship and are evaluated case-by-case.
5. Submission Requirements: All claims must be accompanied by original receipts and a certificate of completion. Employees must submit documentation within sixty days of the activity conclusion.
6. Processing Rules: All applicants must complete the annual compliance training. Completion restricts reimbursable activities to those lasting fewer than five days. Employees who have not completed the training may claim reimbursement for activities of any duration.
7. Policy Updates: Veridian Solutions reserves the right to modify benefit parameters. Updated versions are published on the internal portal without retroactive effect on pending applications.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, senior analyst Marcus Chen submitted a request for $1,800 to cover a data analytics program. The Finance Department issued its decision on May 20, 2024. On April 1, 2024, the organisation amended the policy, reducing the standard annual reimbursement limit from $2,500 to $1,500.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The March 12 policy version applies, setting the limit at $2,500, which covers the $1,800 request.
criteria.no: The May 20 policy version applies, setting the limit at $1,500, which excludes the $1,800 request.

items.rationale: The policy amendment on April 1 changed the annual limit. Applying the request-date version preserves the higher limit, permitting the claim. Applying the decision-date version enforces the lower limit, denying it.

items.case: On June 5, 2024, marketing coordinator Lisa Vance applied for $900 to cover a seven-day digital strategy program. She provided original receipts and a certificate of completion within the required timeframe. The Finance Department processed the claim on June 6, 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unproven compliance training condition is treated as not satisfied, triggering the exception that allows reimbursement for activities of any duration.
criteria.no: The unproven compliance training condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the restriction that limits reimbursement to activities lasting fewer than five days.

items.rationale: The case omits whether Lisa completed the mandatory training. Instruction A treats this as unmet, activating the any-duration rule and approving the seven-day program. Instruction B treats it as met, activating the under-five-days cap and rejecting it.

items.case: On August 10, 2024, software engineer David Park requested $600 for a two-day professional workshop on cloud architecture. He submitted valid receipts and proof of attendance within sixty days. The organisation’s current annual limit applies.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The workshop qualifies as similar to the listed examples, satisfying the coverage requirement.
criteria.no: The workshop is not explicitly listed in the policy, and the list is treated as exhaustive, failing the coverage requirement.

items.rationale: The policy lists courses, certifications, and textbooks. The case involves a workshop. Instruction A treats the list as complete, excluding the workshop. Instruction B treats it as illustrative, including the workshop by similarity.

title: Oakridge Academy Trust Admissions Policy
policy:
1. All applications for Year 7 entry must be submitted via the online portal by 31 March 2024. Late applications will not be processed.
2. Priority for admission is given to children of current staff members, provided the staff member has been employed continuously for at least two academic years prior to the application date. Employment records must be submitted with the application.
3. Siblings of currently enrolled pupils receive secondary priority, subject to available places after staff children are allocated.
4. A tuition fee waiver of 15 per cent is available for pupils from households receiving local authority free school meals, verified by a council letter dated within six months of the application. The waiver applies to the first term only.
5. Pupils admitted under clauses 2 or 3 may request a deferred start date for up to one term, subject to headteacher approval.
6. All admission decisions are final and communicated by 15 May 2024. Appeals must be lodged within ten working days of notification.
7. The discretionary bursary is denied to pupils who have previously attended a boarding school.

items.case: On 15 March 2024, Mr. Davies submits an application for his daughter to receive a 10 per cent academic merit scholarship for Year 7 entry. The family does not receive free school meals, and Mr. Davies is not a staff member. The application is complete and timely.
items.question: Is the scholarship request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request concerns an academic merit scholarship, which is not addressed by any clause, and the instruction states that uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: The request concerns an academic merit scholarship, which is not addressed by any clause, and the instruction states that uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: Clause 4 covers financial aid but only for free school meal recipients. No clause mentions merit scholarships. The instruction alone determines whether the gap in coverage results in permission or denial.

items.case: On 20 March 2024, Mrs. Chen applies for the discretionary bursary for her son's Year 7 entry. The application includes all required forms and a reference letter. The submission does not state whether the pupil has previously attended a boarding school.
items.question: Is the discretionary bursary granted?

criteria.yes: The policy denies the bursary only if the pupil attended a boarding school. Treating this unestablished condition as not satisfied means the denial condition fails, so the bursary is granted.
criteria.no: The policy denies the bursary only if the pupil attended a boarding school. Treating this unestablished condition as satisfied means the denial condition is met, so the bursary is not granted.

items.rationale: Clause 7 requires attendance at a boarding school to trigger denial. The case omits this fact. Instruction A treats the missing condition as false, avoiding denial. Instruction B treats it as true, triggering denial.

items.case: A parent submits an application on 28 March 2024. The admissions committee makes its decision on 10 April 2024. On 5 April 2024, the Trust amended Clause 1 to set the submission deadline at 20 March 2024. The application is complete and meets all other requirements.
items.question: Is the application processed?

criteria.yes: Applying the policy version on the request date shows the original 31 March deadline, making the 28 March submission timely and eligible for processing.
criteria.no: Applying the policy version on the decision date shows the amended 20 March deadline, making the 28 March submission late and ineligible for processing.

items.rationale: Clause 1 originally set a 31 March deadline. The amendment on 5 April changed it to 20 March. The instruction determines which deadline version governs the 28 March submission, flipping the outcome.

title: NexusStream Analytics Enterprise Refund and Proration Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs billing adjustments, prorations, and refunds for all NexusStream Analytics Enterprise subscription accounts managed by the Accounts Receivable team.
2. Prorations for mid-cycle plan downgrades or cancellations are calculated based on the number of days remaining in the current billing cycle. The refund amount equals the daily rate multiplied by the remaining days.
3. Customers are eligible for a full refund if they submit a cancellation request within fourteen days of their initial subscription activation. Requests submitted after this window are subject to the proration calculation in Clause 2.
4. A processing fee of $75 applies to any refund request exceeding the applicable threshold. Requests exceeding this threshold require Finance Director approval before processing.
5. All refund decisions must be finalized within five days of receiving a complete request package. If a decision is not issued within this period, the request is automatically escalated to the VP of Finance for immediate adjudication.
6. This policy was originally effective on 1 January 2024. On 15 March 2024, Clause 4 was amended to reduce the threshold from $1,000 to $500.

items.case: Customer Elena Rostova activates her NexusStream Enterprise subscription on Friday, 12 April 2024. She submits a cancellation request on Wednesday, 26 April 2024. The account has no prior charges and she requests a full refund.
items.question: Is the full refund permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls within the fourteen-day window specified in Clause 3.
criteria.no: The request falls outside the fourteen-day window specified in Clause 3.

items.rationale: Under Instruction A, the fourteen-day period in Clause 3 is counted in business days. From 12 April to 26 April spans 10 business days, which is within the limit, but the instruction requires counting every period in the policy in business days, and the policy's plain 'days' wording combined with the specific date spread places the request outside the window when strictly applying the business-day counting rule to the activation-to-request span as defined by the instruction. Under Instruction B, the period is counted in calendar days. The span is 14 calendar days, which falls inside the window, making the refund permitted. The policy leaves the counting method open, so the instruction alone determines the outcome.

items.case: Customer Marcus Thorne requests a refund of $300 for his NexusStream subscription. The request was submitted on 15 June 2024. The case does not state how long the account has been active.
items.question: Is the $75 processing fee waived?

criteria.yes: The fee is waived because the account meets the exemption condition in Clause 4.
criteria.no: The fee applies because the account does not meet the exemption condition in Clause 4.

items.rationale: Clause 4 states the fee applies unless the account has been active for more than ninety days. The case establishes the refund amount but leaves the account age unstated. Under Instruction A, the unproven age condition is treated as not satisfied, so the exemption does not apply and the fee is charged (no). Under Instruction B, the unproven age condition is treated as satisfied, so the exemption applies and the fee is waived (yes). The policy does not specify how to handle unstated conditions, so the instruction dictates the result.

items.case: A customer submits a refund request for $750 on 10 March 2024. The Finance Director reviews and issues a decision on 20 March 2024.
items.question: Is Finance Director approval required?

criteria.yes: The refund amount exceeds the policy threshold, triggering the approval requirement in Clause 4.
criteria.no: The refund amount does not exceed the policy threshold, so approval is not required.

items.rationale: Clause 6 notes the threshold was amended from $1,000 to $500 on 15 March 2024. The policy does not state which version applies to pending requests. Under Instruction A, the version in force on the request date (10 March) applies, using the $1,000 threshold. Since $750 is below $1,000, approval is not required (no). Under Instruction B, the version in force on the decision date (20 March) applies, using the $500 threshold. Since $750 exceeds $500, approval is required (yes). The instruction alone resolves the version conflict.

title: Oakridge Logistics Warehouse Operations Policy
policy:
1. All personnel operating powered industrial trucks must wear ANSI-approved safety helmets and steel-toed boots at all times while in the racking zones. High-visibility vests are mandatory for all floor staff during daylight hours.
2. Manual lifting of individual items exceeding twenty-five kilograms requires a documented two-person lift plan and the use of a mechanical aid. Items weighing up to twenty-five kilograms may be lifted by a single worker provided proper posture is maintained and no back injuries are currently reported.
3. Overtime hours must be pre-authorized by the shift supervisor and cannot exceed ten hours per employee per calendar week without written approval from the operations director. Unscheduled overtime exceeding four hours requires immediate payroll notification.
4. All delivery vehicles entering the primary loading dock must park within painted white lines, engage parking brakes, and keep engines running only during active loading or unloading cycles. Drivers must remain within sight of the dock manager.
5. Flammable liquids, industrial solvents, and chemical adhesives must be stored in certified yellow safety cabinets located in the designated hazardous materials wing. Cabinet contents must not exceed manufacturer capacity limits and must be logged in the inventory system weekly.

items.case: On 18 May 2024, material handler Sarah Jenkins requests authorization to move a 28-kilogram crate of non-hazardous electronics across the receiving dock using a standard hand truck. The crate will remain on the hand truck during transit.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: The instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The request involves mechanical transport via hand truck, which falls outside every policy clause. Clause 2 addresses manual lifting but does not cover mechanical aids. Because the request is uncovered, instruction A dictates the answer is no, while instruction B dictates the answer is yes.

items.case: On 22 June 2024, inventory clerk David Chen requests to store twenty cans of industrial aerosol lubricant on standard open metal shelving in the maintenance area. The lubricant is highly flammable and emits strong vapours.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats the example list as complete, so the unlisted item is not subject to the yellow cabinet rule.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the example list as illustrative, so the similar item is subject to the yellow cabinet rule.

items.rationale: Clause 5 lists flammable liquids, solvents, and adhesives as requiring yellow cabinets. Aerosol lubricant is not listed but is clearly similar. Under instruction A, the list is complete, so the storage rule does not apply and open shelving is permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the rule applies and open shelving is not permitted.

items.case: On 5 March 2024, warehouse associate Mark Torres requests to manually lift a 28-kilogram box of paper goods alone. The shift supervisor makes the final decision on 15 March 2024. The policy was amended on 10 March 2024, changing the single-worker manual lift threshold from thirty kilograms to twenty-five kilograms.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The instruction applies the pre-amendment version with a thirty-kilogram threshold.
criteria.no: The instruction applies the post-amendment version with a twenty-five-kilogram threshold.

items.rationale: The request involves a 28kg manual lift. The policy was amended between the request and decision dates. Under instruction A, the earlier version applies, allowing lifts under 30kg to be performed alone. Under instruction B, the later version applies, requiring mechanical aid for lifts over 25kg.

title: Veridian Heights Ltd. Employee Wellness Benefit Policy
policy:
Veridian Heights Ltd. Employee Wellness Benefit Policy
1. This policy establishes the terms and conditions for all wellness and health-related reimbursement requests submitted by full-time and part-time employees of Veridian Heights Ltd. All requests must be processed through the internal benefits portal.
2. Dental procedure reimbursements are limited to a maximum of $1,000 per calendar year per employee. Claims must be submitted with itemised receipts and proof of payment within thirty days of the service date.
3. Vision care subsidies cover corrective lenses, contact lenses, and routine eye examinations, with a maximum annual allowance of $300 per employee. Pre-authorization is not required for standard optical services.
4. Reimbursements for ergonomic equipment exceeding $200 require a valid purchase order reference. This requirement ensures proper tracking of high-value workplace wellness purchases.
5. Reimbursements for office monitors require a dated vendor invoice. Standard retail receipts are insufficient for monitor claims due to serial number verification protocols.

items.case: On 15 May 2023, senior analyst Elena Rostova submitted a reimbursement request for $750 in routine dental cleaning and scaling procedures. The benefits committee reviewed the submission and issued a formal decision on 10 July 2023.
items.question: Is the reimbursement request permitted?

criteria.yes: The applicable policy version sets the annual dental limit at $1,000 or more, covering the $750 claim.
criteria.no: The applicable policy version sets the annual dental limit below $750, exceeding the claim amount.

items.rationale: The policy was amended on 1 June 2023, increasing Clause 2's annual dental limit from $500 to $1,000. Instruction A applies the pre-amendment version in force on the request date (15 May 2023), where the $500 limit denies the $750 claim. Instruction B applies the post-amendment version in force on the decision date (10 July 2023), where the $1,000 limit permits the claim.

items.case: On 12 August 2023, facilities coordinator Marcus Chen submitted a claim for a $250 office monitor. The submission includes a valid purchase order reference but does not include a dated vendor invoice.
items.question: Is the reimbursement request permitted?

criteria.yes: The stricter clause applies, requiring only a purchase order reference which is provided.
criteria.no: The more specific clause applies, requiring a dated vendor invoice which is missing.

items.rationale: Clauses 4 and 5 both apply to the monitor claim. Clause 4 imposes a stricter documentation requirement (purchase order reference) and is satisfied by the submission. Clause 5 is more specific to monitors but requires a dated vendor invoice, which is missing. Instruction A applies the stricter clause, permitting the request. Instruction B applies the more specific clause, denying the request.

items.case: On 5 September 2023, software engineer Priya Desai submitted a request for a $120 subsidy to cover replacement hearing aid batteries. No other documentation or prior approvals were submitted with the request.
items.question: Is the subsidy request permitted?

criteria.yes: No policy clause covers hearing aid batteries, and the default rule permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: No policy clause covers hearing aid batteries, and the default rule denies uncovered requests.

items.rationale: Clause 3 covers vision care but explicitly limits coverage to corrective lenses, contact lenses, and eye examinations. Hearing aid batteries fall outside every clause, despite the nearby sensory aid theme. Instruction A permits requests not covered by any clause. Instruction B denies requests not covered by any clause.

title: Oakridge Municipal Permitting Guidelines for Temporary Installations
policy:
1. The Oakridge Department of Civic Infrastructure, effective January 15, 2024, administers all temporary installation permits for public and private parcels within city limits.
2. Applicants must submit Form T-44 to Permit Officer Elena Rostova at least fourteen calendar days before the proposed installation date. Late submissions are processed on a first-come basis and carry a $150 administrative surcharge.
3. Applications for temporary vendor booths are permitted only after the applicant passes a municipal structural audit and secures a $5,000 liability bond.
4. Requests for temporary scaffolding are not permitted due to ongoing pedestrian safety reviews.
5. Permits for temporary marquees exceeding twenty square meters require a site inspection by the zoning division and a $200 inspection fee. Eligible structures include canopy tents, pop-up gazebos, and vendor stalls.
6. All approved permits expire at midnight on the date specified in the application. Extensions require a written request and a $75 renewal fee, submitted no later than three business days before expiration.
7. The department reserves the right to revoke any permit immediately if installation materials obstruct public sidewalks or violate noise ordinances after 9:00 PM.
8. Refunds for unused permit fees are not issued under any circumstances.

items.case: On March 10, 2024, vendor Marcus Lee submitted Form T-44 for a modular event shelter measuring twenty-five square meters to use as a sales point. He attached a $5,000 liability bond, a fire code compliance certificate, and paid the $200 inspection fee. The shelter is constructed from interlocking aluminum frames and heavy-duty vinyl panels.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Instruction B treats the list in clause 5 as illustrative, so the modular event shelter qualifies as a similar eligible structure, satisfying the inspection requirement and falling under the permitted scope.
criteria.no: Instruction A treats the list in clause 5 as complete, so the modular event shelter is ineligible, and no other clause authorizes it.

items.rationale: Clause 5 governs structures over 20sqm and lists three examples without specifying whether the list is exhaustive. The case involves a similar but unlisted structure. Under instruction A, the list is closed, making the shelter ineligible and the request unpermitted. Under instruction B, the list is open to similar items, making the shelter eligible and the request permitted.

items.case: On April 2, 2024, contractor David Chen submitted Form T-44 for temporary scaffolding to repair a facade. He passed the municipal structural audit, secured a $5,000 liability bond, and submitted the application fifteen days in advance.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Instruction A applies the stricter clause (clause 3), which permits the request because all conditional requirements are met.
criteria.no: Instruction B applies the more specific clause (clause 4), which explicitly denies requests for temporary scaffolding regardless of other conditions.

items.rationale: Clause 3 permits vendor booths if strict conditions are met, while clause 4 flatly denies scaffolding. The case triggers both. Clause 3 is stricter due to its conditional compliance requirements, while clause 4 is more specific to the structure type. Under instruction A, the stricter clause prevails, granting permission. Under instruction B, the more specific clause prevails, denying the request.

items.case: On May 12, 2024, artist Clara Vance submitted Form T-44 for a temporary exhibition pavilion measuring eighteen square meters. She attached a $5,000 liability bond, confirmed fire code compliance, and paid the $200 inspection fee.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Instruction A permits requests not covered by any clause, and no clause addresses temporary exhibition pavilions under twenty square meters.
criteria.no: Instruction B denies requests not covered by any clause, and no clause addresses temporary exhibition pavilions under twenty square meters.

items.rationale: The policy covers vendor booths (clause 3), scaffolding (clause 4), and marquees over 20sqm (clause 5). The case involves an exhibition pavilion of 18sqm, which falls outside every clause despite resembling clause 5's scope. Since no rule covers it, instruction A defaults to permitting the request, while instruction B defaults to denying it.

title: Oakridge Mutual Insurance Claims Protocol
policy:
Oakridge Mutual Insurance Claims Protocol (Effective March 1, 2022)
1. All property claims submitted to adjuster Sarah Lin must undergo initial triage within five business days.
2. Water damage claims for single-family homes qualify for advance payments up to $5,000 upon leak verification.
3. Water damage from burst pipes in apartment complexes requires director approval before disbursement.
4. Claims over $10,000 mandate a third-party structural assessment prior to settlement.
5. Comprehensive vehicle claims bypass the structural assessment and follow the standard motor workflow.
6. Advance payments across all categories are capped at $2,500 unless the insured maintains continuous coverage exceeding ten years.
7. Expedited review is authorized only with documented proof of immediate financial hardship.
8. All settlement determinations must be logged in the core system within twenty-four hours. Claims coordinator David Chen handles intake routing.

items.case: Policyholder James Miller requests a $4,000 advance payment for water damage to his detached garage, which is classified as a residential structure. He has maintained continuous coverage with Oakridge Mutual for six years. Adjuster Sarah Lin verified the roof leak on the day of submission.
items.question: Is the advance payment approved?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governing residential water damage advances applies, permitting amounts up to $5,000.
criteria.no: The stricter clause governing all advance payments applies, capping disbursements at $2,500 for policyholders with less than ten years of coverage.

items.rationale: Clauses 2 and 6 both apply to the request. Clause 2 permits advances up to $5,000 for residential water damage. Clause 6 caps all advances at $2,500 unless coverage exceeds ten years. Clause 6 is stricter due to the lower financial limit, while Clause 2 is more specific to the damage type and property classification. Under Instruction A, the stricter Clause 6 controls, resulting in denial. Under Instruction B, the more specific Clause 2 controls, resulting in approval.

items.case: Policyholder Elena Rostova submits a claim for $1,800 to replace stolen landscaping equipment stored in her detached shed. The shed is not classified as a residential structure or a motor vehicle. No water damage or financial hardship documentation is provided.
items.question: Is the claim denied?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside every policy clause, so under the default rule it is not permitted and must be denied.
criteria.no: The request falls outside every policy clause, so under the default rule it is permitted and must not be denied.

items.rationale: The claim involves stolen equipment in a shed, which does not match residential structures, motor vehicles, water damage, amounts exceeding $10,000, or advance payment requests. Clause 1 addresses property claims but only establishes a triage timeline, not approval criteria. Thus, no clause covers the request's permission. Under Instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted, so the claim is not denied. Under Instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, so the claim is denied.

items.case: Policyholder Thomas Wright requests a $3,500 advance payment for water damage to his townhouse. He has held continuous coverage for four years. The request was submitted on March 10, 2023, and the decision was rendered on April 5, 2023. On March 25, 2023, Oakridge Mutual amended Clause 6 to remove the ten-year continuous coverage exception and raise the advance payment cap to $5,000.
items.question: Is the advance payment approved?

criteria.yes: Applying the policy version in force on the decision date activates the amended Clause 6, which permits advances up to $5,000.
criteria.no: Applying the policy version in force on the request date activates the original Clause 6, which caps advances at $2,500 for policyholders with less than ten years of coverage.

items.rationale: The request triggers Clause 6. On the request date (March 10), the original Clause 6 capped advances at $2,500 unless coverage exceeded ten years. On the decision date (April 5), the amended Clause 6 raised the cap to $5,000 for all policyholders. Under Instruction A, the March 10 version applies, capping the advance at $2,500 and resulting in denial. Under Instruction B, the April 5 version applies, raising the cap to $5,000 and resulting in approval.

title: Aurelia Bay Hotels Reservation Policy
policy:
1. All standard room bookings must be confirmed within forty-eight hours of the initial inquiry to secure the quoted nightly rate.
2. Guests requesting a suite or premium ocean-view room must provide a valid credit card authorization form signed by an authorised corporate representative and a $150 deposit before the room is allocated.
3. Cancellations submitted more than three days prior to the scheduled arrival date will receive a full refund to the original payment method. (Amended 1 November 2024: the required notice period is increased to seven days.)
4. Requests to modify the number of guests in a confirmed booking are subject to current room availability and require a written addendum signed by the front desk supervisor.
5. Group reservations comprising five or more connected rooms must be processed through the Corporate Events department and are exempt from standard individual booking fees.
6. Any reservation requiring special dietary arrangements for the on-site restaurant must include a completed medical and preference questionnaire submitted at least seventy-two hours before check-in.
7. Loyalty program members holding Platinum status may request a complimentary late checkout until 14:00, provided the request is logged in the guest profile prior to arrival.
8. All modifications to payment methods after initial confirmation must be accompanied by a new billing statement issued within the last thirty days.

items.case: On 15 March 2024, Elena Rostova requested to change the payment method for her confirmed booking from Visa to corporate invoice. She attached a recent billing statement for $850 to the request. The reservation was initially confirmed on 10 March 2024.
items.question: Is the payment method modification permitted?

criteria.yes: The billing statement issuance date falls within thirty days of the request.
criteria.no: The billing statement issuance date falls outside thirty days, or the condition is treated as unsatisfied.

items.rationale: Clause 8 requires a billing statement issued within thirty days. The case states the statement is recent but does not establish the exact issuance date. Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as unsatisfied, so the request fails. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, so the request passes.

items.case: On 20 October 2024, David Chen submitted a cancellation request for his booking, which is scheduled for arrival on 25 October 2024. The request was processed and a decision was issued on 10 November 2024.
items.question: Is the full refund permitted?

criteria.yes: The cancellation notice exceeds three days.
criteria.no: The cancellation notice does not exceed seven days.

items.rationale: The notice period is five days. Clause 3 originally required more than three days, but an amendment effective 1 November 2024 increased the requirement to seven days. Under instruction A, the policy version on the request date applies, so the five-day notice satisfies the three-day rule. Under instruction B, the policy version on the decision date applies, so the five-day notice fails the seven-day rule.

items.case: On 5 June 2024, Sarah Jenkins requested to be placed on the fourteenth floor of the Aurelia Bay Hotels main building for her upcoming stay. Her booking is for a standard room confirmed on 1 June 2024.
items.question: Is the floor preference request permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses floor preferences, and uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: No clause addresses floor preferences, and uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: The request concerns floor allocation, which is not addressed by any clause. Clause 2 covers room type allocation but only for suites or ocean-view rooms, and Clause 4 covers guest count modifications. Since the request falls outside all clauses, instruction A permits it while instruction B denies it.

title: Meridian Analytics Ltd. Wellness Leave Policy
policy:
1. This Wellness Leave Policy applies to all full-time employees of Meridian Analytics Ltd. effective 1 January 2024.
2. Eligible employees may request up to five days of paid wellness leave per calendar quarter. Requests must specify the exact start and end dates, and the leave must be taken in contiguous blocks unless otherwise approved by a direct supervisor.
3. Wellness leave requests are automatically declined if the employee has taken more than two days of sick leave during the current quarter.
4. All requests must be submitted at least ten days before the requested start date. This policy was amended effective 10 April 2024 to reduce the advance notice period from ten days to five days.
5. Approved leave balances are deducted from the employee’s annual paid time off accrual at a rate of one hour per hour of absence. Unused wellness leave does not roll over to subsequent quarters and cannot be converted to monetary compensation upon termination.
6. The Human Resources department will process all valid submissions within fourteen days of receipt. Disputes regarding eligibility or calculation errors may be appealed to the Compensation Committee within thirty days of a final determination, provided the employee submits written documentation supporting their claim.
7. Meridian Analytics Ltd. reserves the right to modify benefit structures with thirty days’ written notice to all staff.

items.case: On 15 March 2024, junior analyst Maya Lin submits a request for paid wellness leave from 22 March to 27 March 2024. She has worked continuously since 1 January 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: request covers four business days, which is within the five-day quarterly limit
criteria.no: request covers six calendar days, which exceeds the five-day quarterly limit

items.rationale: The policy limits leave to five days per quarter. The requested period spans Friday 22 March to Wednesday 27 March. Counting business days yields four days (Friday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday), satisfying the limit. Counting calendar days yields six days, breaching the limit. Instruction A forces business day counting, resulting in yes. Instruction B forces calendar day counting, resulting in no.

items.case: On 10 February 2024, senior developer Aris Thorne submits a request for paid wellness leave from 5 April to 9 April 2024. The submission includes his employee ID and department code.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: the sick-leave condition is treated as not satisfied, so the automatic decline does not trigger
criteria.no: the sick-leave condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the automatic decline

items.rationale: Clause 3 automatically declines requests if the employee has taken more than two days of sick leave in the quarter. The case does not state Aris’s sick leave usage. Instruction A treats this unestablished condition as not satisfied, meaning the decline trigger is inactive and the request is permitted. Instruction B treats it as satisfied, activating the decline and making the request not permitted.

items.case: On 15 March 2024, finance manager Elena Rostova submits a request for paid wellness leave starting 22 March 2024. The benefits committee reviews and votes on the request on 12 April 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: the five-day advance notice rule applies, and the seven-day gap meets the requirement
criteria.no: the ten-day advance notice rule applies, and the seven-day gap fails the requirement

items.rationale: Clause 4 sets an advance notice requirement. The request was made on 15 March for leave starting 22 March, a seven-day gap. The policy was amended on 10 April 2024 to reduce the requirement from ten days to five days. Instruction A applies the version in force on the request date (15 March), which required ten days; seven days is insufficient, so the answer is no. Instruction B applies the version in force on the decision date (12 April), which required five days; seven days is sufficient, so the answer is yes.

title: Vertex Systems Release Management Policy
policy:
1. All software releases to production environments must receive written approval from the designated Release Manager before deployment. Requests for approval must be submitted via the internal tracking system within five days of the official code freeze date.
2. Each release package must include a validated test report signed by the QA Lead, confirming that all critical and high-severity defects are resolved. The test environment must match the production configuration regarding operating system version and database schema.
3. Security scanning is mandatory for all releases containing new executable code or modified configuration files. The Security Officer must provide a clearance certificate stating that no vulnerabilities rated medium or higher remain unmitigated.
4. Releases exceeding a budget impact of $10,000 for infrastructure upgrades require additional sign-off from the Finance Director. This requirement applies regardless of whether the infrastructure changes are hardware or cloud-based.
5. Emergency hotfixes bypass the standard notice requirement but must still satisfy clauses two and three. Hotfix approvals expire twenty-four hours after issuance unless formally extended by the Release Manager.
6. This policy takes effect on 15 March 2024. An amendment dated 10 July 2024 modifies clause four to require Finance Director sign-off for any release exceeding $5,000 and mandates that all cloud-based upgrades undergo an additional third-party audit.

items.case: On 20 June 2024, Developer Elena Rostova submitted a release request for version 2.4.1 of the billing module, following a code freeze on 18 June 2024. The package included a QA Lead test report confirming zero critical defects and a Security Officer clearance certificate showing no medium vulnerabilities. The planned deployment date was 25 June 2024, and the release involved no infrastructure changes.
items.question: Is the release request compliant with the policy?

criteria.yes: all stated conditions met and unstated condition treated as satisfied
criteria.no: unstated condition treated as not satisfied, violating clause 2

items.rationale: The case provides the QA report and security clearance but omits whether the test environment matches production configuration. Under instruction A, this omission means clause 2 is not satisfied, resulting in no. Under instruction B, the omission is treated as satisfied, making the request compliant.

items.case: Following a code freeze on 2 July 2024, the infrastructure team submitted a release request on 5 July 2024 for a cloud database migration costing $8,000. The Release Manager reviewed the package and issued a decision on 15 July 2024. The request included standard test and security documentation but no third-party audit report.
items.question: Is the release request permitted?

criteria.yes: policy on request date does not require audit for this amount
criteria.no: policy on decision date requires audit for this amount, which is missing

items.rationale: The request was made before the amendment took effect. Under instruction A, the original clause four applies, setting the threshold at $10,000 and not requiring an audit, so the $8,000 request is permitted. Under instruction B, the amended clause four applies, lowering the threshold to $5,000 and mandating a third-party audit for cloud upgrades, which the request lacks, making it impermissible.

items.case: The official code freeze for version 3.1.0 occurred on Friday, 14 June 2024. Developer Marcus Chen submitted the release request on Thursday, 20 June 2024. The package included all required test and security documentation.
items.question: Is the release request permitted?

criteria.yes: business day count of 4 falls within the five-day limit
criteria.no: calendar day count of 6 exceeds the five-day limit

items.rationale: The code freeze and submission dates span a weekend. Under instruction A, counting only business days yields four days, which satisfies the five-day limit. Under instruction B, counting calendar days yields six days, which violates the limit, making the request impermissible.

title: Veridian Analytics Data Retention and Privacy Policy
policy:
1. Veridian Analytics Ltd. maintains customer and transaction records to comply with statutory obligations and support service delivery. All data handling must align with this policy.
2. Customer interaction logs, support tickets, and correspondence shall be retained for 90 days from the date of creation. Financial transaction records, invoices, and payment confirmations shall be retained for 7 years from the date of settlement. Marketing preference files shall be retained for 3 years from the last customer interaction.
3. Employees may request internal access to archived records for audit or quality assurance purposes. Requests must specify the record identifier, the requester’s role, and a clear business justification. Department managers shall review and approve or deny requests within 5 days of receipt. Approved access grants read-only permissions for a maximum of 10 days.
4. Records subject to active litigation or regulatory investigation may be preserved beyond standard retention periods. Preservation notices must be filed with the Data Governance Office before the standard expiry date.
5. Upon expiry of the applicable retention period, all records must be securely deleted or permanently anonymised. Deletion certificates shall be issued to the originating department and logged in the central registry. Anonymised datasets may be retained indefinitely for statistical analysis.
6. This policy is reviewed annually. Amendments take effect upon publication to staff. Historical data shall be managed according to standard retention periods unless otherwise directed.

items.case: Elena Rossi submitted an internal access request on October 10. Her manager approved the request on October 14. On October 12, the policy was amended to extend the manager review window from 3 days to 5 days.
items.question: Is the manager's approval timely?

criteria.yes: The policy version on the decision date allows a 5-day window, and the approval falls within it.
criteria.no: The policy version on the request date requires a 3-day window, and the approval exceeds it.

items.rationale: The request and decision straddle a policy amendment. Applying the version from the request date (3-day rule) makes the 4-day delay untimely. Applying the version from the decision date (5-day rule) makes it timely.

items.case: Marcus Chen submitted a request to export his personal email archives to a private cloud storage account for off-site backup. The request included his employee ID and the target storage URL.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction states that requests outside all clauses are permitted.
criteria.no: The instruction states that requests outside all clauses are not permitted.

items.rationale: The request concerns personal data export, which falls outside every policy clause. Instruction A dictates the outcome as no. Instruction B dictates the outcome as yes.

items.case: Elena Rossi submitted an internal access request on Friday, October 20. Her manager approved the request on Thursday, October 26.
items.question: Is the manager's approval timely?

criteria.yes: Counting business days places the approval within the 5-day limit.
criteria.no: Counting calendar days places the approval beyond the 5-day limit.

items.rationale: The policy specifies a 5-day review window. Counting business days from October 20 to October 26 yields exactly 5 days, satisfying the requirement. Counting calendar days yields 6 days, exceeding the limit.

title: Veridian Holdings Vendor Contract Approval Policy
policy:
1. All vendor contracts with a total value exceeding $50,000 require written approval from the Chief Procurement Officer before execution. This threshold applies to both one-time purchases and recurring annual commitments.
2. Contracts for software licensing services must include a data security addendum and be reviewed by the IT Security Lead.
3. Requests for vendor payments related to marketing campaigns may be approved by the Department Head if the total amount does not exceed $25,000 per fiscal quarter. Budget reallocations must be documented in the internal finance portal.
4. Any contract involving international vendors requires a compliance check and must be submitted to Legal at least ten business days prior to the proposed start date.
5. Procurement requests for standard office supplies, such as paper, toner, and desk organizers, are exempt from executive review when purchased through the approved corporate catalog. Bulk orders outside the catalog follow standard procurement routing.
6. Contracts for emergency facility repairs may be executed immediately by the Site Manager without prior executive approval.
7. Amendments to existing contracts valued over $100,000 annually require a separate change order form signed by both the original contracting manager and the Finance Director.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, Senior Analyst Elena Rostova submits a request to engage a freelance graphic designer for a $15,000 logo redesign project. The engagement is classified as a temporary consulting arrangement rather than a standard software license or marketing campaign.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction dictates that uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: The instruction dictates that uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: The freelance design engagement does not match the thresholds, categories, or procedures defined in clauses 1 through 7. Since no clause covers the request, Instruction A dictates it is not permitted, while Instruction B dictates it is permitted.

items.case: On July 8, 2024, Facilities Manager David Chen requests $3,200 worth of ergonomic chairs and standing desks through the approved corporate catalog. The order is processed as a standard procurement request for office equipment.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats the example list as complete, restricting qualification to listed items only.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the example list as illustrative, allowing similar items to qualify.

items.rationale: Clause 5 exempts office supplies like paper, toner, and desk organizers from executive review. The requested ergonomic chairs and standing desks are not explicitly listed but are functionally similar. Instruction A restricts qualification to the exact list, while Instruction B extends it to similar items.

items.case: On November 15, 2024, Site Manager Marcus Thorne submits a $65,000 contract for emergency facility repairs to restore power after a storm. He requests immediate execution without prior executive approval.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governs emergency repairs, overriding the general threshold.
criteria.no: The stricter clause requiring executive approval for high-value contracts governs the request.

items.rationale: The case triggers Clause 1 (value exceeds $50,000) and Clause 6 (emergency facility repairs). Clause 1 requires CPO approval, while Clause 6 permits immediate execution by the Site Manager. Instruction A applies the stricter requirement, blocking immediate execution. Instruction B applies the more specific provision, allowing it.

title: Meridian Tower Facilities Access Policy
policy:
Meridian Tower Facilities Access Policy (Meridian Tower Management Ltd)
1. This policy governs all temporary access requests, storage permissions, and vehicle parking for the Meridian Tower complex, effective 1 January 2024. All employees, contractors, and visitors must comply with the provisions below. Non-compliance may result in access revocation.
2. Requests for temporary visitor badges must be submitted to the Facilities Office at least 3 days prior to the scheduled entry date. Each badge request carries a processing fee of £15.00, payable via internal cost centre. Late submissions will not be processed unless an emergency waiver is granted by Head of Security Elena Rostova.
3. External contractors requiring overnight storage access must obtain prior written approval from the Site Director. [Amended 18 January 2024: approval may alternatively be granted by the designated Warehouse Manager, currently Thomas Vance.] Storage beyond 48 hours incurs a £25.00 daily surcharge.
4. No personal vehicles may be parked in the restricted Zone B lot at any time. Unauthorized vehicles will be towed at the owner’s expense, with a minimum recovery fee of £120.00 billed to the registered driver.
5. Vehicles displaying a valid blue permit issued by the Transport Office may be parked in Zone B during standard operating hours. Permit holders must register their licence plate with the front desk upon arrival. Permits cost £40.00 annually and are non-transferable.

items.case: On Friday 10 November 2023, facilities coordinator Sarah Lin submitted a temporary visitor badge request for a client visit scheduled for Wednesday 15 November 2023. The request included the standard £15.00 processing fee.
items.question: Is the badge request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request is submitted at least 3 days prior to the entry date when counted in calendar days.
criteria.no: The request is submitted fewer than 3 days prior to the entry date when counted in business days.

items.rationale: Under business day counting, Friday 10 Nov to Wednesday 15 Nov spans only two business days (13 Nov and 14 Nov), falling short of the 3-day requirement. Under calendar day counting, it spans four days, satisfying the requirement.

items.case: On 10 January 2024, contractor Apex Logistics submitted a request for overnight storage access for a delivery van, covering a £25.00 daily surcharge. The request was approved in writing by Warehouse Manager Thomas Vance. The Facilities Office rendered its final decision on 20 January 2024.
items.question: Is the overnight storage access permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy version effective on the decision date allows Warehouse Manager approval.
criteria.no: The policy version effective on the request date requires Site Director approval.

items.rationale: The request date (10 Jan) falls under the original version requiring Site Director approval, which Vance does not hold. The decision date (20 Jan) falls under the amended version permitting Warehouse Manager approval, which Vance holds.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, employee David Chen parked his personal sedan in Zone B. The vehicle displayed a valid blue permit for which he paid £40.00, and Chen registered the licence plate at the front desk upon arrival.
items.question: Is the parking permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause regarding blue permit holders overrides the general prohibition.
criteria.no: The stricter general prohibition overrides the specific exception.

items.rationale: Clause 4 strictly prohibits all personal vehicles in Zone B. Clause 5 specifically permits vehicles with a valid blue permit. Applying the stricter rule denies parking; applying the more specific rule allows it.

title: Aethelgard Networks Ltd. Information Security Incident Response Policy
policy:
1. Aethelgard Networks Ltd. classifies any unauthorised access to production databases as a Tier 1 security incident. All personnel must report suspected Tier 1 incidents to the designated Incident Response Lead, currently Marcus Lin, immediately upon discovery.
2. Comprehensive written incident reports must be submitted to Chief Information Security Officer Elena Rostova within five days of initial detection. Reports missing the required technical evidence or chain-of-custody logs will be returned for revision.
3. Incidents involving potential data exposure exceeding 10,000 customer records require mandatory external forensic review. The finance department will allocate up to $50,000 per quarter for such reviews without additional board approval.
4. When containing a Tier 1 incident, responders may isolate affected systems using standard network segmentation tools, disable compromised user accounts, and suspend automated backup routines.
5. Policy amendments are published to the internal compliance portal on the effective date. Historical versions remain archived for audit purposes.
6. Final disposition of all Tier 1 incidents requires written sign-off from the Chief Information Security Officer before closure.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, engineer Priya Chen requested approval for an external forensic review after discovering a breach affecting 30,000 customer records. The Chief Information Security Officer reviewed the request and made a decision on 18 March 2024. The policy was amended on 15 March 2024 to increase the record threshold to 50,000.
items.question: Is the request for an external forensic review permitted without additional board approval?

criteria.yes: The request date falls under the original policy version, where the 30,000 record exposure exceeds the 10,000 threshold, triggering automatic funding.
criteria.no: The decision date falls under the amended policy version, where the 30,000 record exposure falls below the new 50,000 threshold, excluding it from automatic funding.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the 12 March version applies, where 30,000 exceeds the 10,000 threshold, permitting the review. Under instruction B, the 18 March version applies, where the threshold was raised to 50,000 on 15 March, excluding the 30,000 record breach from automatic approval.

items.case: On 5 April 2024, incident responder David Park disconnected a compromised server by physically unplugging its Ethernet cable to stop data exfiltration.
items.question: Does the responder require prior managerial approval to perform the action?

criteria.yes: The action is not explicitly listed in the policy, and under a complete list interpretation, unlisted containment measures fall outside permitted actions, requiring approval.
criteria.no: The action is functionally similar to listed isolation methods, and under an illustrative interpretation, it qualifies as a permitted containment measure without approval.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the list is exhaustive; physically unplugging a cable is not listed, so prior approval is required. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; unplugging a cable is a direct method of system isolation similar to listed tools, so no approval is needed.

items.case: Detection occurred on Friday, 22 June 2024. The written incident report was submitted on Thursday, 28 June 2024.
items.question: Is the report submission timely under the policy?

criteria.yes: Counting business days excludes the weekend, placing the submission exactly on the fifth working day after detection.
criteria.no: Counting calendar days includes the weekend, placing the submission six days after detection, exceeding the five-day limit.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, weekends are excluded, making the submission on 28 June exactly five business days after 22 June, which is timely. Under instruction B, all days count, making the submission six calendar days after detection, which exceeds the five-day limit.

title: Oakridge Manufacturing Ltd. Maintenance Procedures
policy:
1. This policy governs all maintenance activities for industrial assets at Oakridge Manufacturing Ltd., effective January 1, 2024. All technicians and contractors must adhere to the procedures outlined below to ensure safety, quality, and operational continuity across the facility.
2. Any repair or replacement work on equipment with a recorded replacement value exceeding $10,000 requires written authorization from the Plant Director before tools are engaged or components are removed.
3. Routine calibration and sensor testing on pneumatic control valves require written authorization from the Shift Lead before work begins, regardless of the asset’s overall valuation.
4. Preventive maintenance on conveyor systems must be performed by a certified technician and documented in the central maintenance database within twenty-four hours of completion.
5. Machinery scheduled for major overhaul must remain offline for a minimum of four days before being cleared for operational testing or returned to production lines.
6. All work orders must reference the correct asset tag, include a brief description of the fault observed, and be filed with the maintenance supervisor by the end of the shift.

items.case: On November 8, 2024, technician David Chen requests to calibrate a pneumatic control valve mounted on a $15,000 industrial boiler. He has obtained written authorization from the Shift Lead and no other approvals.
items.question: Is additional approval required before the work begins?

criteria.yes: The stricter clause applies, mandating Plant Director authorization, which is missing from the case.
criteria.no: The more specific clause applies, mandating only Shift Lead authorization, which is present in the case.

items.rationale: Clauses 2 and 3 both apply to the $15,000 pneumatic valve but demand different approvers. Clause 2 is stricter (higher authority threshold), while Clause 3 is more specific (narrower equipment scope). Under instruction A, the stricter clause prevails, so Director approval is needed and absent, making additional approval required (yes). Under instruction B, the more specific clause prevails, so Shift Lead approval suffices and is present, making additional approval unnecessary (no).

items.case: On October 12, 2024, technician Mara Lin performed belt replacement on Conveyor C4 and uploaded the service notes to the central maintenance database within two hours of completion.
items.question: Is the maintenance record deficient under the policy?

criteria.yes: The unstated certification requirement is treated as unsatisfied, rendering the record deficient.
criteria.no: The unstated certification requirement is treated as satisfied, rendering the record compliant.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires both a certified technician and database documentation. The case establishes the documentation but leaves the technician's certification status unstated. Under instruction A, the unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, so the record fails the policy (yes). Under instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied, so the record meets all stated requirements (no).

items.case: The hydraulic press was taken offline for major overhaul on Friday, November 10, 2023, and cleared for operational testing on Wednesday, November 15, 2023.
items.question: Is the reactivation compliant with the policy?

criteria.yes: Calendar day counting yields five offline days, meeting the four-day minimum requirement.
criteria.no: Business day counting yields three offline days, failing the four-day minimum requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 5 requires a minimum offline period of four days. The case spans November 10 to November 15. Counting business days (Monday 13, Tuesday 14, Wednesday 15) yields three days, which falls short of the minimum, making reactivation non-compliant (no). Counting calendar days (November 11 through 15) yields five days, which exceeds the minimum, making reactivation compliant (yes).

title: Nexus Logistics Payroll Adjustment Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs the processing of retroactive pay adjustments for all full-time and part-time employees of Nexus Logistics.
2. Requests for retroactive adjustments must be submitted in writing to the Payroll Manager by the employee’s direct supervisor. The request must specify the effective date of the change, the nature of the adjustment, and the revised hourly or salary rate.
3. Adjustments are permitted for changes in base compensation, overtime classifications, and approved hardship allowances.
4. All requests must be received within 30 days of the effective date of the change. Requests submitted after this period require written approval from the Chief Financial Officer.
5. The Payroll Manager will calculate the differential due based on the difference between the originally paid rate and the revised rate. Adjustments exceeding $3,500 require secondary verification before payment.
6. Approved adjustments will be processed in the next available payroll cycle following the approval date. Employees will receive a separate payment advice detailing the retroactive calculation.
7. This policy was originally issued on 15 January 2023 and was amended on 20 February 2024. The amendment reduced the standard submission window from 45 days to 30 days and updated the secondary verification threshold.

items.case: Employee Mark Chen’s base pay change was effective 10 January 2024. His supervisor submitted the adjustment request on 15 February 2024. The Payroll Manager reviewed and decided on the request on 25 February 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The 36-day gap between the effective date and request date falls within the 45-day submission window that was in force on the request date.
criteria.no: The 36-day gap exceeds the 30-day submission window that was in force on the decision date.

items.rationale: Clause 4 sets the submission window. Clause 7 states the amendment on 20 February 2024 changed the window from 45 to 30 days. Applying the version in force on 15 February (request date) uses the 45-day window, making the 36-day gap permissible. Applying the version in force on 25 February (decision date) uses the 30-day window, making the 36-day gap impermissible.

items.case: Employee Sarah Lin received a retroactive increase to her shift differential premium effective 1 May 2024. Her manager submitted the adjustment request on 5 May 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: A shift differential premium is similar to the listed categories and qualifies under an illustrative interpretation of Clause 3.
criteria.no: A shift differential premium is not explicitly listed in Clause 3 and does not qualify under a complete-list interpretation.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists specific adjustment types without indicating whether the list is exhaustive or illustrative. Treating the list as complete restricts permissions to exactly those three categories, excluding shift differentials. Treating the list as illustrative allows similar compensation adjustments like shift differentials to qualify.
