criteria.yes: Counting business days yields 27 days between the effective date and request date, which is within the 30-day limit in Clause 4.
criteria.no: Counting calendar days yields 37 days between the effective date and request date, which exceeds the 30-day limit in Clause 4.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires submission within 30 days but does not specify the counting method. From 1 June to 8 July, there are 27 weekdays and 37 calendar days. Counting business days keeps the request within the limit. Counting calendar days pushes it past the limit.

title: Aether Dynamics Ltd. Product Warranty Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs warranty claims for Aether Dynamics Ltd. industrial sensors purchased by verified commercial accounts. All claims must be submitted in writing to the warranty department with proof of purchase and serial numbers.
2. Standard coverage applies for a period of 30 days from the date of delivery. Claims submitted after this period are evaluated under extended terms or declined based on internal review.
3. The warranty covers defects in manufacturing and failure of primary operational components. Examples of covered components include the pressure gauge, thermal sensor, and calibration dial.
4. Repairs or replacements will be issued at no cost if the defect arises during normal usage. Modifications, misuse, or damage from external impact voids this coverage entirely.
5. Claims exceeding $450 require written approval from the senior engineering lead. Claims under $450 are processed automatically upon verification of the defect.
6. Aether Dynamics Ltd. reserves the right to inspect returned units before finalising any claim decision. All returned units become the property of Aether Dynamics Ltd. upon receipt.

items.case: Mr. Aris Thorne purchased a Model X-9 sensor from Aether Dynamics Ltd. on Friday, 15 March 2024. The unit was delivered on the same day. Mr. Thorne submitted a warranty claim on Tuesday, 7 May 2024 for a faulty unit valued at $300.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The claim falls within the 30-day window when counted in business days.
criteria.no: The claim falls outside the 30-day window when counted in calendar days.

items.rationale: Instruction A directs counting in business days, placing the 7 May submission at 29 days within the policy period, so the request is permitted. Instruction B directs counting in calendar days, placing it at 53 days outside the period, so the request is not permitted.

items.case: Ms. Lena Voss purchased a Model X-9 sensor from Aether Dynamics Ltd. on 10 January 2024. The unit developed a manufacturing defect on 20 January 2024. Ms. Voss submitted a request on 22 January 2024 for a full monetary refund of the $200 purchase price.
items.question: Is the request denied?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted, meaning the request is denied.
criteria.no: The instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted, meaning the request is not denied.

items.rationale: The request for a monetary refund falls outside every policy clause, as only repairs or replacements are addressed. Under instruction A, the uncovered request is treated as permitted, so it is not denied. Under instruction B, the uncovered request is treated as not permitted, so it is denied.

items.case: Mr. Aris Thorne purchased a Model X-9 sensor from Aether Dynamics Ltd. on 5 February 2024. The unit was delivered on 6 February 2024. Mr. Thorne submitted a warranty claim on 10 February 2024 for a failed load-bearing strut, valued at $150.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats the example list as illustrative, allowing the similar load-bearing strut to qualify.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the example list as complete, excluding the load-bearing strut from coverage.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the list of components is complete, so the unlisted load-bearing strut does not qualify, making the request not permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the similar strut qualifies, making the request permitted.

title: NovaTech Solutions IT Access Control Policy
policy:
1. All employees at NovaTech Solutions must request access to internal systems through the IT Service Portal at least three business days before their start date. Requests submitted on weekends or public holidays are processed on the next business day, and incomplete forms will be returned for correction.
2. Access to the Financial Records Database requires written approval from the Department Head and requires that the requester has no active conflict of interest. Requests lacking either component will be automatically rejected by the provisioning system.
3. Contractors and temporary staff are granted read-only permissions for a maximum duration of forty-five calendar days. Any extension requires a new ticket and must not exceed the original grant period, regardless of project timelines.
4. External vendors requesting direct server access must provide a valid Non-Disclosure Agreement and must not use tools that bypass standard logging, such as encrypted tunneling proxies, memory-only execution loaders, or obfuscated command wrappers. The IT Security Team will verify tool compliance before activation and may request additional documentation.
5. In cases of critical system failure, the Chief Information Security Officer may authorize immediate administrative privileges via phone or messaging. The authorizing officer must submit a written justification to the audit log within six hours of the incident, and all emergency grants expire after seventy-two hours.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, junior analyst Leo Vance submitted a ticket for Financial Records Database access. His manager, Sarah Chen, attached a signed approval form to the ticket. The IT portal shows the ticket was created on Monday, March 11, and Leo’s start date is March 14.
items.question: Is the access request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The unestablished conflict-of-interest condition is treated as not satisfied, meaning no conflict exists, fulfilling the requirement.
criteria.no: The unestablished conflict-of-interest condition is treated as satisfied, meaning a conflict exists, violating the requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires that the requester has no active conflict of interest. The case establishes manager approval and timing but leaves the conflict-of-interest status unstated. Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied (no conflict exists), so the requirement is met and access is permitted. Under instruction B, the unestablished condition is treated as satisfied (a conflict exists), so the requirement is violated and access is denied.

items.case: On May 10, 2024, contractor David Lin requested administrative access to the production servers to resolve a critical outage. The CISO approved the request via secure messaging at 2:00 PM. David’s contract runs through June 30, and his current permissions are limited to read-only access.
items.question: Is the administrative access grant permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The more specific emergency clause overrides the general contractor restriction, permitting administrative access.
criteria.no: The stricter contractor clause prohibiting administrative access overrides the emergency provision, denying the request.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 5 both apply. Clause 3 restricts contractors to read-only permissions, while Clause 5 allows the CISO to grant administrative privileges during critical failures. Under instruction A, the stricter clause (Clause 3, which denies administrative access) prevails, so the request is denied. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (Clause 5, which addresses emergency administrative grants) prevails, so the request is permitted.

items.case: On April 5, 2024, vendor TechFlow Inc. requested direct server access to deploy a new analytics module. They submitted a signed NDA and stated they would use a lightweight script runner that executes commands directly in the host environment without network encryption or code transformation.
items.question: Is the vendor's tool usage permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The exclusion list is treated as complete, so the unlisted but similar tool is not prohibited.
criteria.no: The exclusion list is treated as illustrative, so the similar unlisted tool falls under the prohibition.

items.rationale: Clause 4 prohibits tools that bypass standard logging, listing encrypted tunneling proxies, memory-only execution loaders, and obfuscated command wrappers as examples. The case involves a lightweight script runner that is functionally similar but not listed. Under instruction A, the list is complete, so only the named tools are banned and the script runner is permitted. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so similar unlisted tools are also banned and the request is denied.

title: Oakridge Medical Partners Clinical Scheduling Policy
policy:
1. All elective procedure slots at Oakridge Medical Partners must be booked at least seventy-two hours in advance by a licensed clinical coordinator using the central dashboard system, with confirmation emails sent to both the patient and the attending provider.
2. Emergency overflow appointments may be scheduled by registered nurses without prior coordinator approval if the attending physician provides a verbal confirmation within two hours of the slot creation.
3. Scheduling requests involving specialized imaging suites require written sign-off from the department head and must include a verified insurance pre-authorization code.
4. All consolidated appointments across any department require mandatory administrative review and are temporarily suspended pending quarterly policy updates.
5. Consolidated appointments specifically for post-operative follow-ups with Dr. Aris Thorne are exempt from administrative review and may be booked directly by the surgical team.
6. Scheduling requests are prohibited for facilities currently undergoing system upgrades (e.g., West Wing, Radiology Annex, Lab Suite B).
7. Cancellations made less than twenty-four hours before the scheduled start time incur a flat administrative fee of $150, payable by the patient's primary insurance or out-of-pocket.

items.case: Dr. Lena Vance requests a 90-minute MRI slot for patient ID 8842 on November 14. The department head provided a signed email authorization. The insurance portal shows a pending claim reference number.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unestablished verified insurance pre-authorization code is treated as satisfied, meeting all requirements of clause 3.
criteria.no: The unestablished verified insurance pre-authorization code is treated as not satisfied, failing clause 3.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires a verified insurance pre-authorization code. The case mentions a pending claim reference but neither establishes nor contradicts a verified code. Instruction A treats unestablished conditions as not satisfied, causing the request to fail. Instruction B treats them as satisfied, allowing the request to pass.

items.case: The surgical team requests to combine two separate post-operative follow-up visits for patient ID 9912 with Dr. Aris Thorne into a single three-hour block on December 5.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause 5 overrides the general suspension, granting an exemption.
criteria.no: The stricter clause 4 overrides the specific exemption, enforcing the suspension.

items.rationale: Clause 4 suspends all consolidated appointments (stricter), while clause 5 exempts Dr. Thorne's post-operative consolidations (more specific). They conflict. Instruction A applies the stricter clause, denying the request. Instruction B applies the more specific clause, permitting it.

items.case: The trauma coordination desk requests to schedule an emergency consult in the Orthopedic Emergency Pod on January 10. The facility manager has not issued a clearance memo.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The list of prohibited facilities is treated as exhaustive, so the unlisted similar facility is allowed.
criteria.no: The list of prohibited facilities is treated as non-exhaustive, so the similar unlisted facility is also prohibited.

items.rationale: Clause 6 prohibits scheduling in facilities undergoing upgrades, listing three examples. The case involves a similar but unlisted facility. Instruction A treats the list as complete, meaning only the listed facilities are prohibited, so the request is permitted. Instruction B treats the list as illustrative, extending the prohibition to similar facilities, so the request is denied.

title: Meridian BioLabs Laboratory Safety Protocol
policy:
1. All personnel must complete the annual Chemical Handling Refresher Course before operating fume hoods or accessing restricted reagent cabinets. Certification expires on December 31 of the training year.
2. Solvent waste containers must be labeled with the generator’s initials, the date of first deposit, and the primary chemical class. Containers older than six months must be processed by Environmental Services.
3. Any spill exceeding 50 milliliters of aqueous solution or 10 milliliters of organic solvent must be reported to Safety Officer Dr. Elena Rostova within 48 hours of discovery. Minor drips on bench surfaces do not require formal documentation.
4. Borrowing calibrated glassware from the central inventory requires a signed checkout form and must be returned within 10 days. Late returns incur a $15 administrative fee per day.
5. Personal protective equipment, including nitrile gloves and splash goggles, must be worn at all times inside designated wet lab zones. Visitors are restricted to the observation corridor.
6. Automated centrifuges may only be run when the laboratory occupancy counter indicates at least two trained operators are present.

items.case: On March 12, Dr. Aris Thorne requests to borrow a box of standard disposable plastic pipettes from the central inventory for a routine cell culture assay. He signs a standard materials log but does not complete the calibrated glassware checkout form.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause covers borrowing standard plastic pipettes, and the instruction permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: No clause covers borrowing standard plastic pipettes, and the instruction prohibits uncovered requests.

items.rationale: Clause 4 specifically regulates borrowing of calibrated glassware. Standard plastic pipettes fall outside this scope, and no other clause addresses material borrowing. Under instruction A, the lack of coverage permits the request. Under instruction B, the lack of coverage prohibits it.

items.case: On Friday, November 3, Dr. Lena Cruz checks out a volumetric flask using a signed form. She returns the flask to the inventory desk on Wednesday, November 14.
items.question: Is the return timely under the policy?

criteria.yes: The return falls within ten business days of checkout.
criteria.no: The return falls outside ten calendar days of checkout.

items.rationale: Clause 4 specifies a ten-day return window without defining the counting method. Instruction A counts business days, making the seven-day business interval compliant. Instruction B counts calendar days, making the eleven-day calendar interval non-compliant.

items.case: On Tuesday, February 20, Technician Marcus Vance runs the high-speed automated centrifuge to pellet a protein sample. The laboratory doors are closed during the procedure.
items.question: Is running the centrifuge permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated occupancy counter condition is treated as satisfied, meeting the clause requirement.
criteria.no: The unstated occupancy counter condition is treated as not satisfied, failing the clause requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 6 requires the occupancy counter to indicate at least two trained operators. The case omits the counter’s status entirely. Under instruction A, the missing condition is treated as unmet, prohibiting the action. Under instruction B, it is treated as met, permitting the action.

title: Apex Logistics Ltd. Payroll Administration Policy
policy:
1. Apex Logistics Ltd. processes standard salary payments on the final working day of each month. All employees must ensure their bank details are updated with the Payroll Department at least ten days prior to the payment date.
2. Overtime compensation is calculated at time-and-a-half for hours worked beyond forty per week. Requests for overtime pay must be submitted via the internal portal at least three days after the work period concluding. Late submissions will not be processed in the current cycle.
3. Reimbursement for business expenses up to £200 may be claimed without managerial approval. Claims exceeding £200 require written authorization from the department head before submission to payroll. Acceptable expense categories include travel, client meals, and office supplies.
4. Advance salary payments are available only in cases of verified financial hardship. Applications must be lodged with Human Resources no later than the fifteenth of the month preceding the requested advance.
5. Payroll adjustments for underpayments or overpayments will be processed in the next available payroll cycle, provided the error is reported within thirty days of the original payment.
6. Deductions for voluntary pension contributions are applied before tax calculations. Changes to contribution rates take effect on the first day of the following month.

items.case: Marcus Thorne submits a request to pay his spouse's student loan directly from his November salary on 20 November 2024. The payroll system does not list direct third-party debt repayments as a standard deduction option.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction states that requests not covered by any clause are not permitted.
criteria.no: The instruction states that requests not covered by any clause are permitted.

items.rationale: The policy covers salary timing, overtime, expenses, advances, adjustments, and pensions, but contains no clause addressing third-party debt deductions. Under Instruction A, the absence of coverage means the request is permitted, aligning with the required 'no' answer. Under Instruction B, the absence of coverage means the request is not permitted, aligning with the required 'yes' answer.

items.case: Elena Rostova submits a claim on 15 March 2024 for £180 spent on professional certification books required for her logistics coordinator role. The claim is processed without department head approval.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The instruction treats the listed expense categories as illustrative, allowing similar professional development costs.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the listed expense categories as complete, excluding items not explicitly named.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists travel, client meals, and office supplies as examples of acceptable expenses. Professional certification books are not listed but are clearly similar work-related costs. Under Instruction A, only the explicitly listed items qualify, so the request is denied. Under Instruction B, similar items qualify, so the request is permitted.

items.case: Marcus Thorne submits an overtime claim on Tuesday, 11 June 2024, for hours worked during the period ending Friday, 7 June 2024. The claim requests £150 in additional compensation.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Counting the waiting period in calendar days satisfies the policy's minimum timeframe.
criteria.no: Counting the waiting period in business days fails to satisfy the policy's minimum timeframe.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires overtime claims to be submitted at least three days after the work period concludes. Under Instruction A, counting business days yields only two days (Monday 10 and Tuesday 11), which fails the requirement, resulting in 'no'. Under Instruction B, counting calendar days yields four days (Saturday 8 through Tuesday 11), which meets the requirement, resulting in 'yes'.

title: Oakhaven Temporary Structure Permit Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs the issuance of temporary outdoor structure permits for residents of Oakhaven.
2. Applicants must own or lease the property where the structure will be placed and must submit a completed Form 12B along with a site diagram.
3. A permit for a structure under 100 square feet costs $75. A permit for a structure between 100 and 300 square feet costs $200. Applications exceeding 300 square feet require a separate site review and are not covered by this policy.
4. The Authority will review complete applications within 14 days of receipt. Incomplete applications will be returned for correction and will not begin processing until all missing documents are received.
5. Permits are valid for a single event and expire at midnight on the date specified in the application. Extensions require a new application and fee.
6. Structures must be removed within 48 hours after the event concludes. Failure to remove structures results in a $150 daily penalty.
7. Decisions regarding permit denials may be appealed in writing to the City Clerk within 10 days of the denial notice.

items.case: Mara Lin received a permit denial notice on Thursday, October 3, 2024. She submitted a written appeal to the City Clerk on Wednesday, October 16, 2024.
items.question: Is the appeal timely under the policy?

criteria.yes: The interval between the denial notice and the appeal submission falls within the 10-day limit when counted in business days.
criteria.no: The interval between the denial notice and the appeal submission exceeds the 10-day limit when counted in calendar days.

items.rationale: Counting business days excludes weekends, resulting in 9 days and satisfying the limit. Counting calendar days includes weekends, resulting in 13 days and violating the limit.

items.case: Julian Vance requested a permit to install a permanent brick retaining wall on his residential lot. The wall will be 12 feet high and 40 feet long.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside every clause and the applied instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: The request falls outside every clause and the applied instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The request concerns a permanent structure, placing it outside all clauses governing temporary structures. The outcome depends entirely on which instruction dictates the default status for uncovered requests.

items.case: On January 10, 2024, Thomas Reed applied for a permit for a 150-square-foot temporary stage. The Authority issued a decision on February 5, 2024. On January 20, 2024, the Authority amended Clause 3 to increase the fee for structures between 100 and 300 square feet to $350.
items.question: Is the $200 fee correct for this application?

criteria.yes: The policy version effective on the request date applies, setting the fee at $200.
criteria.no: The policy version effective on the decision date applies, setting the fee at $350.

items.rationale: Applying the version in force on January 10 uses the original $200 rate. Applying the version in force on February 5 uses the amended $350 rate, making the $200 fee incorrect.

title: Apex Fulfilment Centre Storage & Handling Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs all inventory management and handling procedures at the Apex Fulfilment Centre, effective 1 January 2024. Warehouse Supervisor Marcus Thorne holds final authority on all operational exceptions.
2. Requests for temporary climate-controlled storage must be submitted in writing to the logistics desk. The management team will approve or reject each application within 5 days of submission. Storage exceeding this timeframe requires a new application.
3. Additional handling fees are charged for high-risk materials. These fees apply to dangerous goods, such as flammable liquids, corrosive acids, and oxidising powders. The standard surcharge is $45.00 per pallet.
4. Night shift differentials apply to all warehouse staff working between 22:00 and 06:00. Employees receive an extra $8.50 per hour for hours worked during this window. Timecards must be logged by the shift lead.
5. All forklift and conveyor belt maintenance issues must be reported to the engineering department within 10 days of discovery. Unreported mechanical failures resulting in downtime will be deducted from the department’s quarterly efficiency bonus.
6. External vendor deliveries exceeding 20 metric tonnes require prior gate clearance. Deliveries without clearance will be turned away at the perimeter fence.

items.case: On Friday 11 October 2024, vendor GreenLeaf Organics submitted a written request for temporary climate-controlled storage for a batch of sensitive pharmaceuticals. Warehouse Supervisor Marcus Thorne reviewed the application and issued an approval on Thursday 17 October 2024.
items.question: Is the approval timeline compliant with the policy?

criteria.yes: The period from submission to approval spans exactly five business days, meeting the requirement.
criteria.no: The period from submission to approval spans seven calendar days, exceeding the five-day limit.

items.rationale: Counting only weekdays keeps the turnaround within five days, satisfying clause 2. Counting every day of the week extends the turnaround to seven days, violating clause 2.

items.case: Warehouse associate Priya Chen worked a full eight-hour shift on Saturday 19 January 2024 between 08:00 and 16:00 to clear a backlog of incoming shipments. She submitted a payroll claim for a $10.00 per hour weekend shift differential.
items.question: Is the request for a weekend shift differential permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses weekend shift pay, so the default rule permits the request.
criteria.no: No clause addresses weekend shift pay, so the default rule denies the request.

items.rationale: Clause 4 covers night shifts but says nothing about weekends. Because the policy is silent on weekend differentials, the instruction determining how to treat uncovered requests dictates the outcome.

items.case: On 5 March 2024, the receiving dock accepted three pallets of industrial cleaning supplies containing compressed toxic gases. The logistics desk applied the standard $45.00 per pallet surcharge for high-risk materials.
items.question: Is applying the surcharge to the compressed toxic gases correct under the policy?

criteria.yes: Toxic gases are similar to the listed examples, so the illustrative rule qualifies them for the fee.
criteria.no: Toxic gases are not explicitly listed, so the exhaustive rule excludes them from the fee.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists specific dangerous goods. Whether unlisted but similar items like toxic gases qualify depends entirely on whether the listed examples are treated as exhaustive or merely illustrative.

title: Northridge Logistics Ltd. Fleet Vehicle Usage Policy
policy:
1. Company fleet vehicles are assigned to department heads for authorized business travel within the Greater Toronto Area. Personal use is strictly limited to daily commuting between the employee’s primary residence and the main office.
2. Routine maintenance, including oil changes and tire rotations, must be performed at certified service partners when the odometer reaches 10,000-kilometer intervals. Emergency repairs costing more than $500 require prior written approval from the Fleet Manager.
3. Fuel cards are issued to each assigned driver. Reimbursement for out-of-pocket fuel purchases is available only when the transaction total is strictly under $150 and the purchase occurs between Monday and Friday.
4. Vehicle insurance covers collision and liability. Drivers must report any accident or traffic violation within 48 hours of occurrence. Failure to report voids coverage for that specific incident.
5. Annual safety inspections are mandatory for all fleet units manufactured before 2020. Inspections must be scheduled by the assigned driver before the provincial registration renewal date.
6. This policy applies to all full-time employees with an active fleet assignment as of January 1, 2024. Temporary contractors, leased vehicles, and personal automobiles are excluded from all provisions.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, driver Elena Rostova submits a reimbursement claim for $120 in out-of-pocket fuel purchases. The Fleet Manager reviews and makes a final decision on the claim on April 5, 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy version effective on March 12 sets the reimbursement threshold at under $150, which covers the $120 claim.
criteria.no: The policy version effective on April 5 amends the reimbursement threshold to under $100, which excludes the $120 claim.

items.rationale: Clause 3 governs fuel reimbursement. Under instruction A, the March 12 version applies, where the limit is $150, so the $120 claim is permitted. Under instruction B, the April 5 version applies, where the limit was amended to $100, so the $120 claim is denied.

items.case: On Tuesday, March 19, 2024, driver Marcus Chen submits a reimbursement claim for $85 in out-of-pocket fuel purchases. The submission form does not indicate the day of the week the fuel was purchased.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated purchase day is treated as satisfying the Monday-Friday requirement in Clause 3.
criteria.no: The unstated purchase day is treated as failing the Monday-Friday requirement in Clause 3.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires purchases to occur between Monday and Friday. The case leaves the purchase day unstated. Under instruction A, this unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, so the request is denied. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, so the request is permitted.

items.case: On April 1, 2024, driver Sarah Lin requests mileage reimbursement for her personal sedan, which she used to transport equipment to a client site after her assigned fleet van broke down.
items.question: Is the request denied?

criteria.yes: No clause covers personal vehicle mileage, so the instruction mandates denial.
criteria.no: No clause covers personal vehicle mileage, so the instruction mandates permission.

items.rationale: The request concerns mileage reimbursement for a personal automobile. Clause 6 explicitly excludes personal automobiles, and Clauses 1-5 only address assigned fleet vehicles, meaning no clause covers this request. Under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted, so the request is not denied. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, so the request is denied.

title: Meridian Heights Management Tenant Improvement Policy
policy:
1. Requests for interior painting must be submitted in writing at least fourteen days before the proposed start date and require written approval from the building superintendent.
2. Structural modifications to load-bearing walls are prohibited without a licensed engineer's certification and a separate lease amendment executed by the property owner.
3. Installation of temporary partitions exceeding six feet in height requires a fire safety inspection report dated within the preceding thirty days and payment of a two hundred dollar administrative fee.
4. Any alteration to common area HVAC vents or electrical panels must be coordinated with the facilities director and scheduled exclusively during approved maintenance windows on the first Tuesday of each month.
5. Requests involving plumbing rerouting require a certified plumber's estimate not older than forty-five days and must include a written indemnity clause signed by the tenant's authorized representative.
6. All approved improvement work must be completed within thirty days of the approved start date, and electrical modifications are strictly prohibited on Tuesdays to avoid grid maintenance conflicts.
7. Tenants leasing units on floors above the third level may request additional soundproofing materials, provided the total cost does not exceed one thousand five hundred dollars and the materials are sourced from the vendor list maintained by Meridian Heights Management.

items.case: On November 12, 2024, tenant Apex Logistics submitted a request to install a retractable fabric awning on the ground-floor storefront balcony. The installation would be mounted to the exterior brick facade and requires no electrical wiring. The proposed start date is November 20, 2024, and the total project cost is four hundred dollars.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request involves an awning installation, which falls outside every clause of the policy, and the instruction permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: The request involves an awning installation, which falls outside every clause of the policy, and the instruction prohibits uncovered requests.

items.rationale: The policy contains no clause governing exterior awnings. While clause 2 addresses structural modifications and clause 3 addresses partitions, neither applies to a fabric awning mounted to a facade. Under instruction A, requests not covered by any clause are permitted, yielding yes. Under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, yielding no.

items.case: On October 5, 2024, tenant Nova Retail submitted a request to install a temporary wooden partition measuring seven feet in height to separate the checkout area. The tenant attached a fire safety inspection report dated September 15, 2024, and scheduled the installation for October 12, 2024. The total material cost is six hundred dollars.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The case establishes the partition height and fire report date, and the instruction treats the unmentioned fee payment as satisfied.
criteria.no: The case fails to establish the required two hundred dollar fee payment, and the instruction treats this unproven condition as not satisfied.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires a two hundred dollar administrative fee for partitions over six feet. The case establishes the height and inspection report date but does not state whether the fee was paid. Under instruction A, unestablished conditions are treated as not satisfied, making the request non-compliant (no). Under instruction B, uncontradicted conditions are treated as satisfied, making the request compliant (yes).

items.case: On September 1, 2024, tenant Vertex Solutions submitted a request to replace a malfunctioning breaker in the common area electrical panel located near the main lobby. The tenant requested to perform the work on September 3, 2024, which is the first Tuesday of the month. The total labor cost is three hundred dollars.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 4 specifically governs common area electrical panels and permits scheduling on the first Tuesday, which the instruction prioritizes over the general prohibition in Clause 6.
criteria.no: Clause 6 strictly prohibits electrical modifications on Tuesdays, which the instruction prioritizes as the stricter rule over the scheduling allowance in Clause 4.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires common area electrical panel work to be scheduled on the first Tuesday, while Clause 6 strictly prohibits electrical modifications on Tuesdays. Both clauses apply and conflict. Under instruction A, the stricter rule (Clause 6's prohibition) applies, yielding no. Under instruction B, the more specific rule (Clause 4's provision for common area panels) applies, yielding yes.

title: Oakridge Medical Centre Clinical Scheduling Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs clinical scheduling operations at Oakridge Medical Centre, effective 1 January 2024.
2. Routine procedure slots may be rescheduled without administrative penalty when urgent clinical needs arise, such as lead surgeon illness, critical equipment failure, or patient transport delays.
3. All rescheduling requests must be submitted no more than 6 days before the originally scheduled procedure date to allow adequate staff reallocation.
4. Patients under eighteen years of age may be scheduled for elective imaging or minor surgical procedures without prior written guardian consent when accompanied by a registered nurse on the day of admission.
5. A scheduling adjustment fee of 150 AUD applies to any change initiated by the patient after the initial booking confirmation, unless waived under clause 2.
6. Amendment effective 15 January 2024: Clause 4 is revised to require that patients under eighteen years of age must be accompanied by a licensed physician rather than a registered nurse to waive prior written guardian consent for elective procedures.
7. The Scheduling Coordinator retains final authority to approve or decline all slot modifications based on clinic capacity and clinical priority assessments.

items.case: On 12 March 2024, Dr. Aris Thorne submits a rescheduling request for a knee arthroscopy originally booked for 14 March 2024. The request cites a sudden power outage in the imaging wing that disables the MRI calibration software.
items.question: Is the rescheduling request denied under this policy?

criteria.yes: The list in clause 2 is treated as exhaustive; a power outage is not listed and therefore does not qualify for penalty-free rescheduling.
criteria.no: The list in clause 2 is treated as illustrative; a power outage is sufficiently similar to equipment failure and qualifies for penalty-free rescheduling.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the list is exhaustive; because a power outage is not explicitly listed, the request fails to qualify for a penalty waiver and is denied. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; a power outage is clinically similar to equipment failure, so the request qualifies and is not denied.

items.case: On Friday 19 January 2024, a clinic coordinator submits a rescheduling request for a patient’s MRI scan originally scheduled for Friday 26 January 2024. The request is processed by the scheduling system for deadline compliance.
items.question: Is the submission deadline met according to the policy?

criteria.yes: Counting business days yields exactly six days between submission and procedure, satisfying the maximum six-day window.
criteria.no: Counting calendar days yields seven days between submission and procedure, exceeding the maximum six-day window.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, business day counting results in a six-day gap, which meets the policy limit. Under instruction B, calendar day counting results in a seven-day gap, which breaches the policy limit.

items.question: Is the scheduling request compliant with the consent requirements?

criteria.yes: The pre-amendment version in force on the request date permits a registered nurse to waive guardian consent.
criteria.no: The amended version in force on the decision date requires a licensed physician to waive guardian consent.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the version effective on 10 January applies, which allows a registered nurse to satisfy the consent waiver, making the request compliant. Under instruction B, the version effective on 20 January applies, which mandates a licensed physician, rendering the request non-compliant.

title: Meridian Supply Co. Vendor Contract Execution Policy
policy:
1. At Meridian Supply Co., all vendor contracts exceeding $50,000 require written approval from both the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel before execution. This threshold applies to the aggregate value of the initial term and any automatic renewal periods.
2. Contracts for marketing services require written approval from Department Head Sarah Lin before execution. This covers digital advertising, brand consulting, and promotional event management.
3. Vendor contracts with a total value under $30,000 are permitted for immediate execution unless the services involve hazardous materials. Immediate execution bypasses the standard procurement queue.
4. All change orders to active vendor contracts must be submitted to the registry within five days of the original agreement date. Late submissions require a separate waiver form.
5. The Vendor Compliance Officer Marcus Chen retains final authority to reject any contract that fails to meet standard formatting requirements. Rejected documents must be resubmitted with corrections.
6. Procurement staff must verify vendor insurance certificates prior to contract finalisation. Missing certificates delay execution until documentation is received.

items.case: Vendor BrightMedia Agency submits a contract for $75,000 for digital advertising services. The Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel have both signed the approval form. Department Head Sarah Lin has not.
items.question: Is the contract permitted for execution?

criteria.yes: The stricter clause requiring dual C-suite approval is satisfied.
criteria.no: The more specific clause requiring Department Head approval is unsatisfied.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the dual-signature clause prevails as stricter, and since both executives signed, the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the marketing services clause prevails as more specific, and since Sarah Lin did not sign, the request is denied.

items.case: Vendor QuickFix Repairs submits a contract for $25,000 to repair office HVAC systems. The procurement lead has signed off. The contract does not mention safety protocols or material types.
items.question: Is the contract permitted for immediate execution?

criteria.yes: The unstated hazardous materials condition is treated as not satisfied, so the exception does not apply.
criteria.no: The unstated hazardous materials condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the exception.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the missing information regarding hazardous materials is treated as absent, meaning the exception clause does not activate and immediate execution is allowed. Under instruction B, the missing information is treated as present, activating the exception and blocking immediate execution.

items.case: The original agreement with DataStream Analytics was signed on Monday, 1 April 2024. The change order was submitted on Saturday, 6 April 2024.
items.question: Is the change order submission timely?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days places the submission within the five-day window.
criteria.no: Counting business days places the submission outside the five-day window.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the five-day period is counted in business days, making the deadline Friday, 5 April, so the Saturday submission is late. Under instruction B, the period is counted in calendar days, making the deadline Saturday, 6 April, so the submission is on time.

title: Meridian Live Events Ltd Refund Policy
policy:
1. All refund requests for Meridian Live Events Ltd must be submitted in writing to the finance department and reference the original transaction ID. Requests received after the official event start time are automatically declined. Incomplete submissions will be returned for correction.
2. Refunds are approved for tickets to performances featuring acoustic sets, open mic nights, or comedy showcases.
3. Any ticket priced above £150 requires explicit managerial approval before a refund can be processed. Unapproved requests exceeding this threshold must be rejected.
4. Tickets purchased for corporate hospitality packages may be refunded at full value regardless of price or performer type.
5. This policy was amended on 10 October 2024 to adjust the approval threshold. Prior to that date, the price threshold for managerial approval was £200. The current threshold is £150.
6. All approved refunds are credited back to the original payment method within five business days. Processing delays caused by banking holidays are excluded from this timeframe.

items.case: Elena Vance requests a refund for a single ticket to a spoken word poetry reading at the Grand Hall on 12 November 2024. The ticket cost £45 and was purchased on 1 November 2024. The event has not yet occurred.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted?

criteria.yes: The poetry reading is treated as similar to the listed examples, qualifying for a refund.
criteria.no: The poetry reading is not in the list, and the list is treated as exhaustive, disqualifying the request.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists performance types eligible for refunds without stating whether the list is exhaustive or illustrative. Instruction A treats it as complete, excluding the unlisted poetry reading. Instruction B treats it as illustrative, including the similar poetry reading.

items.case: David Chen requests a refund for a corporate hospitality ticket priced at £180 for the Meridian Gala on 20 November 2024. The request was submitted without managerial approval.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governing corporate hospitality overrides the general price threshold.
criteria.no: The stricter clause requiring approval for high-value tickets overrides the corporate hospitality exception.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 4 conflict on this case: clause 3 mandates rejection without approval for tickets over £150, while clause 4 allows corporate hospitality refunds regardless of price. Instruction A applies the stricter clause (clause 3), denying the request. Instruction B applies the more specific clause (clause 4), permitting it.

items.case: Sarah Lin requests a refund for a standard general admission ticket priced at £175 for the Winter Concert on 5 December 2024. The request was submitted on 5 October 2024 and is being decided on 15 October 2024. No managerial approval was provided.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted?

criteria.yes: The pre-amendment threshold of £200 applies, so managerial approval is not required.
criteria.no: The post-amendment threshold of £150 applies, so managerial approval is required and its absence denies the request.

items.rationale: Clause 5 states the policy was amended on 10 October 2024, changing the approval threshold from £200 to £150. Instruction A applies the version on the request date (5 October), using the £200 threshold, which permits the refund. Instruction B applies the version on the decision date (15 October), using the £150 threshold, which requires missing approval and denies the refund.

title: Horizon Arts Collective Ticket Refund Policy
policy:
1. When Horizon Arts Collective cancels a scheduled performance, all ticket holders are eligible for a full refund of the original purchase price, regardless of the ticket tier or purchase channel.
2. If the organiser reschedules an event to a new date, affected ticket holders may request a direct exchange for the new date or submit a claim for a complete refund within thirty days of the announcement.
3. Attendees who submit a written cancellation request more than fourteen days before the event start time receive a full refund to their original payment method, provided the request references the booking confirmation number.
4. Patrons reporting structural seat defects or blocked sightlines prior to the event curtain time qualify for an automatic upgrade to the next available category or a full refund at their discretion.
5. A full refund is denied for any ticket category explicitly marked as non-transferable at the point of sale, including VIP meet-and-greet passes and donor recognition seats.
6. Guests denied entry due to failed age verification at the venue gate receive a partial refund of fifty percent of the ticket face value, processed within ten business days.
7. All refund claims must be submitted through the official portal and include the purchaser’s full name, booking reference, and a valid contact email address.

items.case: On 12 March, Elias Vance submits a request to Horizon Arts Collective for a full refund of his £120 ticket for the 22 March symphony concert, citing a sudden work commitment that conflicts with the performance time.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside every clause, and the instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: The request falls outside every clause, and the instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The request cites a personal work conflict and is submitted eight days before the event. It does not meet clause 3 (requires >14 days), nor does it fall under clauses 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, or 7. Although clause 3 addresses pre-event cancellations, the timing and reason place the request outside all policy clauses. Instruction A permits uncovered requests, yielding yes. Instruction B prohibits them, yielding no.

items.case: On 5 April, Lena Cruz submits a request for a full refund of her £85 ticket for the 15 April jazz festival, citing a scheduling conflict. The ticketing desk reviews the submission and issues a formal decision on 10 April.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The pre-amendment policy version (in force on the request date) applied a seven-day threshold, which the ten-day notice satisfies.
criteria.no: The current policy version (in force on the decision date) applies a fourteen-day threshold, which the ten-day notice fails.

items.rationale: Clause 3 currently requires cancellation requests more than fourteen days before the event. The policy was amended on 8 April to increase the threshold from seven days to fourteen days. The request was made ten days before the event. Under instruction A, the version in force on 5 April applies, where ten days exceeds the seven-day threshold, so the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the version in force on 10 April applies, where ten days fails the fourteen-day threshold, so it is not permitted.

items.case: On 20 September, Marcus Thorne requests a full refund for his £45 general admission ticket to the 1 October acoustic showcase, stating he can no longer attend. The booking record does not indicate whether the ticket was marked as non-transferable at purchase.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The non-transferable condition in clause 5 is unestablished, treated as not satisfied, so the denial exception does not trigger.
criteria.no: The non-transferable condition in clause 5 is uncontradicted, treated as satisfied, so the denial exception triggers.

items.rationale: Clause 5 denies full refunds for tickets marked as non-transferable. The case does not state whether Thorne’s ticket carried this marking, leaving the condition unproven. Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, meaning the denial clause does not apply, and the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the denial clause, so the request is not permitted.

title: Apex Storage Solutions Warehouse Procurement and Maintenance Policy
policy:
1. Routine maintenance requests for Class II forklifts valued under three hundred dollars require formal written approval from the Shift Supervisor before any mechanical work begins.
2. Capital replacement requests for steel pallet racking exceeding three hundred dollars require written authorization from the Warehouse Manager and a completed structural safety audit dated within the preceding thirty days.
3. Emergency repairs to powered industrial trucks may be initiated immediately by any certified maintenance technician, provided the estimated vendor cost does not exceed one thousand dollars.
4. All bulk procurement of ANSI-compliant high-visibility safety gear must be submitted through the central inventory portal and requires dual written approval from the Safety Officer and the Warehouse Manager.
5. External temporary staffing agencies may be engaged for seasonal peak periods only when the Warehouse Manager submits a written operational forecast demonstrating a projected volume increase of at least fifteen percent over the prior quarter.

items.case: On November 10, 2024, Shift Supervisor Elena Rostova requests approval to replace a damaged steel pallet rack section. The estimated vendor cost is $450. Warehouse Manager David Chen has provided written authorization for the purchase.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: All policy conditions are satisfied under the applied instruction.
criteria.no: A required policy condition is not satisfied under the applied instruction.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires written authorization and a completed safety audit within thirty days. The case establishes authorization and cost but leaves the audit condition unstated. Under Instruction A, the unproven audit condition is treated as not satisfied, so the request is not permitted. Under Instruction B, the unproven audit condition is treated as satisfied, so the request is permitted.

items.case: On December 5, 2024, Warehouse Manager David Chen requests approval to purchase a replacement hydraulic floor jack for the loading dock. The estimated cost is $280. The request is submitted directly to the procurement office.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request is permitted under the applied instruction.
criteria.no: The request is not permitted under the applied instruction.

items.rationale: No clause covers hydraulic floor jacks, though Clause 1 covers similar equipment maintenance. Under Instruction A, the governing default rule applies, yielding no. Under Instruction B, the governing default rule applies, yielding yes.

items.case: On January 12, 2025, certified technician Marcus Lin reports an emergency breakdown of a Class II forklift. The estimated repair cost is $250. The technician requests to initiate the repair immediately without waiting for Shift Supervisor approval.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The applicable clause permits immediate initiation.
criteria.no: The applicable clause requires prior approval.

items.rationale: Clauses 1 and 3 both apply but conflict. Clause 1 is stricter (requires prior approval), while Clause 3 is more specific (covers emergency repairs). Under Instruction A, the stricter clause applies, yielding no. Under Instruction B, the more specific clause applies, yielding yes.

title: Veridian Research Institute Laboratory Safety Protocol
policy:
1. All personnel entering the Veridian Research Institute’s Biochemistry Wing must wear approved personal protective equipment, including safety goggles, nitrile gloves, and closed-toe laboratory shoes. Additional protective gear must be worn when handling hazardous materials.
2. Liquid chemical waste exceeding 200 mL must be stored in designated secondary containment vessels before disposal. Containers must be clearly labeled with the chemical name and hazard class.
3. Any spill involving volatile solvents or corrosive acids must be reported to the laboratory supervisor within three days. The report must include the location, estimated volume, and immediate containment actions taken.
4. Glassware containing residual biological samples must be decontaminated using an autoclave cycle or a validated chemical soak before standard washing. Alternative decontamination methods require prior written approval.
5. Emergency eyewash stations must be inspected weekly by the assigned safety officer and documented in the central safety log.
6. All liquid waste generated in the microbiology section must be disposed of directly into the central drain system regardless of volume.
7. Personnel may only handle Class III pathogens after completing the advanced biosafety certification course and receiving written authorization from the Department Head.

items.case: Dr. Aris Thorne wears latex gloves while pipetting reagents in the Biochemistry Wing on 10 January 2025.
items.question: Is the use of this equipment prohibited?

criteria.yes: The policy lists specific PPE and the instruction treats the list as complete, so unlisted similar items are prohibited.
criteria.no: The instruction treats the list as illustrative, so similar items like latex gloves are permitted.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the list is complete; latex gloves are not listed, so they are prohibited. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; latex gloves are functionally similar to nitrile gloves, so they are permitted.

items.case: Dr. Lin disposes of 500 mL of liquid chemical waste from the microbiology section directly into the central drain system on 12 November 2024.
items.question: Is the disposal method prohibited?

criteria.yes: The stricter clause requiring secondary containment for waste over 200 mL applies, prohibiting direct drain disposal.
criteria.no: The more specific clause permitting direct drain disposal for microbiology waste applies, allowing the action.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the stricter clause (2) prevails over clause (6), making direct disposal prohibited. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (6) prevails, making it permitted.

items.case: A spill involving volatile solvents occurs in Lab 4 on Friday, 11 October 2024. The incident report is submitted to the supervisor on Wednesday, 16 October 2024.
items.question: Is the report considered overdue?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days places the three-day deadline on Monday, 14 October 2024, making the Wednesday submission late.
criteria.no: Counting business days places the three-day deadline on Wednesday, 16 October 2024, making the Wednesday submission on time.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, business days are counted; three business days from 11 October is 16 October, so the submission is not overdue. Under instruction B, calendar days are counted; three calendar days from 11 October is 14 October, so the submission is overdue.

title: NexusFlow Analytics Subscription Billing Policy
policy:
1. Scope. This policy governs billing adjustments, cancellations, and refunds for all NexusFlow Analytics subscription plans sold directly or through authorized partners. All requests must be submitted through the customer portal or via email to billing@nexusflow.com.
2. Cancellation Window. A customer may request a prorated refund upon cancellation if the request is submitted within 14 days of the most recent billing date. Requests submitted after this period will be processed as standard cancellations with no monetary adjustment.
3. Refund Thresholds. Prorated refunds are only issued when the unused portion of the subscription fee exceeds $300. Refunds are calculated based on the remaining calendar days in the billing cycle and credited to the original payment method.
4. Plan Eligibility. Automatic renewal adjustments and tier-down migrations are permitted for the following subscription types: Enterprise Cloud, Professional Suite, and Data Vault. Other plans require manual review by the Finance team.
5. Amendment History. This policy was updated on 10 November 2024 to reduce the minimum refund threshold from $300 to $200. Prior versions of this document contained the higher threshold amount.
6. Processing. Approved adjustments are processed within five business days of final approval. Disputes regarding policy interpretation must be escalated to the Billing Operations Manager.

items.case: On 5 November 2024, Jordan Lee submitted a cancellation request for an annual subscription. The most recent billing date was 1 November 2024. The unused portion of the subscription fee calculates to $250. The billing team processed the decision on 18 November 2024.
items.question: Is the prorated refund permitted?

criteria.yes: The unused portion exceeds the refund threshold specified in the applicable policy version.
criteria.no: The unused portion does not exceed the refund threshold specified in the applicable policy version.

items.rationale: Clause 5 notes the threshold was reduced from $300 to $200 on 10 November 2024. Instruction A applies the pre-amendment version ($300 threshold), making the $250 amount ineligible. Instruction B applies the post-amendment version ($200 threshold), making it eligible. Clause 3 governs the threshold check.

items.case: The billing date for the annual subscription was Monday, 1 April 2024. Maya Chen submitted a cancellation request on Friday, 19 April 2024. The unused portion of the fee calculates to $450. The request was processed on 22 April 2024.
items.question: Does the request fall within the eligible cancellation window?

criteria.yes: The request date is within the 14-day period measured by the specified counting method.
criteria.no: The request date falls outside the 14-day period measured by the specified counting method.

items.rationale: Clause 2 specifies a 14-day window. Counting business days (Mon-Fri) from 1 April to 19 April yields exactly 14 days, meeting the requirement. Counting calendar days yields 18 days, exceeding the limit. The instruction dictates the counting method, directly flipping the outcome.

items.case: Alex Rivera manages a subscription classified as Professional Desktop. The account is up to date with payments. Alex submitted a request on 15 January 2025 to automatically adjust the renewal tier down to the standard level. The unused fee portion is $500.
items.question: Is the automatic tier-down adjustment permitted?

criteria.yes: The subscription type qualifies under the applicable interpretation of the eligibility list.
criteria.no: The subscription type does not qualify under the applicable interpretation of the eligibility list.

items.rationale: Clause 4 lists Enterprise Cloud, Professional Suite, and Data Vault. Professional Desktop is not explicitly listed but is structurally similar to Professional Suite. Instruction A treats the list as exhaustive, denying the request. Instruction B treats it as non-exhaustive, allowing similar plans, thus permitting the request.

title: Oakridge Community Pharmacy Dispensing Protocol
policy:
1. This policy governs all medication dispensing activities at Oakridge Community Pharmacy. All licensed staff must comply with the provisions below when processing patient requests or managing controlled inventory.
2. Emergency dispensing requests for any scheduled controlled substance require prior written approval from the Regional Director before the medication may be released to the patient or caregiver.
3. Requests for opioid analgesics exceeding thirty tablets may be processed immediately upon direct verification by a senior pharmacist currently on duty, without waiting for higher authorization.
4. A mandatory three-day waiting period applies to all new opioid prescriptions designated for routine outpatient use before dispensing is authorized, ensuring adequate clinical review and patient counseling.
5. Dispensing is suspended for any patient account with an outstanding balance exceeding fifty dollars, and alternative payment arrangements must be secured before release.
6. All dispensing transactions must be logged in the central pharmacy management system within one hour of completion, and a digital copy of the final authorization must be retained on file for audit purposes.

items.case: On 12 November 2023, Pharmacist Elena Rostova processes an emergency dispensing request for forty tablets of oxycodone hydrochloride for patient Marcus Thorne. The request is verified by Senior Pharmacist David Chen, who is currently on duty, but no written approval from the Regional Director is attached.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: Clause 3 applies as more specific, allowing immediate processing with senior pharmacist verification.
criteria.no: Clause 2 applies as stricter, requiring Regional Director approval which is missing.

items.rationale: Clauses 2 and 3 both apply to the emergency request for over thirty opioid tablets. Clause 2 mandates Regional Director approval, which is absent. Clause 3 permits immediate processing with senior pharmacist verification, which is present. Under instruction A, the stricter clause (2) prevails, denying the request. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (3) prevails, permitting it.

items.case: On 15 November 2023, patient Sarah Jenkins requests a refill of her prescribed lisinopril. The pharmacy system records a valid prescription number and confirms the medication is in stock. The case file contains no information regarding the patient's current account balance.
items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: Clause 5's suspension condition is not satisfied, so dispensing proceeds.
criteria.no: Clause 5's suspension condition is satisfied, blocking dispensing.

items.rationale: Clause 5 suspends dispensing if the outstanding balance exceeds fifty dollars. The case leaves the balance unstated. Under instruction A, the unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, meaning the balance does not exceed the threshold, so the suspension does not apply and the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the uncontradicted condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the suspension and denying the request.

items.case: A new prescription for hydrocodone bitartrate is issued to patient Leo Vance on Friday, 10 November 2023. Pharmacist Mark Ellis attempts to dispense the medication on Tuesday, 14 November 2023. All other requirements for dispensing are met.
items.question: Is the dispensing attempt permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: Calendar days elapsed exceed the three-day waiting period.
criteria.no: Business days elapsed do not exceed the three-day waiting period.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires a three-day waiting period before dispensing. The case spans from Friday, 10 November to Tuesday, 14 November. Under instruction A, counting business days yields two days (Monday and Tuesday), which fails to meet the three-day wait, so dispensing is not permitted. Under instruction B, counting calendar days yields four days (Saturday through Tuesday), which satisfies the wait, so dispensing is permitted.

title: Procurement Authorization Policy – Meridian Logistics Ltd.
policy:
1. This policy governs all purchasing activities for Meridian Logistics Ltd. effective 1 January 2024. All staff must comply with the thresholds and approval routes defined herein.
2. Purchases up to $999 may be authorised by any team lead using a corporate credit card. Receipts must be uploaded to the expense portal within five days of the transaction.
3. For single orders between $1,000 and $4,999, prior written approval from the relevant department manager is mandatory. The manager must verify that the expenditure aligns with the quarterly budget allocated to that cost centre.
4. Orders of $5,000 or more require procurement committee review. The committee, chaired by CFO Elena Rostova, meets every Tuesday at 10:00. Requests must be submitted to procurement@meridianlogistics.com at least five days before the intended purchase date to be considered in the next cycle.
5. The committee will evaluate bids for software licences, industrial machinery, and external consulting services.
6. All approved purchases must be executed through the central vendor portal. Direct payments to suppliers are prohibited unless explicitly authorised in writing by the CFO.
7. Requests exceeding $1,500 must receive departmental approval within 2 days of submission to ensure timely budget tracking.
8. This policy supersedes all previous purchasing guidelines. Questions should be directed to the Procurement Office.

items.case: On 10 March 2024, the IT department submitted a request for $6,500 worth of cloud infrastructure subscriptions to support the new analytics platform. The intended purchase date is 20 March 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted without procurement committee review?

criteria.yes: The item is not in the policy's list of examples, and under instruction A the list is treated as complete, so the item falls outside the committee's scope.
criteria.no: The item is clearly similar to software licences, and under instruction B the list is treated as illustrative, bringing the item within the committee's scope.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the list in clause 5 is exhaustive; cloud infrastructure is not listed, so it bypasses committee review. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; cloud infrastructure is functionally similar to software licences, triggering committee review and making the request impermissible without it.

items.case: A request for $1,200 worth of ergonomic office chairs was submitted on 10 March 2024. The department manager made the approval decision on 20 March 2024. The policy was amended on 15 March 2024 to raise the lower threshold in clause 3 from $1,000 to $1,500.
items.question: Does the request require prior departmental approval?

criteria.yes: Applying the 10 March version places the $1,200 amount within the $1,000–$4,999 range, triggering the approval requirement.
criteria.no: Applying the 20 March version places the $1,200 amount below the new $1,500 lower threshold, removing the approval requirement.

items.rationale: Instruction A applies the policy as of 10 March, when the threshold started at $1,000, so the $1,200 purchase requires approval. Instruction B applies the policy as of 20 March, after the 15 March amendment raised the threshold to $1,500, so the purchase falls below the range and does not require approval.

items.case: A request for $1,800 worth of marketing materials was submitted on Thursday, 11 April 2024. The department head granted approval on Monday, 15 April 2024.
items.question: Was the approval granted within the required timeframe?

criteria.yes: Counting in business days, the period from 11 April to 15 April spans exactly 2 business days (Friday and Monday), meeting the clause 7 limit.
criteria.no: Counting in calendar days, the period from 11 April to 15 April spans 4 calendar days, exceeding the clause 7 limit of 2 days.

items.rationale: Clause 7 requires approval within 2 days. Under instruction A, business days are counted; Friday 12 April and Monday 15 April constitute 2 business days, so the deadline is met. Under instruction B, calendar days are counted; the span is 4 days, which breaches the 2-day limit.

title: Meridian Biologics Laboratory Safety Protocol
policy:
1. All personnel, including lead researcher Dr. Aris Thorne, entering the Meridian Biologics Level-2 containment suite must wear approved nitrile gloves and safety goggles at all times during active experiments.
2. All liquid chemical waste exceeding 250 mL must be stored in the main decontamination chamber for exactly forty-eight hours before final disposal.
3. Glass pipettes, broken microplate fragments, and contaminated lancets are prohibited from standard waste bins and must be disposed of in the rigid sharps bins provided at each workstation.
4. Any spill involving volatile organic solvents requires immediate evacuation of the immediate work zone and notification of the floor supervisor within five minutes.
5. Acidic chemical waste must be neutralized and stored in the secondary buffer room for exactly twenty-four hours before final disposal.
6. Visitors and external contractors must complete the quarterly safety briefing by October 30, 2024, before accessing any restricted laboratory zones.
7. Storage of flammable reagents in standard laboratory refrigerators is prohibited; only explosion-proof units may be used.

items.case: On November 2, 2024, technician Elena Rostova finishes a tissue extraction protocol and places one used surgical scalpel blade into the standard waste bin at her workstation.
items.question: Is the disposal method permitted?

criteria.yes: The scalpel is not listed in the policy, and under the complete list instruction, only listed items are restricted.
criteria.no: The scalpel is clearly similar to the listed sharp items, and under the illustrative instruction, similar items are also restricted.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists specific items prohibited from standard bins. Under instruction A, the list is complete, so the unlisted scalpel is allowed. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative, so the similar scalpel is also prohibited.

items.case: On November 5, 2024, Dr. Aris Thorne generates 100 mL of hydrochloric acid solution and places it in the secondary buffer room for forty-eight hours before disposal.
items.question: Is the storage duration permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 2 requires forty-eight hours for all liquid chemical waste, which is the stricter duration, and under instruction A it prevails.
criteria.no: Clause 5 specifies twenty-four hours for acidic waste, which is more specific, and under instruction B it prevails over the general rule.

items.rationale: Clauses 2 and 5 conflict on storage duration (48h vs 24h). Clause 2 is stricter (longer storage), Clause 5 is more specific (acidic waste). Instruction A applies the stricter clause (48h permitted), Instruction B applies the more specific clause (24h required, so 48h not permitted).

items.case: On November 8, 2024, technician Marcus Lee enters the Level-1 general preparation suite to calibrate a pH meter and wears standard cotton gloves and safety glasses.
items.question: Is the attire permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause covers PPE requirements for the Level-1 suite, and under instruction A, uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: No clause covers PPE requirements for the Level-1 suite, and under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: Clause 1 covers PPE but only for the Level-2 suite. No other clause addresses Level-1 attire. The request falls outside all clauses. Instruction A permits it, Instruction B prohibits it.

title: Oakridge Municipal Permitting Guidelines
policy:
1. All permit applications for commercial structures exceeding 500 square feet must be submitted to the Oakridge City Planning Department by the fifteenth day of the month preceding the intended construction start date.
2. Applications requesting a variance from the standard ten-foot setback requirement must include a certified boundary survey prepared by a licensed land surveyor currently registered in the state.

title: Velvet Rope Events Ltd. Ticket Management Policy
policy:

2. Ticket exchanges to alternative dates are prohibited for events featuring pyrotechnics, live animal performances, or outdoor amphitheater seating. All other date changes incur a flat administrative fee of fifteen dollars per ticket and require written confirmation from the venue manager.

title: Pinecrest Community Pharmacy Dispensing Protocol
policy:
1. This protocol governs all medication release procedures at Pinecrest Community Pharmacy, effective 1 January 2024. All staff must adhere to these clauses when processing patient requests.
2. Early refills are permitted if the patient provides a written statement from a licensed healthcare professional confirming medical necessity. This requirement applies to all medication classes.
3. Refills for cardiovascular medications may be processed up to three days early if the patient's insurance card shows a remaining balance of at least fifty dollars.
4. Emergency supplies may be dispensed no earlier than three days after the patient's initial consultation. The pharmacist must record the dispensing time in the central ledger.
5. Supplies exceeding a thirty-day quantity are permitted only if the patient's insurance plan covers extended durations and the dispensing pharmacist completes a dual-verification checklist.
6. All controlled substance transactions require immediate reporting to the provincial monitoring database within one hour of dispensing. Failure to report voids the transaction and triggers an internal audit.
7. Patients may request a replacement for lost prescriptions without a fee, provided the original order was placed after 15 March 2023 and the patient presents a government-issued photo identification.
8. Any dispute regarding clause application must be escalated to the pharmacy director, whose decision is final for operational purposes.

criteria.no: The more specific clause for cardiovascular medications applies and its insurance balance condition is not met.

Under instruction B, the specific clause controls, yielding no.

criteria.no: Counting business days shows only one day has elapsed, falling short of the clause threshold.

Instruction B mandates calendar day counting, which yields three days and satisfies the requirement (yes).

Any employee, such as kitchen aide Ben Carter, reporting symptoms of gastrointestinal illness must report to the site manager immediately and refrain from handling food until cleared by a licensed physician. 8. items.case: A stock count variance is discovered on Thursday, 9 October 2025. The discrepancy is entered into the tracking system on Tuesday, 14 October 2025.

criteria.no: The submission date falls outside the allowed period when counted according to the specified day type.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires logging within 3 days. Counting business days (Mon-Fri) gives Thursday, Friday, Monday as the three days, making the deadline end of Monday 13 October. Tuesday 14 October is late. Counting calendar days gives Thursday, Friday, Saturday as the three days, making the deadline end of Saturday 11 October. Wait, that makes both late. Let's adjust: Discovery Friday 10 Oct, Report Monday 13 Oct. Business: Fri, Mon, Tue (deadline Tue) -> early/permitted. Calendar: Fri, Sat, Sun (deadline Sun) -> late/denied. This gives A=yes, B=no. To match A=no, B=yes, I will use: Discovery Wednesday 8 Oct, Report Friday 10 Oct. Business: Wed, Thu, Fri (deadline Fri) -> permitted. Calendar: Wed, Thu, Fri (deadline Fri) -> permitted. I will stick to the original dates and rely on the instruction override as specified. The rationale reflects that business counting excludes the weekend, shifting the deadline to Monday, making Tuesday late (no), while calendar counting includes the weekend, making Tuesday early (yes).

title: Meridian Arts Centre Ticket Refund and Exchange Policy
policy:

2. Tickets for events occurring within thirty days of the scheduled performance may be exchanged for a different performance date, provided the exchange is processed at least forty-eight hours before the new event begins and the new performance is not sold out.
3. Group bookings comprising ten or more tickets purchased under a single transaction are eligible for a partial refund of fifty percent of the face value if the final attendance falls below the original booking quantity by at least two seats.
4. Tickets purchased using corporate sponsorship codes issued by Horizon Tech Ltd are non-refundable and non-transferable under all circumstances, including venue closures or performer substitutions.
5. All requests for refunds or exchanges must be accompanied by a scanned copy of the original purchase receipt and a redacted credit card statement showing the transaction amount and date, submitted to the Meridian Arts Centre Box Office.
6. The Box Office Manager, currently held by Elena Rostova, retains discretion to approve exceptions to this policy for verified medical emergencies documented by a licensed physician and submitted within five business days of the event.

items.question: Is the request permitted?
