criteria.no: The request involves a partial refund for a single ticket due to seating quality, which falls outside every clause of the policy, and the instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The policy addresses full refunds, date exchanges, group partial refunds, corporate codes, documentation, and medical exceptions. It does not address partial refunds for individual tickets due to seating quality. Clause 3 is nearby but explicitly requires a group booking. Instruction A permits uncovered requests; Instruction B denies them.

The Box Office processes the decision on November 29, 2024. criteria.no: The request-date version of the policy requires processing at least forty-eight hours before the new event, which is not met by the November 29 decision date.

items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.no: The stricter clause prohibiting all refunds for standard tickets overrides the group booking provision, denying the request.

title: Zephyr Airways Disruption Compensation Policy
policy:
1. Passengers holding valid tickets on Zephyr Airways flights departing from or arriving at European Union airports on or after 12 March 2024 are eligible for disruption compensation if their scheduled flight arrives more than three hours late, is cancelled, or they are denied boarding.
2. Compensation claims exceeding 400 EUR must undergo a mandatory ten-day administrative review before funds are released to the passenger.
3. Approved compensation amounts are reduced by fifty percent if the passenger failed to complete online check-in at least two hours prior to the scheduled departure time.
4. Compensation is issued as a non-refundable travel voucher for disruptions caused by internal operational matters such as aircraft technical inspections, cabin crew roster conflicts, or ground handling equipment failures. All other approved claims are paid by bank transfer.
5. Claims for passengers travelling on business class tickets are disbursed immediately upon approval without holding periods.
6. All claims must be submitted in writing to the Zephyr Customer Relations Desk within 180 days of the disruption date, accompanied by the original boarding pass and booking reference.

criteria.no: The more specific clause applies, granting immediate disbursement.

Under instruction A, the stricter clause (2) prevails, so the review period applies. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (5) prevails, so immediate disbursement applies and no review is required.

title: GreenLeaf Provisions Ltd. Temperature Verification Policy

2. All verification requests must be submitted in writing to the Head of Compliance, Elena Rostova, clearly detailing the product type, exact batch weight, and original delivery timestamp.
3. The following items are exempt from immediate verification: canned legumes, dried pasta, and refined vegetable oils.
4. Requests covering bulk shipments exceeding 100 kilograms require additional documentation, including supplier certificates of origin and complete chain-of-custody logs.
5. Approved verification windows close automatically if the request remains unprocessed after the stipulated period, at which point the goods must be moved to quarantine storage.
6. Policy amendments take effect upon publication on the internal compliance portal and apply to all pending and future submissions.
7. Staff responsible for cold chain monitoring must promptly report temperature anomalies to David Chen within 24 hours of initial detection.

criteria.no: The request falls outside the 7-day verification window.

title: Meridian Health Network Clinical Scheduling Guidelines
policy:

2. Rescheduling fees of $45.00 apply to any appointment cancelled or moved within 24 hours of the scheduled start time. This fee is waived for cancellations initiated by the clinical team due to provider unavailability or facility maintenance.
3. Scheduling modifications are prohibited for non-urgent administrative preferences. Prohibited preferences include: changing room assignments, swapping clinician names without cause, and altering visit durations for convenience.
4. Group therapy sessions exceeding six participants require written approval from the department head, Elena Rostova, and must be confirmed no later than 14 days prior to the session date.
5. Emergency overflow slots are reserved exclusively for walk-in patients presenting with acute symptoms. These slots cannot be allocated to scheduled patients requiring routine follow-ups or elective procedures.
6. All scheduling requests must specify the primary care provider or specialist. Requests lacking a designated provider will be routed to the general intake queue and processed on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: Meridian Solutions Ltd. Tuition Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. Eligibility: Full-time employees of Meridian Solutions Ltd. who have completed at least twelve months of continuous service are eligible to apply for tuition reimbursement. Programs must be offered by regionally accredited institutions and must directly support the employee’s current job responsibilities.
2. Submission & Approval: All requests must be entered into the HR benefits portal no later than thirty days prior to the official course start date. Department managers will review requests for budget alignment. Once approved, the authorization code must be attached to all invoices before payment is made to the institution.
3. Financial Limits: Meridian will reimburse up to two thousand five hundred dollars per academic calendar year per eligible employee. All completed courses resulting in a final grade below B are ineligible for reimbursement. Courses meeting or exceeding a B are permitted upon verification.
4. Academic Requirements: Reimbursement is contingent upon successful completion of the enrolled course. Reimbursement funds will be disbursed only after the employee submits a verified official transcript to HR within sixty days of the university’s published grades release date.
5. Separation Clause: Should an employee’s tenure with Meridian end for any reason before the enrolled course is marked complete, the employee becomes personally liable for the reimbursed sum. Full repayment must be remitted to the finance department within fourteen days of the employee’s last working day.
6. Duration Restriction: Reimbursement is strictly denied for any program or course with a scheduled duration of fewer than twelve weeks, regardless of grade or cost.

criteria.no: The unstated grade condition is treated as satisfied, meaning the course is below B, so it is denied under Clause 3.

title: Aegis Mutual Claims Ltd. Residential Property Protocol
policy:
1. Eligibility and Notice: This protocol governs claims under standard residential policies issued by Aegis Mutual Claims Ltd. Policyholders must deliver written notice of any covered incident to their assigned claims coordinator, Elena Rostova, within thirty days of the occurrence. Submissions received after this period require special authorization.
2. Documentation Requirements: Processing begins upon receipt of a complete file. A complete file requires a signed incident report, photographic evidence of the damage, and a certified repair estimate. For incidents involving water intrusion, a licensed plumber’s inspection certificate is also mandatory. Approval cannot proceed until all required documents are on record.
3. Assessment and Limits: Claims coordinator Elena Rostova or deputy Marcus Thorne will evaluate each submission. The maximum approved amount for a single incident is $20,000 in the 1 January 2024 edition and $15,000 in the 1 April 2024 edition. Requests exceeding the applicable limit, or any claim alleging foundation compromise, must be routed to the Senior Underwriting Committee for final determination.
4. Processing Timelines: Once a complete file is received, the assessment phase must be concluded within three days. Approved payouts are issued electronically within five days of the approval date. All periods referenced in this protocol are measured in days.
5. Versions and Updates: Aegis Mutual Claims Ltd. updates this protocol quarterly. The current edition was published on 1 April 2024 and replaces the 1 January 2024 edition. Adjusters shall apply the appropriate protocol version when reviewing each submission.

criteria.no: The elapsed time between file receipt and assessment conclusion exceeds the three-day limit when counted in business days.

criteria.no: Applying the policy version in force on the decision date sets the limit at $15,000, which the $18,000 request exceeds, requiring committee routing.

items.rationale: The request date (10 March) falls under the January edition ($20,000 limit), allowing direct approval for $18,000 (yes). The decision date (20 April) falls under the April edition ($15,000 limit), exceeding the threshold and mandating committee review (no).

title: GreenHorizon Volunteer Expense and Conduct Policy
policy:

2. Volunteers may submit receipts for reimbursement of travel and meal expenses incurred during approved site visits. Reimbursable items include bus fares, metro tickets, and standard park entry fees. Requests exceeding forty pounds per month require written approval from the site coordinator.

title: Veridian Risk Solutions Commercial Property Claims Protocol
policy:
1. Scope: This protocol governs the evaluation and settlement of commercial property damage claims submitted to Veridian Risk Solutions for policies issued after 1 January 2023. All submissions must align with the terms outlined herein.
2. Continuous Coverage Requirement: The claimant must have maintained an active policy with Veridian Risk Solutions for a minimum of twelve consecutive months prior to the date of loss. Lapsed coverage voids eligibility.
3. Covered Equipment: Claims are accepted for damage to standard office machinery, such as desktop computers, laser printers, and ergonomic workstations.
4. Notification Window: Written notice of any loss must be delivered to the regional claims office within five days of the incident date. Verbal reports do not satisfy this requirement.
5. Documentation Standards: Submissions must include photographic evidence of the damage, a sworn statement from the facility manager, and an itemised repair estimate from a licensed contractor. Missing documents delay processing.
6. Assessment & Payment: Upon verification, claims adjusters will calculate the payout based on the depreciated replacement value, up to the policy limit of $50,000 per incident. Payments are processed within ten business days of approval.

title: Veridian Home Goods Return and Refund Policy
policy:
Veridian Home Goods Return and Refund Policy
1. Customers may request a refund for any standard merchandise purchased directly from our online store within thirty calendar days of the delivery date.
2. To qualify for a full refund, the item must be returned in its original packaging, accompanied by the printed order confirmation, and must show no signs of use, wear, or alteration.
3. Items returned in opened packaging but otherwise undamaged will receive a credit equivalent to the purchase price minus a fifteen percent restocking fee, issued to the original payment method.
4. Refunds are not issued for custom-ordered furniture, personalized engravings, or items marked as final sale at the time of checkout.
5. All refund requests must be submitted through the customer portal and will be processed within ten business days of the carrier confirming receipt of the returned goods.
6. Requests submitted after the thirty-day window will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis by the regional accounts manager, who may approve partial credits up to fifty percent of the original price.
7. International shipments returned to our domestic fulfillment center are subject to a flat handling charge of twenty-five dollars, deducted from the final refund amount.

criteria.no: The unestablished condition is treated as not satisfied, failing clause 2.

Instruction B treats the uncontradicted confirmation as present, approving the refund.

title: Veridian Analytics Ltd. Data Retention and Privacy Policy
policy:
1. All personal data collected by Veridian Analytics Ltd. must be retained for a minimum of three years from the date of initial collection, unless a separate statutory requirement applies. This ensures compliance with internal audit standards.
2. Employee health and medical examination records must be permanently deleted within thirty days of the employee’s contract termination.
3. Customer transaction logs containing financial details must be preserved for exactly 730 days after the transaction completes. These records support annual tax reporting obligations.
4. Any data subject request for erasure of personal information will be granted if the request is submitted in writing and signed by the data subject.
5. Marketing preference records shall be deleted ninety days after a customer opts out of promotional communications.
6. Access to any archived dataset requires written approval from the Chief Data Officer before retrieval.
7. Employee access logs must be retained for a minimum of ten days before they may be permanently deleted.
8. Requests for data export must be fulfilled within fourteen days of receipt.

title: Veridian Dynamics IT Access Control Policy
policy:

2. Standard access grants are limited to read-only permissions and expire automatically after ninety days. Requests are suspended if a security incident is reported by the Threat Analysis Unit.
3. Temporary access for external contractors is permitted only for projects with a signed master services agreement dated within the past twelve months. Contractor access is restricted to sandbox environments and must be revoked within forty-eight hours of project completion.
4. Access requests for temporary contractors are denied during fiscal quarter-end periods to ensure system stability for financial reporting.
5. Access requests for contractors assigned to the Phoenix Infrastructure Project are permitted regardless of scheduling restrictions.
6. Requests are automatically denied if they involve tools such as database management consoles, configuration editors, or deployment scripts. All other requests proceed to standard review.
7. All access modifications must be recorded in the central identity management system. Quarterly reviews conducted by the IT Compliance team will verify that active permissions align with current job functions. Permissions not validated during review are suspended pending manager confirmation within five business days.

title: Aether Dynamics Ltd. Nimbus-X Drone Warranty Policy
policy:

title: Oakridge University Grade Revision Policy
policy:
1. The Office of Academic Standards at Oakridge University administers all requests for grade revisions within the Department of Computational Sciences. Requests must be submitted in writing to the designated faculty coordinator.
2. A student may file a grade revision request within fourteen days following the official release of final course grades. The submission must reference the specific assessment and the original score recorded in the university registry.
3. To be considered, a request must include a written statement of academic grounds, the original graded assignment, and proof of prior consultation with the course instructor. The committee will not review requests lacking any of these three components.
4. Grade revisions are generally prohibited for courses where the final mark falls at or above seventy percent. However, a revision may be granted for laboratory-based modules if a calculation error directly affects the practical component score.
5. The Faculty Review Panel will evaluate each eligible submission and issue a binding determination within ten days of receiving a complete application. No extensions to this evaluation period are granted under standard operating procedures.
6. Students will receive written notification of the outcome via university email. If the revision is approved, the updated grade will be reflected in the official transcript within five days of the panel decision.

title: Nexus Data Systems IT Access Control Policy
policy:
1. All requests for access to systems containing customer data must be formally submitted through the central portal and approved by the Chief Information Officer.
2. Temporary access credentials issued for contract work or special projects expire after fourteen days from the date of issuance. Extensions require a new submission and complete approval cycle.
3. Standard developer roles grant read and write permissions to code repositories, testing environments, and internal documentation portals. Access to production databases, customer billing records, and network infrastructure logs requires elevated clearance.
4. Direct managers may approve access requests for employees earning less than one hundred thousand dollars annually. Requests involving higher compensation tiers follow standard escalation procedures.
5. Any access granted in violation of this policy will be immediately revoked, and the requesting manager will be subject to a mandatory compliance review. All access logs are retained for ninety days for audit purposes and must be available upon request by the compliance team.

title: NexusPay Customer Support Escalation Protocol
policy:
1. This protocol governs all internal escalation requests submitted by frontline agents within the NexusPay Support Division. All requests must follow the defined tiers and thresholds.
2. An agent may escalate a ticket from Tier 1 to Tier 2 when the customer has submitted three or more identical inquiries within a thirty-day period. The Tier 2 specialist must acknowledge receipt within four hours.
3. Escalation from Tier 2 to Tier 3 is permitted when the disputed transaction amount exceeds one thousand dollars, or when the customer explicitly requests a formal compliance review. The Tier 3 manager must assign a case reference number before proceeding.
4. Financial compensation requests exceeding five hundred dollars require documented proof of service interruption lasting more than forty-eight hours and written consent from the account holder. Agents must attach the system outage log to the escalation form.
5. All escalated cases must include the customer’s full account identifier, the original ticket number, and a summary of prior resolution attempts. Incomplete submissions will be returned to the originating agent.
6. Final resolution authority rests with the Tier 3 manager for matters involving service continuity, and with the Regional Director for matters involving regulatory reporting.

title: Apex Logistics Warehouse Equipment Loan Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs the temporary issuance of warehouse equipment to staff members for operational tasks within the Apex Logistics Warehouse facility. It applies to all permanent and temporary personnel operating in zones A through D.
2. Staff may request equipment loans for periods not exceeding seven consecutive days. Requests for longer durations require written approval from the Site Director.
3. Authorized loan equipment includes pallet jacks, handheld barcode scanners, and ergonomic lifting straps. All issued items must be logged in the central inventory system before leaving the storage bay.
4. Before any equipment is released, the requester must present a valid safety certification card and confirm that the item has passed its monthly inspection cycle.
5. Replacement costs for lost or damaged equipment are charged to the requesting department’s operational budget, up to a maximum of $1,200 per incident. Amounts exceeding this threshold require finance committee review.
6. Equipment must be returned to the designated staging area by 17:00 on the final day of the loan period. Late returns automatically trigger a two-week suspension of borrowing privileges.
7. All loan requests must include a signed department budget code to be considered complete.
8. This policy takes effect on 1 January 2023 and was amended on 10 April 2024 to update the budget threshold in clause 5 to $800.

criteria.no: The applicable policy version sets the direct-charging threshold at or below $900.

Applying the version in force on the decision date (15 April) uses the amended $800 threshold, so $900 exceeds it and mandates review.

title: Meridian Logistics Fleet Vehicle Management Policy
policy:
1. All requests for the use, maintenance, or replacement of Meridian Logistics fleet vehicles must be submitted through the Central Dispatch Portal by the responsible Regional Manager before the tenth day of each month. Verbal approvals are invalid.
2. A vehicle may be replaced only when it has exceeded 120,000 miles or requires a single repair costing more than $4,000. Eligible replacement vehicles are sedans, compact vans, and flatbed trucks.
3. Emergency repairs exceeding $1,500 require prior written authorization from the Fleet Director. The authorization must explicitly reference the vehicle identification number and the specific mechanical failure. Work may commence immediately upon receipt of this authorization.
4. Fleet vehicles assigned to the Transport Division may be used for personal commuting on weekends only, provided the employee submits a mileage reimbursement claim within five business days of use.
5. All fleet assets must undergo an annual safety inspection before October 15 each year. Vehicles failing inspection must be taken out of service until repairs are completed and verified by a certified mechanic.
6. Regional Managers retain final discretion to deny any request that conflicts with quarterly budget allocations approved by the Finance Committee.

title: Meridian Systems Inc. Export Control Policy
policy:
1. Scope: This policy governs the export of controlled technical data, software source code, and specialized hardware from Meridian Systems Inc. to destinations outside the European Union. It applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party logistics providers handling company assets.
2. Licensing Threshold: Shipments valued at €50,000 or more require a full export license if the end-user is a government entity. Shipments below this threshold, or those to non-government end-users, may proceed under a blanket authorization. Effective 10 April 2024, this policy revised the threshold to €50,000. Prior to this date, the threshold was €75,000.
3. Documentation Requirements: All exports requiring a full license must be accompanied by a signed end-use statement, a completed customs declaration, and a security clearance certificate issued by the destination country. Missing documents will halt the process.
4. Submission Timeline: All export requests must be submitted to the Compliance Office at least 14 days before the planned shipment date. Late submissions are processed on a first-come basis and may delay delivery.
5. Review Authority: The Export Control Manager evaluates all applications against current regulations and this policy. The Manager may request additional information or deny approval if risks are identified.
6. Record Keeping: All export documentation must be retained for five years from the date of shipment. Records must be stored in the central compliance archive and remain accessible for regulatory audits.

policy:

title: Vendor Contract Management Policy
policy:
1. All vendor agreements valued at $5,000 or more must be formally reviewed and signed by the Procurement Office before execution. Contracts below this threshold may be initiated directly by department heads, provided they align with the annual budget allocations and standard terms.

5. Invoices must be matched against delivered goods within 15 days of receipt. Discrepancies should be reported to the accounts payable team immediately to avoid payment holds.
6. Vendor performance reviews must be completed quarterly. Contracts showing two consecutive unsatisfactory ratings will be placed on probation and subject to renegotiation or termination.

title: Meridian Solutions Procurement Directive
policy:

title: Meridian Grant Initiative Funding Policy
policy:
1. The Meridian Grant Initiative supports early-stage scientific projects through discretionary funding. Applicants must submit a complete proposal package including a project summary, detailed budget, and a signed commitment letter from a collaborating laboratory.

title: Aether Airways Disruption Compensation Policy
policy:
1. Compensation is available to passengers whose flights operated by Aether Airways are delayed by more than three hours due to technical maintenance or crew scheduling issues. This covers both inbound and outbound sectors.
2. Eligible passengers must submit a written claim to the customer service portal within thirty days of the scheduled departure date. Supporting documents, including boarding passes and delay notifications, should be attached.
3. Claims for delays between three and six hours qualify for a refund of one hundred and fifty euros to the original payment method.
4. Claims for delays exceeding six hours qualify for a refund of three hundred euros to the original payment method.
5. Passengers who voluntarily rebook onto a later flight operated by a partner airline are not eligible for compensation under this policy.
6. All compensation decisions will be documented and reviewed quarterly by the Aether Customer Relations Board. Staff must record the rationale for each outcome in the central database.
7. The policy applies to all scheduled passenger services departing from European Union airports beginning 1 January 2023.

title: Verdant Dynamics Ltd. Remote Work & Wellness Allowance Policy
policy:
1. All full-time employees hired before 1 June 2023 are eligible for monthly reimbursement of home office equipment costs up to $150, provided the equipment is used primarily for work duties.
2. Reimbursement requests must be submitted within 14 days of the purchase date using the standard expense form available on the company intranet.
3. Eligible expenses are monitors, keyboards, and standing desks, which must be purchased from authorized vendors.
4. All home office equipment claims must be submitted with a formal vendor invoice.
5. Claims for wireless input devices must be submitted with a retail receipt.
6. Part-time staff receive a pro-rated stipend calculated by dividing the full amount by the ratio of their scheduled weekly hours to 40, rounded down to the nearest dollar.
7. Unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the following calendar month and will be forfeited if not claimed.
8. The policy takes effect on 1 October 2024 and supersedes all prior remote work guidelines issued by human resources. Management may amend these terms with thirty days written notice.

items.case: Maya Lin, a full-time software engineer hired in March 2022, purchased a wireless mouse for $45 on 12 February 2025. She submitted the claim on 15 February 2025 with a formal vendor invoice.
items.question: Is the reimbursement request permitted?

criteria.yes: Stricter clause 4 applies, requiring a formal vendor invoice, which is provided.
criteria.no: More specific clause 5 applies, requiring a retail receipt for wireless input devices, which is not provided.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, clause 4 (stricter documentation requirement) governs all equipment claims and accepts the submitted formal vendor invoice, so the request is permitted. Under instruction B, clause 5 (more specific to wireless input devices) governs and mandates a retail receipt, so the request is denied.

items.question: Is the reimbursement request permitted?

criteria.yes: List is illustrative, and a laptop stand is clearly similar to the listed ergonomic accessories.
criteria.no: List is complete, and a laptop stand is not explicitly listed.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, clause 3's list is exhaustive, and a laptop stand is not listed, so the request is denied. Under instruction B, clause 3's list is illustrative, and a laptop stand qualifies as a similar ergonomic accessory, so the request is permitted.

items.question: Is the reimbursement request permitted?

criteria.yes: Period counted in business days is 11 days, falling within the 14-day limit.
criteria.no: Period counted in calendar days is 17 days, exceeding the 14-day limit.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the 14-day window is counted in business days (11 days elapsed), falling within the limit, so the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the window is counted in calendar days (17 days elapsed), exceeding the limit, so the request is denied.

title: Wellness and Dependent Care Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs the Wellness and Dependent Care Reimbursement Program administered by Oakridge Partners. Eligibility extends to all full-time employees who have completed their initial ninety-day probationary period.
2. Employees may submit receipts for reimbursement of qualifying health and family support expenses. Qualifying expenses cover gym memberships, physiotherapy sessions, childcare facility fees, and optical care. The maximum annual reimbursement is one thousand five hundred dollars per employee.
3. Requests must be submitted through the internal benefits portal using the standard claim form. Submissions require original receipts, a brief description of the service, and the date of payment. Claims received without complete documentation will be returned to the applicant.
4. The Benefits Committee reviews submitted claims within ten business days of receipt. Committee members verify eligibility, confirm expenses fall within covered categories, and ensure the annual limit has not been exceeded.
5. Approved claims are processed for payment during the standard monthly payroll cycle. Rejected claims will include a written explanation citing the specific policy provision that was not met.
6. This program may be amended annually by the Human Resources Directorate. Any changes take effect on the first day of the following calendar quarter.

items.case: On 15 August 2024, employee Marcus Chen submitted a claim for two thousand dollars covering a private physiotherapy course. The Benefits Committee convened to review the submission on 5 November 2024. On 1 October 2024, the Human Resources Directorate implemented a policy amendment that increased the maximum annual reimbursement to two thousand five hundred dollars. Marcus has been employed full-time for three years and submitted all required documentation.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The decision date version sets the limit at two thousand five hundred dollars, which covers the two thousand dollar claim.
criteria.no: The request date version sets the limit at one thousand five hundred dollars, which excludes the two thousand dollar claim.

items.rationale: Clause 2 originally caps reimbursement at $1,500. The amendment effective 1 October 2024 raises it to $2,500. Under instruction A, the pre-amendment limit applies, making the $2,000 claim exceed the cap. Under instruction B, the post-amendment limit applies, placing the claim within the cap.

items.case: On 10 March 2024, employee Sarah Lin submitted a claim for eight hundred dollars covering a twelve-month subscription to a certified sports massage therapy clinic. Sarah has been employed full-time for five years and provided all original receipts and service descriptions. The Benefits Committee reviewed the submission on 20 March 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Massage therapy is functionally similar to the listed physiotherapy and gym categories, qualifying under an illustrative interpretation.
criteria.no: Massage therapy is not explicitly listed among the four qualifying expense categories, disqualifying it under a complete list interpretation.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists four specific categories. Under instruction A, the list is treated as exhaustive, excluding massage therapy. Under instruction B, the list is treated as non-exhaustive, allowing similar wellness expenses to qualify.

items.case: On 12 May 2024, employee David Ross submitted a claim for six hundred dollars covering a one-day professional career development workshop. David has been employed full-time for four years and submitted all required documentation. The Benefits Committee reviewed the submission on 22 May 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the applied instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the applied instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The career development workshop is not a health or family support expense, placing it outside the scope of Clause 2. It also does not trigger the procedural or approval mechanisms of Clauses 3, 4, 5, or 6. Under instruction A, the policy treats uncovered requests as permitted, but the specified correct answer is no; under instruction B, uncovered requests are not permitted, yielding yes.

title: Lumina Festival Group Ticket Refund and Exchange Policy
policy:
1. Ticket holders may request a full refund if the scheduled event date is moved by more than fifteen days after the original purchase date.
2. Holders of general admission tickets may exchange their ticket for a premium seating ticket within thirty days of purchase, provided the premium ticket price does not exceed the original purchase amount by more than fifty dollars.
3. Refund requests submitted for weather-related postponements are processed only when the organiser issues a formal written notice of delay at least forty-eight hours before the event start time.
4. All refund and exchange requests must be submitted through the official customer portal before 17:00 local time on the business day immediately preceding the event.
5. A processing fee of twelve dollars applies to every approved refund or exchange request, deducted from the total reimbursement amount.
6. Requests involving group bookings of six or more tickets are evaluated individually for each ticket in the reservation.
7. The customer service team retains discretion to approve partial refunds for events that proceed but have fewer than half of the advertised performances cancelled.
8. Refunds for tickets purchased with corporate vouchers follow the standard reimbursement schedule outlined in section four.

items.case: Clara Vance purchased a general admission ticket for the Orion Music Festival for eighty dollars. She submitted a request to exchange her ticket for a premium seating ticket priced at one hundred ten dollars. The festival is scheduled for 15 June 2024.
items.question: Is the exchange request permitted?

criteria.yes: The thirty-day exchange window is treated as satisfied, meeting all clause two requirements.
criteria.no: The thirty-day exchange window is treated as not satisfied, failing clause two.

items.rationale: Clause two requires the exchange to occur within thirty days of purchase. The case establishes the ticket type, pricing difference, and event date, but omits the purchase and request dates. Instruction A treats this unstated condition as not satisfied, failing the clause and yielding no. Instruction B treats it as satisfied, meeting all clause requirements and yielding yes.

items.case: On 5 April 2024, David Chen purchased a standard ticket for the Summer Arts Gala for one hundred dollars. On 10 April 2024, he submitted a request to transfer the ticket to his sister's customer account because he can no longer attend. The gala is scheduled for 20 July 2024.
items.question: Is the transfer request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all clauses, and the instruction permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all clauses, and the instruction denies uncovered requests.

items.rationale: The policy addresses date moves, seating exchanges, weather postponements, submission deadlines, fees, group bookings, partial refunds, and corporate vouchers. It contains no clause governing account or name transfers, though clause two covers ticket exchanges. Instruction A permits requests lacking a governing clause, yielding yes. Instruction B denies them, yielding no.

items.case: On 1 February 2024, Elena Rostova submitted a refund request for a ticket to the Coastal Jazz Weekend after the event date was moved by twelve days. The customer service team processed the decision on 15 March 2024. On 10 February 2024, the organisation updated clause one to reduce the required date change threshold from fifteen days to ten days.
items.question: Is the refund request permitted?

criteria.yes: The amended policy version applies, setting a ten-day threshold that the twelve-day shift exceeds.
criteria.no: The original policy version applies, setting a fifteen-day threshold that the twelve-day shift does not meet.

items.rationale: Clause one governs date-change refunds. The case states the threshold was fifteen days on the request date and ten days on the decision date. Instruction A applies the request-date version (fifteen-day threshold), which the twelve-day shift fails, yielding no. Instruction B applies the decision-date version (ten-day threshold), which the twelve-day shift meets, yielding yes.

title: Aether Dynamics Ltd. Export Control Policy
policy:
1. All outbound commercial shipments of dual-use hardware components valued at $50,000 USD or more require a prior export license issued by the Chief Compliance Officer before the goods leave any Aether Dynamics facility.
2. Shipments destined for nations listed in Annex B of the Corporate Restricted Jurisdictions Register are strictly prohibited unless a written waiver is obtained from the Board of Directors prior to dispatch.
3. Any transfer of technical documentation accompanying licensed hardware must include a validated end-user certificate signed by the recipient’s authorized procurement officer and notarized by an independent legal entity.
4. Requests for export authorization must be submitted through the Global Trade Portal at least ten business days before the intended shipment date, accompanied by a completed commercial invoice and packing list.
5. The Chief Compliance Officer may delegate license approval authority to Regional Trade Managers for shipments valued between $50,000 and $150,000 USD, provided the destination is not subject to a comprehensive embargo.
6. All export records, including licenses, waivers, certificates, and correspondence, must be retained in the central archive for a period of seven years following the transaction date and made available for internal audit upon request.

items.case: On 14 March 2024, Elena Rostova requested authorization to ship $75,000 worth of dual-use sensor arrays to a distributor in Lyon, France. The shipment includes a full set of technical manuals. The request was submitted via the Global Trade Portal on 5 March 2024, and the intended dispatch date is 20 March 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated notarized end-user certificate condition is treated as satisfied, meeting all policy requirements.
criteria.no: The unstated notarized end-user certificate condition is treated as not satisfied, failing Clause 3.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires a notarized end-user certificate for technical documentation accompanying licensed hardware. The case establishes the shipment value, destination, documentation inclusion, and portal submission, but leaves the certificate requirement completely unstated. Instruction A treats the unestablished condition as unsatisfied, triggering a prohibition. Instruction B treats the uncontradicted condition as satisfied, allowing the request.

items.case: On 10 October 2024, Marcus Chen submitted a request to export $65,000 worth of dual-use calibration tools to a partner facility in Munich, Germany. The intended shipment date is 30 October 2024. The compliance team scheduled a final authorization decision for 25 October 2024. A policy amendment effective 18 October 2024 revised the licensing threshold in Clause 1 to $80,000 USD.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Applying the post-amendment threshold of $80,000 USD exempts the $65,000 shipment from licensing requirements.
criteria.no: Applying the pre-amendment threshold of $50,000 USD triggers Clause 1, and no prior license is established.

items.rationale: Clause 1 requires a license for shipments at or above $50,000 USD. The case establishes a $65,000 shipment requested on 10 October, with a decision dated 25 October, and notes an amendment on 18 October raising the threshold to $80,000 USD. Instruction A applies the version in force on the request date, making the shipment subject to licensing without an established license. Instruction B applies the version in force on the decision date, exempting the shipment.

items.case: On 12 November 2024, David Park requested authorization to export $35,000 worth of standard commercial office furniture to a corporate subsidiary in Dublin, Ireland. The shipment includes product assembly manuals and a commercial invoice. The intended dispatch date is 20 November 2024.
items.question: Is the request prohibited?

criteria.yes: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the default rule treats uncovered requests as prohibited.
criteria.no: The request falls outside all policy clauses, and the default rule treats uncovered requests as permitted.

items.rationale: The policy exclusively regulates dual-use hardware components, associated technical documentation, and related licensing procedures. The case involves standard commercial office furniture, which is not dual-use hardware, and falls outside Clauses 1 through 6. Clause 3 references technical documentation but explicitly ties it to licensed hardware, leaving the furniture shipment uncovered. Instruction A permits uncovered requests, so the answer is no. Instruction B prohibits them, so the answer is yes.

title: Apex Manufacturing Ltd. Equipment Maintenance Policy
policy:
Apex Manufacturing Ltd. implements the following equipment maintenance standards for all facility operations:
1. All scheduled preventive maintenance on production-line CNC machines must be fully documented and logged in the central tracking system within seven days of completion.
2. Routine calibration of precision measuring instruments requires a signed authorization form from the Quality Assurance Manager before any adjustments are made.
3. Replacement of hydraulic cylinders on automated assembly robots must receive written approval from the Plant Director if the total unit cost exceeds $2,500.
4. Emergency repairs to primary conveyor belts may bypass standard procurement procedures, but a detailed post-incident report must be submitted to operations management within three days of the repair.
5. Operational training records for personnel assigned to overhead cranes must be reviewed and formally verified by the Safety Coordinator every ninety days.
6. Requests for external contractor support require a minimum of five business days’ advance notice to the Procurement Office to allow for vendor scheduling.

items.case: On March 12, technician Lin Chen calibrated the facility’s primary micrometer set. The calibration was completed at 14:00, and all measurement results were within acceptable tolerances. Chen logged the activity in the maintenance database immediately afterward.
items.question: Is the calibration request permitted?

criteria.yes: The unstated authorization condition is treated as satisfied, meeting all policy requirements.
criteria.no: The unstated authorization condition is treated as unmet, violating clause 2.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires a signed authorization form from the Quality Assurance Manager. The case establishes the calibration occurred and was logged, but neither establishes nor contradicts whether Chen obtained the required form. Under Instruction A, this unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, making the request impermissible. Under Instruction B, it is treated as satisfied, making the request permissible.

items.case: On Friday, May 12, a primary conveyor belt suffered a sudden drive motor failure. The emergency repair was completed at 16:30. The operations supervisor submitted the required post-incident report on Tuesday, May 16.
items.question: Is the report submission compliant with the policy?

criteria.yes: Counting the interval in calendar days places the submission within the three-day limit.
criteria.no: Counting the interval in business days places the submission outside the three-day limit.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires submission within three days. The interval from Friday May 12 to Tuesday May 16 spans four calendar days but only two business days. Under Instruction A, counting the period in business days treats the elapsed time as exceeding the three-day threshold, yielding non-compliance. Under Instruction B, counting in calendar days treats the elapsed time as falling within the threshold, yielding compliance.

items.case: On April 5, operator Maria Santos requested routine brake pad replacement for the facility’s warehouse forklift fleet. The total parts cost is $850, and the work is scheduled for the upcoming weekend shift.
items.question: Is the maintenance request permitted?

criteria.yes: No policy clause explicitly covers forklift maintenance, and the instruction permits uncovered requests.
criteria.no: No policy clause explicitly covers forklift maintenance, and the instruction prohibits uncovered requests.

items.rationale: The policy explicitly covers CNC machines, measuring instruments, assembly robots, conveyor belts, overhead cranes, and external contractors. Forklift maintenance falls outside every clause, though it resembles material-handling equipment that might appear related to cranes or robots. Under Instruction A, requests not covered by any clause are permitted, yielding yes. Under Instruction B, they are not permitted, yielding no.

title: Vertex Dynamics IT Access Control Policy
policy:
1. All Vertex Dynamics personnel requesting elevated privileges for the Orion database must submit a written justification to the IT Security Office detailing the intended use case and expected duration.
2. Requests for administrative access to customer financial records are approved only when the requester holds a Senior Analyst title or higher.
3. Junior staff members may receive administrative access to any database for emergency incident response, provided the access period does not exceed forty-eight hours.
4. Access to systems containing proprietary engineering schematics, such as CAD repositories and version control servers, requires a cleared security badge and dual-factor authentication linked to a corporate email address.
5. Temporary access tokens for external vendor portals expire after seventy-two hours unless renewed by the procurement department.
6. This policy was originally issued on 10 March 2023. An amendment effective 15 August 2024 updates Clause 5 to reduce the expiration period from seventy-two hours to twenty-four hours.

items.case: On 12 May 2024, Marcus Chen, a Junior Systems Administrator at Vertex Dynamics, submitted a ticket requesting administrative access to the Orion customer financial database to resolve a critical payment processing outage. The IT Security Office processed the request on 13 May 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governing emergency incident response overrides the general title requirement, allowing junior staff temporary admin access.
criteria.no: The stricter clause prohibiting admin access to financial records for non-Senior Analysts overrides the emergency exception, denying the request.

items.rationale: Clause 2 denies access due to the requester's junior title, while Clause 3 permits it due to the emergency context. Under instruction A, the stricter denial prevails. Under instruction B, the more specific emergency exception prevails.

items.case: On 5 June 2024, Elena Rostova, a Senior Mechanical Engineer at Vertex Dynamics, requested system access to the company's product lifecycle management database to review historical assembly diagrams. She possesses a cleared security badge and dual-factor authentication linked to her corporate email.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The product lifecycle management database is functionally similar to the listed examples and falls under the schematics access requirement.
criteria.no: The product lifecycle management database is not explicitly listed in the examples, and the list is treated as exhaustive.

items.rationale: Clause 4 lists CAD repositories and version control servers as examples of systems containing schematics. The requested PLM database is not listed but serves the same purpose. Under instruction A, only listed systems qualify. Under instruction B, similar systems qualify.

items.case: On 10 August 2024, Sarah Lin requested a temporary access token for the Apex vendor portal to complete a project scheduled to last three days. The IT Security Office approved and issued the token on 20 August 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The original seventy-two-hour expiration rule applies, which covers the requested three-day duration.
criteria.no: The amended twenty-four-hour expiration rule applies, which is shorter than the requested three-day duration.

items.rationale: Clause 5 originally allowed 72-hour tokens but was amended to 24 hours on 15 August 2024. The request was made before the amendment, but the decision occurred after. Under instruction A, the pre-amendment rule applies, permitting the three-day token. Under instruction B, the post-amendment rule applies, denying it.

title: Meridian Logistics Ltd. Fleet Allocation Policy
policy:
1. All fleet vehicle requests must be submitted to the Transport Coordinator, Sarah Jenkins, at least forty-eight hours before the intended start date.
2. Standard passenger vans may be allocated for up to five consecutive days per calendar month without additional approval.
3. Requests for heavy goods vehicles exceeding 3.5 tonnes require prior written authorisation from the Fleet Manager, David Chen.
4. No fleet vehicle may be allocated for more than three consecutive days without manager sign-off.
5. Fuel card transactions exceeding ninety pounds per day must be reconciled with a scanned receipt within three working days of the transaction date.
6. Vehicles may not be used for private journeys unless the driver holds a valid personal use permit issued by Human Resources.
7. Emergency breakdown replacements are authorised automatically by the system when a fault code is logged.
8. All policy interpretations regarding fleet allocations remain subject to final review by the Operations Director, Maria Lopez.

items.case: Tom Briggs requests reimbursement for a fuel card transaction of £110 without submitting a scanned receipt. The request was submitted on 10 April 2024. The decision is made on 25 April 2024. The policy was amended on 15 April 2024 to raise the daily fuel threshold from £90 to £130.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The applicable policy version sets the daily threshold above £110, removing the receipt requirement.
criteria.no: The applicable policy version sets the daily threshold at £90, requiring a scanned receipt for transactions over that amount.

items.rationale: Clause 5 sets a £90 threshold requiring receipts. Under Instruction A, the version on the request date (10 April) applies, keeping the threshold at £90; £110 exceeds it, so the request without a receipt is denied. Under Instruction B, the version on the decision date (25 April) applies, reflecting the 15 April amendment raising the threshold to £130; £110 falls below it, so the receipt is not required and the request is approved.

items.case: Elena Ross requests a standard passenger van for four consecutive days starting 12 May 2024. She submits the request to Sarah Jenkins forty-eight hours in advance and does not seek manager sign-off.
items.question: Is the allocation request permitted?

criteria.yes: The more specific clause governs, allowing up to five consecutive days for passenger vans.
criteria.no: The stricter clause governs, limiting all allocations to three consecutive days without sign-off.

items.rationale: Clause 2 permits passenger vans for up to five days, while Clause 4 limits all vehicles to three days without sign-off. These clauses conflict for this case. Clause 4 is stricter (three days), while Clause 2 is more specific (passenger vans). Under Instruction A, the stricter Clause 4 applies, capping allocation at three days, so the four-day request is denied. Under Instruction B, the more specific Clause 2 applies, allowing up to five days, so the four-day request is approved.

items.case: Mark Lin requests a company-branded roof sign for his allocated electric delivery van. The request is submitted to Sarah Jenkins with all standard forms completed.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses roof signs, and the applicable instruction treats uncovered requests as permitted.
criteria.no: No clause addresses roof signs, and the applicable instruction treats uncovered requests as not permitted.

items.rationale: The policy covers submission timing, allocation duration, heavy goods authorisation, fuel receipts, private use, breakdowns, and director review. It contains no clause governing exterior vehicle modifications like roof signs. Clause 6 regarding private journeys is nearby in theme but does not cover branding. Because the request falls outside every clause, the outcome depends entirely on the appended instruction. Under Instruction A, the outcome is no. Under Instruction B, the outcome is yes.

title: Meridian Health Partners Clinical Scheduling Protocol
policy:
1. All appointment requests for outpatient services at Meridian Health Partners must be submitted through the central scheduling portal no later than forty-eight hours prior to the desired start time. Submissions received after this window will be queued for the next available cycle.
2. Standard consultation slots are limited to forty-five minutes. Requests exceeding this duration must be classified as extended assessments and require prior authorization from a department lead.
3. A scheduling request is automatically denied if the requested reason is listed below: duplicate follow-ups, administrative paperwork reviews, and non-clinical facility tours.
4. Priority booking overrides standard wait times only when the patient presents a documented acute exacerbation of a chronic condition and the request is submitted before 09:00 on a business day.
5. Requests are automatically rejected if the patient has outstanding balances exceeding $50. Cancellations or rescheduling within twelve hours incur a $75 administrative fee.
6. The scheduling coordinator retains final discretion to adjust slot assignments based on clinician availability, provided patient safety standards are maintained.

items.case: On November 12, 2024, administrative staff member Elena Rostova submitted a scheduling request to book a ninety-minute orientation walkthrough for new clinical residents at the Meridian Health Partners downtown clinic. The request was entered into the portal at 14:00 on November 10, 2024, and included a $0 administrative deposit.
items.question: Is the scheduling request permitted under the policy?

criteria.no: The request reason is similar to a listed denial reason, and under the instruction, the list is illustrative, so similar reasons are also denied.

Under A, the list is complete, so only the exact listed reasons are denied; the request is permitted. Under B, the list is illustrative, so similar reasons are also denied; the request is not permitted.

items.question: Is the request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: No clause addresses cross-branch transfers, and under the instruction, uncovered requests are permitted.
criteria.no: No clause addresses cross-branch transfers, and under the instruction, uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.rationale: The policy covers submission timing, duration limits, denial reasons, priority booking, and cancellation fees. It does not address inter-branch transfers. Clause 5 covers cancellations/rescheduling, which might seem nearby, but the case explicitly involves a branch transfer without cancellation or rescheduling of the time slot itself. Under A, uncovered requests are permitted. Under B, uncovered requests are not permitted.

items.case: On April 10, 2024, patient Sarah Lin requested to schedule a standard forty-minute consultation for April 15. She submitted the request at 10:00 on April 12, 2024, and referenced a $200 service estimate. Her account balance status was not mentioned in the submission.
items.question: Is the scheduling request permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The case does not establish the outstanding balance condition, and under the instruction, unproven conditions are treated as not satisfied, so the rejection clause is not triggered.
criteria.no: The case does not contradict the outstanding balance condition, and under the instruction, unproven conditions are treated as satisfied, so the rejection clause is triggered.

Under A, the condition is treated as not satisfied, so the request is not rejected and is permitted. Under B, the condition is treated as satisfied, so the request is rejected and not permitted.

title: Veridian Home Goods Customer Refund and Return Policy
policy:
1. All refund requests must include the original purchase receipt and a valid government-issued photo ID matching the purchaser name.
2. All return requests submitted after fourteen days from purchase are rejected.
3. Custom-ordered furniture, engraved accessories, and personalized apparel are excluded from standard return eligibility.
4. Items showing visible wear, physical damage, or missing hardware will receive a partial refund or store credit only, at the discretion of the processing clerk.
5. Returns of camping equipment are accepted for processing.
6. High-value electronics exceeding two hundred dollars require a manufacturer inspection report before processing, and the report must be stamped by an authorized technician.
7. All returned items must be in their original packaging to qualify for a cash or card refund.
8. Refunds for group purchases are processed individually based on each item’s original payment method, and transaction logs must be retained for audit purposes.

items.case: Elena Rostova purchased a monogrammed leather wallet on October 5, 2023. She requests a full refund on October 20, 2023, presenting the original receipt and valid photo ID. The wallet shows no signs of wear and is in its original packaging.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The monogrammed wallet is not explicitly listed in clause three, so under a complete-list interpretation it qualifies for a standard refund.
criteria.no: The monogrammed wallet is clearly similar to the engraved and personalized items listed in clause three, so under an illustrative-list interpretation it falls under the exclusion.

items.rationale: Clause three lists excluded items without specifying whether the list is exhaustive. Instruction A treats the list as complete, meaning only the listed items are excluded, so the similar but unlisted wallet qualifies. Instruction B treats the list as illustrative, meaning similar items like the monogrammed wallet are also excluded.

items.case: Marcus Chen returns a set of camping equipment on day twenty of the purchase period. He submits the original receipt and valid photo ID. The equipment is in its original packaging and shows no damage.
items.question: Is the return rejected?

criteria.yes: Clause two imposes a strict fourteen-day limit that rejects the return, and under the stricter-clause rule it overrides the other provision.
criteria.no: Clause five specifically addresses camping equipment and accepts it, and under the more-specific-clause rule it overrides the general time limit.

items.rationale: Clause two (rejects after fourteen days) and clause five (accepts camping equipment) conflict for a day-twenty camping equipment return. Clause two is stricter regarding the refund outcome, while clause five is more specific regarding the product category. Instruction A applies the stricter clause, triggering rejection. Instruction B applies the more specific clause, triggering acceptance.

items.case: Sarah Lin requests a refund for a standard kitchen mixer purchased on November 1, 2023. She submits the request on November 10, 2023, and provides the original purchase receipt. The mixer is in its original packaging and shows no damage.
items.question: Is the refund request denied?

criteria.yes: The case does not establish that a valid photo ID was provided, so under the unproven-as-false rule the mandatory condition fails and the request is denied.
criteria.no: The case does not contradict the presence of a valid photo ID, so under the unproven-as-true rule the mandatory condition is met and the request proceeds.

items.rationale: Clause one requires both a receipt and a matching photo ID. The case confirms the receipt but leaves the photo ID unstated. Instruction A treats unestablished conditions as unsatisfied, so the missing ID triggers denial. Instruction B treats uncontradicted conditions as satisfied, so the assumed ID allows the request to proceed.

title: Veridian Systems IT Access Control Policy
policy:
1. All personnel requesting access to the Veridian Systems production database must submit a standard form to the IT Security Office at least 48 hours before the intended start date, including a detailed justification statement.
2. Access to customer financial records is permitted for any employee who has completed advanced data handling training.
3. Access to customer financial records for employees in the Sales division is denied pending annual review.
4. Temporary access granted for system maintenance must not exceed 72 hours and requires a ticket logged in the service portal by a certified engineer, with automatic revocation upon expiry.
5. Access to legacy reporting tools is restricted to staff members who completed the compliance training module prior to October 1, 2023, and remains valid for one calendar year from the grant date.
6. Any request involving cross-departmental data sharing must include a signed data processing agreement and is subject to a 10-business-day review period by the corporate legal team.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, junior developer Aris Thorne submitted a ticket requesting read-only access to the archived project files repository for a historical audit. The IT desk reviewed the request on March 14, 2024.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

title: Apex Shield Mutual Claims Processing Guidelines

title: Veridian Mutual Insurance Home Contents Claims Policy
policy:
1. This policy governs claims for damaged or stolen personal property under Veridian Mutual Insurance Home Contents plans. Eligible claimants must hold an active policy at the time of loss and reside within the insured address.

4. Approved claims are paid via direct deposit to the account on file. Payments exceeding five thousand dollars require secondary review by the regional underwriting manager before disbursement.
5. Claims are denied if the loss results from intentional damage, normal wear and tear, or events occurring while the property was unoccupied for more than sixty consecutive days. Claims for single-item losses exceeding five thousand dollars are excluded from coverage. All claims are subject to the deductible specified in the original contract.

title: Meridian Gear Co. Standard Warranty Policy

title: Verdant Goods Co. Customer Refund and Return Guidelines
policy:
1. All refund requests must be submitted to the Customer Care desk within 10 days of the original purchase date. Late submissions will be automatically declined unless extenuating circumstances are documented.
2. Items returned in their original packaging with a valid receipt are eligible for a full refund up to the purchase price. Partial refunds may be issued if accessories are missing.

5. Portable computing devices purchased for educational use are exempt from the hardware inspection form requirement and qualify for immediate processing upon receipt verification. This streamlines support for academic institutions.
6. If a returned item shows signs of heavy use or damage beyond normal testing, the refund amount will be reduced by 40% to cover refurbishment costs. Customers will be notified of any deductions prior to payment.
7. Requests involving promotional bundles must be evaluated based on the individual item values rather than the discounted bundle total. This prevents overpayment when only one component is returned.

2. Emergency aisles and fire exits must remain unobstructed at all times. Any temporary storage within three metres of an exit requires a written clearance permit issued by Safety Manager Elena Rostova.
3. Any inventory movement exceeding 100 units is authorised only when logged in the central tracking system prior to execution. Verbal authorisations are invalid for batches of this size, and digital timestamps serve as the primary record.
4. Forklift operators must complete the quarterly refresher course by 30 September each year. Failure to submit proof of completion suspends operating privileges until the next cycle begins.
5. Movements of fragile glassware exceeding 100 units are prohibited on Fridays to accommodate facility maintenance schedules and reduce collision risks.
6. High-visibility vests are mandatory when operating powered industrial equipment listed below: reach trucks, pallet jacks, and order pickers. Contractors are subject to the same standard.
7. Damaged packaging must be segregated immediately upon discovery. Items with compromised seals or structural deformation shall be moved to the quarantine bay and reported to Shift Supervisor Marcus Thorne within two hours.

items.case: On 14 June 2024, logistics clerk David Chen moves 150 units of decorative glassware from the receiving dock to the staging area. The transfer is logged in the central tracking system at 09:15, but no facility maintenance crew is present that day.
items.question: Is the transfer permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 3 (stricter/general) applies; the movement exceeds 100 units and was logged, satisfying the authorisation requirement.
criteria.no: Clause 5 (more specific) applies; the movement involves glassware exceeding 100 units on a Friday, which is explicitly prohibited.

items.rationale: Clauses 3 and 5 both apply but yield opposite outcomes. Clause 3 is stricter because it applies to all inventory over 100 units and mandates logging. Clause 5 is more specific because it targets only glassware on Fridays. Under instruction A, the stricter clause governs, so the logged status permits the move. Under instruction B, the more specific clause governs, so the Friday glassware restriction prohibits it.

items.case: On 20 April 2024, warehouse associate Sarah Jenkins places three pallets of cardboard boxes two metres from Exit 7 to await loading. The pallets are secured with straps and do not block the doorway.
items.question: Is the storage arrangement compliant?

criteria.yes: The unstated permit requirement is treated as satisfied under the given instruction.
criteria.no: The unstated permit requirement is treated as not satisfied under the given instruction.

items.rationale: Clause 2 requires a written clearance permit from Elena Rostova for any storage within three metres of an exit. The case establishes the distance (two metres) but leaves the permit status entirely unstated. Under instruction A, the unproven condition is treated as not satisfied, making the arrangement non-compliant. Under instruction B, the unproven condition is treated as satisfied, making it compliant.
