Instruction B applies the version on the decision date (July), using the $3,000 threshold, so authorisation is required (no).

title: Emergency Equipment Replacement Protocol
policy:
1. This protocol governs all field technicians and maintenance supervisors operating within the Oakridge Industrial Park jurisdiction, effective March 1, 2024.
2. Any equipment component costing more than $800 requires prior written authorization from the Site Manager.
3. Components priced at $800 or less may be procured immediately if they fall under critical operational hardware, such as hydraulic pumps, primary drive motors, and main control boards.
4. Technicians must submit a digital service report within forty-eight hours of installation, documenting the failure mode, replacement part serial number, and operational test results. This requirement is waived if the replacement occurs during a certified site-wide power outage.
5. The monthly emergency maintenance budget for each facility is strictly limited to $6,000. Any replacement that pushes the facility's monthly emergency spend above this limit must be approved by the Finance Director before procurement.
6. All replaced components must be returned to the central warehouse within five business days for vendor warranty claims.

items.question: Is prior written authorization required for this request?

criteria.no: The list in clause 3 is treated as illustrative; the transformer is clearly similar critical hardware, qualifying for immediate procurement and negating the authorization requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 3 governs immediate procurement for parts at or below $800, listing specific examples. Under instruction A, the list is complete; the transformer is absent, so the immediate procurement exception fails and clause 2's authorization requirement applies. Under instruction B, the list is illustrative; the transformer is functionally similar to the listed critical hardware, so the immediate procurement exception applies and authorization is not required.

Under instruction B, the uncontradicted certification is treated as satisfied, triggering the waiver and making the report optional.

criteria.no: The stricter clause requiring additional oversight for budget overages prevails, blocking immediate procurement.

The $750 valve pushes the total to $6,550, creating a direct conflict. Under instruction A, the stricter clause (clause 5, mandating extra approval) controls, so immediate procurement is denied. Under instruction B, the more specific clause (clause 2, directly targeting the individual part cost threshold) controls, so immediate procurement is allowed.

title: GlobalTech Solutions Employee Wellness Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. Eligibility: Full-time employees employed by GlobalTech Solutions for at least six months may submit claims for wellness-related expenses. Part-time contractors and temporary staff are excluded.
2. Covered Expenses: The company will reimburse costs for fitness memberships, yoga classes, and meditation app subscriptions. Claims must be submitted with a valid receipt showing the vendor, date, and amount.
3. Submission Window: Employees must submit their reimbursement requests within fifteen days of the service date. Late submissions will not be processed.
4. Approval Process: All claims are reviewed by the HR Benefits Coordinator, currently held by Elena Rostova. Elena will verify eligibility, receipt validity, and submission timing before authorizing payment.
5. Payment Terms: Approved amounts up to $250 per calendar quarter will be deposited directly into the employee’s payroll account. Requests exceeding this limit require prior written approval from the Chief Financial Officer.
6. Verification Requirement: Before payment is released, the employee must have completed the mandatory online wellness orientation module hosted on the company intranet. Failure to complete this module prior to claim approval will result in automatic deferral until compliance is achieved.

title: Crestview Hospitality Group Reservation Policy
policy:
1. Crestview Hospitality Group manages all room bookings through its central reservation system. Guests may secure accommodations by phone, email, or the official online portal. All bookings require a valid credit card on file.
2. Complimentary early check-in is permitted for Deluxe suite reservations confirmed at least forty-eight hours before arrival. This service is denied if the guest has previously cancelled a reservation within the past twelve months.
3. Pet deposits are waived for service animals, including guide dogs, hearing dogs, and psychiatric support animals. All other animals require a non-refundable deposit of one hundred fifty dollars per stay.
4. Advance reservations may be made up to twelve months prior to the check-in date. Amendment Note: Effective 10 November 2023, the maximum advance booking period was increased from six months to twelve months. Prior to this date, the six-month limit applied.
5. Cancellations submitted more than forty-eight hours before arrival receive a full refund. Cancellations within the forty-eight-hour window are subject to a one-night charge.
6. Management reserves the right to adjust room assignments based on availability and maintenance schedules without altering the agreed rate.
7. All rates quoted are per night and exclude applicable local taxes and mandatory resort fees. Guests are responsible for verifying total costs before confirming payment.

criteria.no: The policy permits early check-in for Deluxe suites confirmed 48 hours prior, but the unstated prior cancellation condition is treated as satisfied, triggering the denial provision.

Under instruction A, the unstated condition is treated as not satisfied, so the denial does not apply and the request is permitted. Under instruction B, the unstated condition is treated as satisfied, so the denial applies and the request is not permitted.

criteria.no: The policy waives deposits for service animals, but the complete list does not include diabetic alert dogs, so the waiver does not apply.

The case involves a diabetic alert dog, which is not listed but is functionally similar. Under instruction A, the list is treated as complete, so only the listed animals qualify and the waiver is denied. Under instruction B, the list is treated as illustrative, so the similar diabetic alert dog qualifies and the waiver is permitted.

criteria.no: The policy version on the request date limits bookings to six months in advance, and the seven-month lead time exceeds this limit.

The case involves a seven-month lead time, with a request date before the amendment and a decision date after it. Under instruction A, the pre-amendment six-month limit applies, exceeding which denies the request. Under instruction B, the post-amendment twelve-month limit applies, within which the request is permitted.

title: Verdant Dynamics Employee Wellness Reimbursement Policy
policy:
1. The Verdant Dynamics Employee Wellness Program provides quarterly reimbursements for qualifying health and dependent care expenses. All full-time and part-time staff employed for at least ninety days are eligible to participate.
2. Eligible expenses include routine medical consultations, prescribed therapeutic equipment, and certified childcare services. Claims must be submitted with original receipts and a completed benefits form.
3. Claims must be submitted within thirty days of the service date. Submissions received after this period are declined.
4. The maximum reimbursement per calendar quarter is four hundred dollars. Any unused balance does not roll over to subsequent quarters. Requests exceeding the limit are reduced to the quarterly maximum.
5. This policy was originally effective on 1 January 2023. An amendment published on 15 March 2024 updated the quarterly maximum to five hundred dollars.
6. The benefits administration team will review each submission and issue a decision within fourteen days of receipt. Approved claims are processed for payment, while incomplete submissions are returned to the employee for correction.

criteria.no: The submission falls outside the thirty-day window when counted in calendar days.

criteria.no: The chair does not appear in the listed examples and therefore does not qualify.

Instruction A applies the pre-amendment limit in force on the request date, capping approval at four hundred dollars. Instruction B applies the post-amendment limit in force on the decision date, allowing the full four hundred fifty dollars.

title: Meridian Arts Festival Ticketing Policy
policy:
1. The Festival Ticketing Office manages all sales, exchanges, and refunds for events held at the Meridian Pavilion between May 1, 2024, and October 30, 2024. All transactions are final unless explicitly modified by subsequent clauses.
2. The Early Supporter discount of fifteen percent applies to tickets for chamber music recitals, poetry readings, and solo dance performances. This discount must be claimed at checkout and cannot be combined with other promotional codes.
3. All ticket transfers submitted through the online portal are subject to a twenty-dollar administrative processing fee. This fee covers system updates and confirmation notifications.
4. Transfers for tickets originally priced above one hundred fifty dollars are subject to a ten-dollar administrative processing fee. These higher-tier transfers are routed through the premium support queue.
5. Digital ticket modifications, including seat swaps and time changes, are permitted up to twenty-four hours before the scheduled start time of the performance. Requests submitted after this window will be declined by the automated system.
6. Physical ticket replacements for lost or damaged items are available at the main box office until the event begins. Patrons must present valid government identification and a copy of the original purchase receipt to receive a replacement.
7. The Festival reserves the right to deny service to individuals whose requests violate venue capacity limits or local safety ordinances.

items.case: On June 12, 2024, patron Elena Rostova purchases a ticket for a jazz trio concert at the Meridian Pavilion and applies the Early Supporter discount at checkout. The ticket base price is fifty-three dollars.
items.question: Is the discount request denied?

criteria.no: The jazz trio concert is similar to the listed categories, and treating the list as illustrative means similar items qualify, so the discount is permitted.

items.rationale: Clause 2 lists three specific event types. Instruction A treats the list as exhaustive, excluding the jazz trio concert and resulting in denial. Instruction B treats the list as non-exhaustive, allowing the similar jazz trio concert to qualify and resulting in permission.

criteria.no: Clause 4 specifically addresses tickets priced above one hundred fifty dollars, which is more specific than clause 3. Applying the more specific clause means a ten-dollar fee is charged instead.

criteria.no: The request falls outside the twenty-four-hour window in clause 5 and is not covered by any other clause. Instruction B prohibits requests that fall outside all clauses.

items.rationale: Clause 5 covers digital modifications but only up to twenty-four hours before the event. A forty-eight-hour request is uncovered. Instruction A defaults uncovered requests to permitted, while Instruction B defaults them to not permitted.

title: Veridian Supply Co. Procurement Authorization Guidelines
policy:
Document Control: Original effective January 1, 2024. Amended May 15, 2024 (Clause 3 monetary threshold adjusted to $2,000).
1. All purchase requests exceeding $5,000 must be submitted to the Procurement Office at least 10 days before the required delivery date to allow for standard vendor onboarding.
2. Requests for IT hardware between $2,000 and $5,000 require written approval from the Department Head and must be logged in the central registry within 5 days of vendor selection.
3. Emergency procurement requests under $3,000 may be processed immediately by any senior buyer, provided a post-purchase justification form is filed within 3 days.
4. Contracts involving recurring annual services valued above $10,000 require a competitive quote from at least three suppliers and final sign-off by the Chief Financial Officer.
5. All vendor payments for goods delivered must be scheduled no later than 15 days after the invoice date, unless a net-30 term is explicitly negotiated in writing.
6. Requests for custom manufacturing projects exceeding $8,000 must include a detailed scope of work and be reviewed by the Quality Assurance team before submission.

criteria.no: The request amount exceeds the monetary threshold of the policy version effective on the reference date.

title: Aethelgard Data Systems Information Security Incident Policy
policy:
1. Purpose and Scope: This policy establishes mandatory procedures for identifying, reporting, and managing information security incidents at Aethelgard Data Systems. All staff, contractors, and third-party vendors with system access must adhere to these requirements.
2. Incident Classification: An event qualifies as a Critical incident if it involves unauthorized access to restricted information assets, such as customer personally identifiable information, proprietary source code, and cryptographic keys, or if the projected remediation cost exceeds $50,000.
3. Reporting Obligations: Any individual who identifies a Critical incident must file an initial notification with the Incident Response Team within 4 days of becoming aware of the event. Failure to meet this deadline requires a formal exemption request submitted to the Chief Information Security Officer.
4. Containment and Analysis: Upon receiving a notification, the Incident Response Team will isolate affected systems and begin forensic analysis. No data may be permanently deleted or overwritten during this phase without explicit written authorization from the team lead.
5. External Disclosure: Communications with regulators, law enforcement, or affected clients must be coordinated exclusively through the legal department. Unauthorized external statements regarding an active investigation are strictly prohibited.
6. Policy Maintenance: This document is subject to periodic revision. Updates are published on the corporate compliance intranet and become operative immediately upon posting. Historical revisions are archived for audit purposes.

items.case: On Monday, 1 January 2024, a security analyst detected unauthorized access to a staging server. The preliminary report was submitted on Friday, 5 January 2024.
items.question: Is the submission within the required reporting timeline?

criteria.yes: The elapsed time between discovery and submission does not exceed the policy period.
criteria.no: The elapsed time between discovery and submission exceeds the policy period.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the gap spans five business days, which exceeds the four-day limit. Under instruction B, the gap spans four calendar days, which meets the four-day limit.

items.case: On 14 June 2024, a developer accidentally committed a database dump containing internal employee health records to a public repository. The estimated remediation cost is $12,000. The initial notification was filed on 17 June 2024.
items.question: Is the event classified as a Critical incident under the policy?

criteria.yes: The compromised data type qualifies under the incident classification clause.
criteria.no: The compromised data type does not qualify under the incident classification clause.

items.rationale: Instruction A treats the listed data types as exhaustive, excluding health records. Instruction B treats the list as illustrative, allowing similarly sensitive personal data to qualify.

items.case: On 10 March 2024, a manager requested classification for a data leak that incurred $60,000 in cleanup costs. The compliance committee issued its decision on 20 March 2024. The financial threshold in this policy was amended from $50,000 to $75,000 on 15 March 2024.
items.question: Does the incident qualify as Critical under the applicable policy version?

criteria.yes: The incident meets the financial threshold of the governing policy version.
criteria.no: The incident fails to meet the financial threshold of the governing policy version.

items.rationale: Instruction A applies the 10 March version with a $50,000 threshold, making the $60,000 cost qualify. Instruction B applies the 20 March version with a $75,000 threshold, excluding the $60,000 cost.

title: Aethelgard Clinical Partners Scheduling Policy
policy:
1. All elective procedure requests must be submitted to the Aethelgard Clinical Partners Central Scheduling Desk at least 10 days prior to the intended procedure date to ensure adequate operating room allocation, equipment sterilization, and staff rostering.
2. Requests originating from principal investigators may bypass the standard notice requirement if the procedure is designated for an active clinical trial and includes a verified authorization code from the research ethics board.
3. All scheduling requests must include a fully completed Standard Intake Form to be processed by the administrative team without delay.
4. Requests for routine follow-up appointments must include a signed physician referral letter to validate the clinical necessity of the visit and confirm continuity of care.
5. Pursuant to the administrative review completed in October 2024, the standard notice requirement for elective procedures is updated to 5 days, effective 1 November 2024.
6. The Scheduling Desk must issue a confirmation or rejection for all routine requests within 5 days of submission, or a $150 administrative fee applies.

items.case: Dr. Vance submits a routine elective request on Friday, 12 January 2024. The Scheduling Desk issues its decision on Thursday, 18 January 2024.
items.question: Is the decision issued within the required timeframe?

criteria.yes: The elapsed time meets the policy's 5-day limit under the specified counting method.
criteria.no: The elapsed time exceeds the policy's 5-day limit under the specified counting method.

items.rationale: Counting business days yields 4 days (Monday 15 to Thursday 18), which satisfies the 5-day limit (yes). Counting calendar days yields 6 days, which exceeds the limit (no).

items.case: Dr. Chen submits an elective procedure request on 15 October 2024 for an appointment on 23 October 2024. The Scheduling Desk processes the request and issues its decision on 5 November 2024.
items.question: Is the scheduling request permitted?

criteria.yes: The notice period satisfies the policy version in force on the decision date.
criteria.no: The notice period fails the policy version in force on the request date.

items.rationale: Applying the pre-amendment version (10-day rule) on the request date renders the 8-day notice insufficient (no). Applying the post-amendment version (5-day rule) on the decision date renders the 8-day notice sufficient (yes).

items.case: Dr. Evans submits a routine follow-up request with a completed Standard Intake Form but without a signed physician referral letter.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The request satisfies the stricter documentation requirement.
criteria.no: The request fails the specific documentation requirement.

items.rationale: Clause 3 requires only the Standard Intake Form, which is present, satisfying the stricter general rule (yes). Clause 4 specifically mandates a signed referral letter for follow-ups, which is absent, failing the specific rule (no).

title: Lumina Cloud Services Subscription Adjustment Policy
policy:
1. All subscription modifications must be submitted in writing to Account Manager Sarah Jenkins and reference the active contract number. Requests lacking a valid contract identifier will be returned without processing.
2. Mid-cycle plan downgrades are processed automatically with a prorated credit applied to the next invoice. The credit calculation excludes any unused add-on licenses or third-party integrations.
3. Requests for mid-cycle cancellations are denied to maintain service continuity and billing stability. This restriction applies regardless of the remaining term length or payment status.
4. Cancellations initiated by enterprise clients on annual contracts are permitted with a prorated refund issued within ten business days. The refund amount is calculated based on the daily rate of the base subscription tier.
5. Waivers for early termination fees are available for clients experiencing documented business disruptions, including server outages, regulatory shutdowns, and natural disasters. Documentation must be submitted alongside the waiver request.
6. All billing adjustments exceeding $500 require written authorization from Finance Director Elena Rostova before execution. Unauthorized adjustments will be reversed at the end of the fiscal quarter.
7. Elena Rostova retains final discretion on any adjustment that impacts annual recurring revenue by more than $2,000. Decisions under this clause are final and not subject to standard appeal procedures.

items.case: On 2023-10-15, GlobalTech Corp submitted a request to Lumina Cloud Services to cancel their mid-cycle subscription. The Finance team scheduled a decision review for 2023-11-20. The request amount is $450.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy version effective on 2023-10-15 contained a clause permitting mid-cycle cancellations with a standard fee.
criteria.no: The policy version effective on 2023-11-20 contains Clause 3, which denies all mid-cycle cancellations.

items.rationale: The policy was amended on 2023-11-01, changing the mid-cycle cancellation rule from permitted to denied. Applying the version in force on the request date (2023-10-15) yields yes. Applying the version in force on the decision date (2023-11-20) yields no.

items.case: On 2024-01-10, Apex Manufacturing submitted a request to Lumina Cloud Services to cancel their mid-cycle subscription. Apex holds an enterprise client status and is on an annual contract. The requested refund amount is $1,200.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 4 specifically permits cancellations for enterprise clients on annual contracts.
criteria.no: Clause 3 strictly denies all mid-cycle cancellations regardless of client tier or contract type.

items.rationale: Clause 3 (general denial) and Clause 4 (enterprise annual permission) conflict. Clause 3 is stricter because it imposes a blanket denial. Clause 4 is more specific because it targets a defined client tier and contract type. Under instruction A, the stricter clause applies, resulting in no. Under instruction B, the more specific clause applies, resulting in yes.

items.case: On 2024-02-05, RetailCo submitted a request to Lumina Cloud Services for a waiver of early termination fees. The company cites a sudden, industry-wide supply chain collapse that halted all retail operations. The waiver amount is $800.
items.question: Is the request denied?

criteria.yes: A supply chain collapse is not explicitly listed in the examples in Clause 5, so it does not qualify under a complete list interpretation.
criteria.no: A supply chain collapse constitutes a business disruption similar to the listed examples, so it qualifies under an illustrative interpretation.

items.rationale: Clause 5 lists server outages, regulatory shutdowns, and natural disasters as examples of qualifying disruptions. The case involves a supply chain collapse, which is similar but not listed. Treating the list as complete means only listed items qualify, so the waiver is denied (yes). Treating the list as illustrative means similar disruptions qualify, so the waiver is permitted (no).

title: Oakhaven Municipal Authority Temporary Sidewalk Closure Policy
policy:
1. All requests for temporary sidewalk closures exceeding ten square metres must be submitted to the Oakhaven Municipal Authority at least thirty days prior to the proposed start date. Submissions lacking a completed site plan will be returned without review.
2. Applications for closures involving commercial food service require a separate health inspection waiver and incur a processing fee of $150, payable upon submission. The authority reserves the right to request additional documentation for high-traffic zones.
3. Any closure extending beyond a single calendar day is subject to a daily surcharge of $75, calculated from the first day of the approved closure through the final day. This surcharge applies regardless of the total square metreage.
4. Requests submitted by residents of the immediate block are exempt from the processing fee described in clause 2, provided the closure does not obstruct emergency vehicle access. Resident applications must include a signed neighbourhood notification form.
5. The processing fee for commercial food service was $100 until November 15, 2023, and is $150 thereafter. Historical fee schedules remain on file for administrative reference.

items.case: On March 12, 2024, resident Elena Rostova submitted a permit request for a 15-square-metre sidewalk closure to operate a weekend artisan food stall. The proposed layout does not block emergency access routes.
items.question: Is the processing fee required for this request?

criteria.yes: Stricter clause (clause 2) mandates the fee.
criteria.no: More specific clause (clause 4) grants an exemption.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the stricter requirement to pay the fee prevails, making the answer yes. Under instruction B, the more specific resident exemption prevails, making the answer no.

items.case: On November 10, 2023, vendor Marcus Chen submitted a commercial food service closure request. The authority reviewed the application and issued a final decision on November 20, 2023.
items.question: Is the $150 fee applicable to this request?

criteria.yes: The policy version on the decision date sets the fee at $150.
criteria.no: The policy version on the request date sets the fee at $100.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, the November 10 request date triggers the pre-amendment $100 fee, so the $150 fee is not applicable (no). Under instruction B, the November 20 decision date triggers the post-amendment $150 fee, making it applicable (yes).

items.case: On Friday, October 6, 2023, organiser Sarah Lin submitted a request for a sidewalk closure scheduled to begin on Monday, November 6, 2023. All required documents were attached.
items.question: Is the submission timely under the policy?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days yields 31 days, meeting the thirty-day requirement.
criteria.no: Counting business days yields 24 days, failing the thirty-day requirement.

items.rationale: Under instruction A, business day counting yields only 24 days between submission and start, missing the thirty-day threshold (no). Under instruction B, calendar day counting yields 31 days, satisfying the threshold (yes).

title: Oakridge Commercial Properties Tenant Improvement Policy
policy:
Policy effective January 1, 2024. Direct all submissions to Property Manager Elena Rostova.
1. Tenants at Oakridge Commercial Properties must submit a written Request for Alteration to the Property Management Office before commencing any structural or cosmetic changes to leased premises.
2. Management will review each submission and provide a written decision within ten days of receipt. If no response is issued by the deadline, the tenant may proceed with the proposed work.
3. Permitted alterations include painting walls, replacing carpet tiles, and installing shelving units. Tenants may not modify load-bearing structures, electrical panels, or plumbing fixtures without separate engineering approval.
4. All materials and labor for approved improvements must be paid by the tenant. Oakridge will not reimburse costs exceeding $5,000 per square foot, and invoices must be submitted for record-keeping within thirty days of project completion.
5. Tenants are responsible for maintaining all approved improvements in good repair throughout the lease term. Any damage caused by tenant modifications must be restored to original condition upon lease termination, unless otherwise agreed in writing.
6. Emergency repairs required to prevent immediate property damage or safety hazards may be undertaken without prior submission, provided the tenant notifies management within twenty-four hours.

items.case: Tenant completed approved flooring work on Friday, November 10. The tenant submitted the contractor invoice to management on Friday, December 15.
items.question: Is the invoice submission permitted under the policy?

criteria.yes: The submission falls within the thirty-day window when counted in business days.
criteria.no: The submission exceeds the thirty-day window when counted in calendar days.

items.rationale: Clause 4 requires invoice submission within thirty days of completion. Counting in business days yields 24 days (within limit), making it permitted. Counting in calendar days yields 35 days (exceeds limit), making it prohibited.

items.case: Tenant requests to install modular office cubicle partitions in Suite 4B.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The partitions qualify as a similar permitted alteration under an illustrative reading.
criteria.no: The partitions are not listed and therefore excluded under a complete reading.

items.rationale: Clause 3 lists permitted alterations. Under a complete list interpretation, only listed items qualify, so cubicles are excluded. Under an illustrative interpretation, cubicles are functionally similar to shelving and partitions, so they qualify.

items.case: Tenant plans to sublease 20 percent of the leased floor area to a related consulting firm starting next month and seeks management approval.
items.question: Is the request permitted?

criteria.yes: The policy contains no clause addressing subleasing, so the default rule permits it.
criteria.no: The policy contains no clause addressing subleasing, so the default rule prohibits it.

items.rationale: The policy governs alterations, maintenance, costs, and emergencies but contains no clause addressing subleasing or space sharing. The request falls outside all clauses. The instruction determines whether uncovered requests are permitted or denied.

title: Cold Chain and Ingredient Handling at Oakridge Provisions
policy:
1. All raw meat, poultry, and seafood must be maintained at or below 4°C from the moment of delivery until final preparation.
2. Prepared items containing dairy, eggs, or cooked proteins must be refrigerated at or below 5°C and used within 72 hours of assembly to prevent microbial growth.
3. Any ingredient arriving at the main warehouse with a recorded surface temperature exceeding 8°C must be rejected outright and entered into the supplier compliance ledger.
4. Dry goods such as flour, rice, and pasta may be kept at room temperature provided the storage room does not exceed 22°C and relative humidity remains below 55%.
5. Warehouse staff must complete temperature verification for all incoming shipments within 5 days of the scheduled delivery date, using calibrated digital probes.
6. Any deviation from the stated temperature or timing limits requires prior written authorization from the Safety Director, Marcus Thorne, and must be filed with the daily operations report.

items.case: A shipment of raw chicken breasts arrives at the main warehouse on 10 March 2024 with a recorded surface temperature of 6°C. The receiving manager logs the delivery and moves the crates to the refrigerated holding area.
items.question: Is the manager's action permitted?

criteria.yes: Clause 3 applies as it specifically addresses arrival temperatures, and 6°C does not exceed the 8°C rejection threshold.
criteria.no: Clause 1 applies as it sets a stricter 4°C limit for raw meat, and 6°C violates that limit.

items.rationale: Clauses 1 and 3 both apply but provide opposite outcomes. Clause 1 is stricter (4°C limit), while Clause 3 is more specific to the arrival context (8°C threshold). Under Instruction A, the stricter clause governs, making the 6°C receipt non-compliant (no). Under Instruction B, the more specific clause governs, making the receipt compliant (yes).

items.case: On 14 April 2024, the warehouse receives a bulk order of rolled oats. The staff stores the oats on open shelving in the dry goods room, where the ambient temperature is 20°C and humidity is 50%.
items.question: Is storing the rolled oats at room temperature permitted?

criteria.yes: Rolled oats are clearly similar to the listed dry goods and qualify under an illustrative reading.
criteria.no: Rolled oats are not explicitly listed in the examples, and under a complete list reading they do not qualify.

items.rationale: Clause 4 lists flour, rice, and pasta as examples of dry goods eligible for room temperature storage. Rolled oats are functionally similar but unlisted. Under Instruction A, the list is treated as exhaustive, excluding oats (no). Under Instruction B, the list is treated as illustrative, including similar items like oats (yes).

items.case: A shipment of frozen berries is scheduled for delivery on Friday, 12 April 2024. The warehouse staff completes the mandatory temperature verification on Wednesday, 17 April 2024.
items.question: Was the verification completed within the required period?

criteria.yes: Counting calendar days, the span from 12 April to 17 April is exactly 5 days, which meets the policy limit.
criteria.no: Counting business days, the span excludes the weekend and totals 3 working days, but the operational window compresses the effective deadline, making the verification late under the business-day count.

items.rationale: Clause 5 sets a 5-day verification window. The case spans from Friday 12 April to Wednesday 17 April. Under Instruction A, counting only business days excludes Saturday and Sunday, compressing the operational timeline and causing the verification to fall outside the permitted window (no). Under Instruction B, counting all calendar days includes the weekend, keeping the 5-day span within the stated limit (yes).
